Finding your computer and cloud recordings

Category: Product features > Participant features > Recordings

How to find your recordings

Find and access computer recordings

By default, computer recordings are placed in these directories on the following devices:

  • Windows: C:\Username]
  • Mac: /Users/[Username]/Documents/Zoom
  • Linux: home/[Username]/Documents/Zoom

Learn how to access and manage your computer recordings on your device, the Zoom desktop app, or the Zoom web portal.

Find and access cloud recordings

If you recorded a meeting or webinar to the cloud, you can manage your cloud recordings in the Zoom web portal:

  • If you’re the account owner or admin on an account, you can view all recordings on your account in Recording and Transcript Management.
  • You can view your own cloud recordings on the Recordings & Transcripts page. Note: Recordings started by co-hosts will only appear in the host’s list of recordings in the Zoom web portal.

Depending on additional products your Zoom account has enabled, you can also find and manage your recordings from Zoom Video Management channels or in Zoom Hub.

How to confirm your recording’s location

If a recording is missing, learn how to find and confirm the recording’s location.

Check the computer recording file location

If a recording is missing, ensure that the meeting wasn’t actually recorded to the cloud instead of your computer. When you record a meeting or webinar to your computer and that session is ended, Zoom creates a folder on your device based on the location configured in your Zoom desktop app. Follow the instructions to view or change the default file location for computer recordings.

If you can’t find the computer recording on the path listed within the Zoom desktop app, you can confirm the computer recording file location by following these steps:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Recordings & Transcripts.
  3. Click the Computer recordings tab.** You can locate the specific meeting or webinar ID and confirm the exact location of the computer recording files listed under the Location** column.

If you’re still having issues finding your computer recording files, review the computer recording troubleshooting guide.

Check the cloud recording location in Zoom
Account
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Account Management then Recording and Transcript Management. A list of cloud recordings on your account will appear.
  3. Search recordings by entering the meeting ID or topic. You can also enter keywords to search the text in audio transcripts.
  4. (Optional) Click Advanced Search to filter recordings by date range, host, or storage location.
User
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Recordings & Transcripts.
  3. Click the Cloud recordings tab. A list of cloud recordings that you started and have finished processing will appear.
  4. Adjust the date range and status, then search by host, meeting ID, topic, or keyword.

If you’re still having issues finding or sharing a cloud recording, review the cloud recording troubleshooting guide.

How to recover deleted recordings

If you can’t find a recording, it may have been deleted.

  • You can find and recover deleted computer recordings from the trash bin of your computer. Learn more about managing deleted computer recordings.
  • You can find and recover cloud recordings from the trash folder in the Zoom web portal within 30 days. After the 30-day period, files in the trash folder are permanently deleted within 24 hours. Learn more about managing deleted cloud recordings.

How to ensure that the recording starts

If you can’t find a recording, there is also the chance that the manual recording didn’t actually start.

  • Learn how to start a computer recording.
  • Learn how to start a cloud recording.

Managing computer recordings

Category: Product features > Participant features > Recordings

How to view or change the default directory for computer recordings

By default, computer recordings are placed in these directories:

  • Windows:** **C:\Username]
  • Mac:** **/Users/[Username]/Documents/Zoom
  • Linux: home/[Username]/Documents/Zoom

You can find or change the default location of computer recordings in the Zoom desktop app settings:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click the Recording tab .
  4. Under Local recording storage, locate the Storage location. The path listed next to the Storage location field is where your computer recordings are saved. If the path shown isn’t physically located within your device, such as a network drive, you might encounter issues.
  5. (Optional) Click any of the following options next to the Storage location setting:
  • Open: Open the folder where your computer recordings are stored.
  • Change: Update the default location where your computer recordings are stored.

How to access and manage your computer recordings

You can access your computer recordings from the Zoom desktop app and Zoom web portal.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Web portal
View and manage computer recordings on the Zoom desktop app
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Home tab .
  3. Below your daily list of meetings, click Open recordings. You will be redirected to the Hub tab .
  4. On the My files > Meeting recordings page, click the Computer recordings tab. A list of recordings saved on your computer will appear. Recordings not yet converted will display Convert next to the meeting topic.
  5. (Optional) Click the name of the meeting topic to play the recording on your device’s default media player.
  6. (Optional) Hover over the computer recording row and click the ellipsis icon to access the following options:
  • Click Play audio only to play the audio of the recording on your device’s default audio player.
  • Click View file location to open the recording in your device’s files.
  • Click Delete to delete the recording, then click Delete to confirm.

Note: If you experience issues opening or playing the file, check the default recording location and ensure the files are in the correct place.

Share computer recordings

Learn how to share computer recordings.

Convert computer recordings

Computer recordings should automatically convert after they are ended. To manually convert a computer recording:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Access your computer recordings.
  3. Locate the computer recording not yet converted and click Convert. The recording will be converted and open in your default recording location. If you experience any issues, learn how to troubleshoot computer recording conversion failures.
View and manage computer recordings in the Zoom web portal

You can view a list of your personal computer recordings in the Zoom web portal.

Note: Removing items from this list doesn’t remove the actual recording files on your computer. As a result, this list may not show all of your computer recordings.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Recordings & Transcripts.
  3. Click the Computer recordings tab. This will display the meeting topic, meeting ID, date and time, computer name, and file path for your computer recordings.
  4. To the right of each recording, view the available options:
  • Open: View the folder where your computer recording is stored. Your browser will prompt you to open the Zoom desktop app and redirect you to the file’s location. Note: You can only play back computer recordings that were recorded on the same device you’re currently using.
  • Delete: Remove the selected recording from the list. It will no longer appear on the web portal, but the files remain on your computer.

Recovering a deleted local or cloud recording

Category: Product features > Participant features > Recordings

How to recover a deleted local recording from your computer

  • Windows
  • macOS

  1. Open Recycle Bin from your desktop.

  2. Right-click on the recording you want to recover, then select Restore. Your recording will be available again on the Recordings page.

  3. Click the Trash icon in your dock.

  4. Right-click on the recording you want to recover, then select Put Back. Your recording will be available again on the Recordings page.

How to recover a deleted cloud recording in the web portal

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Recordings and Transcripts.
  3. Click the Trash tab to access any cloud recordings in the trash. Note: If the Trash tab is not available, this means that the Enable Trash for Recording and Transcript setting is disabled. You need to contact your Zoom admin.
  4. In the Search by meeting number field, enter the meeting ID of the recording you want to recover then click Search or select a recording from the list.
  5. On the right side of the recording topic you want to recover, click Recover. Note: To recover multiple items simultaneously, next to each meeting’s topic, select the checkbox .
  6. Click Recover again to confirm. Your recording will be available again on the Recordings page.

Protocols for Apple screen mirroring

Category: Product features > Participant features > Screen Sharing

Instructions

Please ensure the following ports are enabled on your computer’s network or desktop firewall:

Type Protocol Port
UDP mDNS 5353
UDP Airplay 7200-17210
TCP Airplay 5000, 7000, 7100, 50000, 7200-17210

On your Windows desktop firewall, allow access to the following applications:

Airhost.exe Type:TCP Allow all
Airhost.exe Type:UDP Allow all
zrAirhost.exe Type:TCP Allow all
zrAirhost.exe Type:UDP Allow all

How to Add a Firewall Exception for airhost.exe

Follow these steps to allow airhost.exe through the Windows firewall:

  1. Open Windows Security
  • Press the Windows key and search for Windows Security.
  • Click to open the app.
  1. Go to Firewall & Network Protection
  • In Windows Security, click Firewall & network protection.
  1. Allow an App Through Firewall
  • Click on Allow an app through firewall to open the Allowed apps list.
  1. Change Settings
  • Click Change settings.
  • Provide administrator permission if prompted.
  1. Add another App
  • Click Allow another app.
  1. Browse for the file
  • Click Browse… and navigate to the airhost.exe file.
  • Default path: C:\YourUsername*.exe
  1. Add and Confirm
  • Click Add, then OK to save your changes.

Sharing a recorded video with sound during your meeting

Category: Product features > Participant features > Screen Sharing

How to share a recorded video in a meeting

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Start or join a Zoom meeting.
  3. In the meeting controls toolbar, click Share .
  4. At the top, click the Advanced tab, and then select Video file .
  5. Click Share. Your system file browser will open for you to select the video file to open.
  6. Navigate to and select the video you want to share, then click Open. The video will now open within Zoom and be visible to meeting participants.

Notes:

  • When using this feature, Optimize for video clip is automatically enabled, which is generally recommended for sharing videos but also restricts and downscales the resolution to 1080/720 to provide improved framerate. This can be manually disabled, which will allow for higher resolution, but this should only be used in situations where framerate is less important.
  • You must be signed in to the desktop app to have this option.

How to use the playback controls

While sharing the video, you will have some common playback controls, which are not visible to other meeting participants. The sharer will have the following controls:

  • Play/Pause: Start or pause the playback of the video.
  • Elapsed time/total video length: Shows the current elapsed time of video playback, and the total length of the video file.
  • Playback slider: Allows you to skip to other points of the video playback range
  • Volume: Allows you to adjust the volume of the video being shared.
  • Fullscreen: Allows you to make the video full-screen for you and viewers.

How video sharing compares to other sharing options

When using the option to share your desktop or an application, the video resolution is dependent upon CPU usage, screen resolution, graphics card, and OS graphic system capabilities. Additionally, when a video is larger than 1080p, Zoom automatically downgrades the resolution to 1080p (or 720p), in order to optimize the content while minimizing the required bandwidth. Depending on how the video is shared, such as sharing a specific application or sharing only a portion of your screen, it may require additional CPU resources, which can further affect the overall quality of both the video share and the meeting for the user who is sharing.

However, when using the video share option, Zoom encodes the video from the file directly and shares it, effectively bypassing some of the limiting factors with standard content sharing. Allowing the Zoom app to handle the encoding and sharing minimizes CPU usage for the participant who is sharing, which allows for higher frame rates and smoother video playback.

Sharing background music or computer audio on Zoom

Category: Product features > Participant features > Screen Sharing

How to share your screen with background music/audio

  1. Start or join a Zoom meeting.
  2. On the meeting toolbar, click Share Screen . The share selection window will appear.
  3. Select the program or desktop you wish to share.
  4. In the share selection window, select Share Sound.
  5. (Optional) Select the down arrow just to the right of the Share Sound option to view audio options and switch between Mono and Stereo (high fidelity) audio options.
  6. In the bottom-right corner, click Share to begin sharing with your device’s audio. Your screen will be shared with background music/audio.

Notes:

  • Sharing device audio can also be enabled after you have begun sharing by locating the share toolbar, clicking More, and then selecting Share Sound.
  • To switch between mono and stereo sound while sharing, locate the share toolbar, click More, then select between Mono and Stereo (high fidelity) options under Select sharing sound mode.
  • For users who join the meeting via both phone and computer, in order to receive audio via the phone and video/screen sharing via computer, if Share Computer Sound is enabled, this will trigger the audio to channel through both their phone and their computer speakers. To avoid audio feedback, mute the speaker of your phone or the speaker of your computer.

How to play background music or audio on Zoom without sharing your screen

During a meeting, you can play background music on Zoom without sharing your screen. You can also play any sound your computer makes, which means if you play a local or online music track on your computer, that track will be played in your meeting as well.

To play music or share audio without sharing your screen while in a Zoom meeting:

  1. Start or join a Zoom meeting.
  2. On the meeting toolbar, click Share Screen . The share selection window will appear.
  3. In the window, click the Advanced tab.
  4. Click the Computer Audio option .
  5. (Optional) In the bottom-right corner of the Computer Audio option, click the down arrow to view additional audio options to switch between Mono and Stereo (high fidelity) for the audio shared in the meeting.
  6. In the bottom-right corner, click Share to begin sharing with your device’s audio.

Zoom share and play your computer audio. This allows you to play music from anywhere—whether streaming services or YouTube. Meeting participants will be able to listen to your music without seeing your screen.

How to control the volume of a shared sound while in a meeting

To control the sound you are sharing directly into the Zoom meeting through share, you must adjust the volume from the application playing the sound or the overall device volume directly. For example, if you play YouTube and share that audio in the meeting, you should adjust the volume on YouTube directly. You can also adjust the overall volume on your device settings, but this will also affect the audio coming out of Zoom. Note: On Windows devices, the ability to control the volume will depend on the audio drivers used by the system. On some computers, the ability to control the volume may vary when switching between different speakers, because built-in speakers and external speakers use different drivers.

Sharing your iOS screen from the Zoom desktop client

Category: Product features > Participant features > Screen Sharing

How to share your iOS screen in a meeting through screen mirroring

  1. In a Zoom meeting, click Share Screen .
  2. Choose iPhone/iPad.
  3. (Optional) If you would like to also share your phone audio into the meeting, in the bottom-left corner, select the check box next to Share sound.
  4. Click Share.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions to connect your iOS device:
  6. On your iPhone/iPad, access the control center by swiping down from the top-right corner of the screen. On iOS 11 or earlier, swipe up from the bottom of the screen.
  7. Tap the icon for Screen Mirroring.
  8. Choose the Zoom-your computer option. Your device’s screen will now be shared into the meeting.
  9. When you’re finished sharing your iOS screen, you can do either of the following:
  • Tap Stop Mirroring on your iPhone/iPad
  • Click Stop Share in the meeting controls toolbar

How to share your iOS screen in a meeting with a wired connection

Note: Sharing with a wired connection is only possible on macOS devices.

  1. In a Zoom meeting, click Share Screen .
  2. Choose iPhone/iPad via Cable.
  3. (Optional) If you would like to also share your phone audio into the meeting, in the bottom-left corner, select the check box next to Share computer sound.
  4. Click Share.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions displayed:
  6. Connect your iPhone or iPad via cable.
  7. When prompted on the iOS device, select Trust.
  8. Enter your passcode if required. Your device’s screen will now be shared into the meeting.

Sharing your iOS screen from the Zoom mobile app

Category: Product features > Participant features > Screen Sharing

How to start sharing your iOS screen in a meeting

Before starting a screen share, enable Do Not Disturb on your device to prevent unexpected notifications from appearing on your screen while you’re sharing it.

  1. Start or join a Zoom meeting from your iPhone or iPad.
  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap Share Content .
  3. Tap Screen. Note: If you don’t see the Screen option, it may be due to the Disable desktop screen sharing for meetings you host setting in the Zoom web portal.
  4. Tap Microphone Off/Microphone On to enable or disable device audio with the screen share. When Microphone On is displayed, your device’s audio will be shared.
  5. Tap Start Broadcast. A 3 second countdown will begin, then your screen will start sharing.
  6. Swipe up or press the home button to navigate away from the broadcast controls and share the content on your screen.
  7. (Optional) Swipe the meeting thumbnail towards the edge of the screen to hide it so you can share your full screen.

How to share your device audio during a screen share

After you start the broadcast, you can include the device audio with the screen share by doing one of the following:

  • If you haven’t navigated away from the initial Screen Broadcast, tap Microphone Off/Microphone On to enable or disable device audio with the screen share. When Microphone On is displayed, your device’s audio will be shared.
  • If you’ve navigated away from broadcasting controls, open the Zoom mobile app and tap Share Device Audio.

Note: There may be a brief delay in the audio that other meeting participants hear.

How to stop sharing your iOS screen in a meeting

You can stop sharing your iOS screen by doing one of the following:

  • Open the Zoom mobile app, then tap Stop Share.
  • Click the red button in the top-left corner of the screen (where the time is displayed), and tap Stop.

When you stop sharing your screen, you will be directed back to the Zoom meeting.

Side-by-side mode for screen sharing

Category: Product features > Participant features > Screen Sharing

How to view a shared screen in side-by-side mode

  1. Start or join a meeting.
  2. Once someone starts a screen share, in the top-right corner of the meeting window, click View . Additional options will appear.
  3. Select one of the following layouts:
  • Side-by-side: speaker
  • Side-by-side: gallery
  • Side-by-side: dynamic gallery
  • Side-by-side: multi-speaker
  1. (Optional) Hover your pointer over the boundary between the shared screen and participants’ video until your pointer changes to a double arrow and you see a grey line separating both views. Click and drag the separator to adjust the size of each view.

Upon leaving side-by-side mode, video thumbnails are displayed either above the content when in windowed mode (similar to speaker view) or over the content in the top-right corner of the screen when in fullscreen. These thumbnails during fullscreen can be moved by clicking and dragging.

How to automatically enter side-by-side mode when a screen share starts

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click the Share screen tab.
  4. Click the See shared content in side-by-side mode toggle to enable it. Zoom will automatically enter side-by-side mode when a participant starts sharing their screen.

How to set side-by-side mode as Webinar host for attendees

  1. As a host, in the top-right corner of the webinar window, click View.
  2. Under Attendee view, select Side-by-side: Speaker or Side-by-side: gallery.

Managing Zoom Surveys as user

Category: Product features > Participant features > Surveys and polls

How to create and send surveys

Use a survey to collect responses through a shared link or after meetings and webinars.

Create a survey
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. In the top-right corner, click + Create. A pop-up window will appear.
  4. In the window, select Survey, then click Create.
  5. Click the Untitled Survey title and enter a survey name.
  6. Click the Describe your survey… section and enter a description about your survey.
  7. Hover your mouse over the first question and do the following actions:
  • Click the picture icon to upload an image for the question. The picture icon will disappear after you upload an image.
  • Click the pencil icon to edit the question.
  • Click the ellipsis , then choose from the following options:
  • Add skip logic: Choose a single-choice question and the option participants can select to skip to another question or the end of the survey. The question will be required.
  • Duplicate: Duplicate the question.
  • Delete: Delete the question.
  1. Review the question types and configuration options, then edit the question and select the question type.
  2. (Optional) Click + Add question to add another question to the survey.
  3. (Optional) For each question that you edit, click the Required toggle to enable or disable it.
  4. In the top-right corner, use the following actions:
  • Click the Zoom AI Companion icon to generate questions with AI Companion. Note: This feature only supports single-choice question types.
  1. Select the Number of questions.
  2. Select the Number of options.
  3. Under I want to create a survey to…, enter a description that includes the audience, goals, and context for the survey. You can also click Try an example to generate an example in the description.
  4. Click Generate. Zoom AI Companion will generate questions for the survey.
  • (Optional) Click the gear icon to configure the following options: A panel will appear.
  • Require answers to be anonymous
  • Numbered questions
  • Show question type
  • Feedback after submission
  • (Optional) Click the color palette icon to customize the survey’s colors and upload a header image.
  • (Optional) Click the preview icon to see a preview.
  • (Optional) Click the ellipsis icon to Save as draft.
  1. (Optional) Click Save to allow the survey to be sent after meetings.
Send a survey

Review our articles on how to assign surveys to meetings or webinars and send them after a session.

How to create and start polls or quizzes

Use a poll or quiz to collect responses or answers during meetings and webinars.

Create a poll or quiz
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. In the top-right corner, click + Create. A pop-up window will appear.
  4. In the window, select Poll or quiz, then click Create. Note: A poll will be created by default.
  5. (Optional) In the top-right corner, click the Make it a quiz toggle to switch the poll to a quiz.
  6. Click the Untitled Poll title to give the poll or quiz a name.
  7. Hover your mouse over the first question and do the following actions:
  • Click the picture icon to upload an image for the question. The picture icon will disappear after you upload an image.
  • Click the pencil icon to edit the question.
  • Click the ellipsis , then choose from the following options:
  • Duplicate: Duplicate the question.
  • Delete: Delete the question.
  1. Review the question types and configuration options, then edit the question and select the question type.
  2. (Optional) Click + Add Question to add another question to the poll or quiz.
  3. (Optional) For each question that you edit, click the Required toggle to enable or disable it.
  4. In the top-right corner, use the following actions:
  • (Optional) Click the Zoom AI Companion icon to generate questions with AI Companion. Note: This feature only supports single-choice question types.
  1. Select the Number of questions.
  2. Select the Number of options.
  3. Under I want to create a survey to…, enter a description that includes the audience, goals, and context for the survey. You can also click Try an example to generate an example in the description.
  4. Click Generate. Zoom AI Companion will generate questions for the survey. Generated questions can be modified or deleted.
  • (Optional) In the top-right corner, click the gear icon to configure the following option: A panel will appear.
  • Require answers to be anonymous
  • (Optional) Click the preview icon to see a preview.
  • (Optional) Click the ellipsis icon to Save as draft.
  1. (Optional) Click Save to allow the poll or quiz to be started during meetings.

Note: If you selected to create a quiz, you must click Set answer to select a correct answer for each question.

Start a poll or quiz during a meeting

Review our articles on how to use polls in meetings and webinars or how to use quizzes in meetings and webinars.

How to view survey, poll, and quiz results

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. Click the All types tab.
  4. To the right of the survey, poll, or quiz you want to view results for, click the analytics icon.

Notes:

  • Users can share their surveys and polls with other users in the same account. Collaborators can view the shared survey or poll content, results, make a copy in their personal library and view results.
  • When viewing the survey results overview, users can switch from the standard view to the advanced bar chart view for enhanced data visualization and analysis.

How to manage surveys, polls, and quizzes

Copy link for participants

You can copy the survey link to share with participants.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. Click the All types or Surveys tab.
  4. To the right of the survey you want to manage, click the ellipsis , then click Copy Link.
  5. Complete the following actions to share your survey with others:
  • Click Copy link to copy the survey link.
  • Click Get QR code. A pop-up window will appear.
  1. In the window, choose from the following actions:
  2. Click Copy to clipboard to copy the QR code.
  3. Click Download PNG to save and download the QR code image as a PNG file.
Close surveys
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. Click the All types or Surveys tab.
  4. To the right of the survey you want to manage, click the ellipsis , then click Close survey. A confirmation window will appear.
  5. In the window, click Confirm.

This survey will stop collecting responses after being closed.

Edit surveys, polls, and quizzes
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. Click the All types, Surveys, or Polls and quizzes tab.
  4. To the right of the survey, poll, or quiz you want to edit, click the ellipsis , then click Edit.
  5. Edit your survey, poll, or quiz.
  6. Click Save.
Preview surveys, polls, and quizzes
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. Click the All types, Surveys, or Polls and quizzes tab.
  4. To the right of the survey, poll, or quiz you want to preview, click the ellipsis , then click Preview. The survey, poll, or quiz preview will appear.
Duplicate surveys, polls, and quizzes
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. Click the All types, Surveys, or Polls and quizzes tab.
  4. To the right of the survey, poll, or quiz you want to duplicate, click the ellipsis , then click Duplicate. The survey, poll, or quiz will be duplicated.

How to delete surveys, polls, and quizzes

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Surveys.
  3. Click the All types, Surveys, or Polls and quizzes tab.
  4. To the right of the survey, poll, or quiz you want to delete, click the ellipsis , then click Delete. A confirmation window will appear.
  5. In the window, click Delete. Note: This action cannot be undone.

Understanding question types for surveys, polls, and quizzes

Category: Product features > Participant features > Surveys and polls

Types of questions

After you create a survey, poll, or quiz, you can choose from the following question types:

Question type Survey Poll or Quiz Consumer Engagement Survey
Single Choice ✔ ✔ ✔
Multiple Choice ✔ ✔
Matching ✔ ✔
Rank Order ✔ ✔
Short Answer ✔ ✔
Long Answer ✔ ✔ ✔
Fill in the blank ✔ ✔
Rating Scale ✔ ✔ ✔
Single choice

Use the single-choice format if you want the participant to answer with only one choice.

  1. Click Untitled Question to enter your question.
  2. Click Choice 1 to enter the first answer. Click Choice 2 to enter the second answer if necessary. (Optional) Click + Add choice, then click Choice 3 to enter the new answer; repeat to add as many choices as needed.
  3. (Optional) Additional customization options include:
  • Delete a choice: Hover your cursor over the choice you want to delete and click the delete icon to the right.
  • Rearrange choice: Hover your cursor over the choice you want to move then click and hold the 6 dots to the right; drag the choice to its new location and drop.
  • Required question: Click the Required toggle if the question has to be answered in order to proceed.
  • Show as dropdown: Click the Show as dropdown toggle for choices to display from a drop-down menu.
  • Upload image: Click the Upload image icon at the bottom right of the question box.
  • Duplicate or delete question: Click the ellipses … icon at the bottom right of the question box and select your option.
  • Rearrange question: Click and hold the 6 dots at the top of the question box; drag to its new location and drop. This is only visible when multiple questions exist.
  1. (Optional) Click + Add Question to add another question.
Multiple choice

Use the multiple-choice format if you want the participant to answer with one or more options.

  1. Click Untitled Question to enter your question.
  2. Click Choice 1 to enter the first answer. Click Choice 2 to enter the second answer if necessary. (Optional) Click + Add choice, then click Choice 3 to enter the new answer; repeat to add as many choices as needed.
  3. (Optional) Additional customization options include:
  • Delete a choice: Hover your cursor over the choice you want to delete and click the delete icon to the right.
  • Rearrange choice: Hover your cursor over the choice you want to move then click and hold the 6 dots to the right; drag the choice to its new location and drop.
  • Required question: Click the Required toggle if the question has to be answered in order to proceed.
  • Upload image: Click the Upload image icon at the bottom right of the question box.
  • Duplicate or delete question: Click the ellipses … icon at the bottom right of the question box and select your option.
  • Rearrange question: Click and hold the 6 dots at the top of the question box; drag to its new location and drop. This is only visible when multiple questions exist.
  1. (Optional) Click + Add Question to add another question.
Matching

Use the matching format if you want the participant to match prompts with possible answers.

  1. Click Untitled Question to enter your question.
  2. Click Prompt 1 to enter the first prompt. Click Prompt 2 and Prompt 3 to enter the others, if necessary. (Optional) Click + Add choice, then click Prompt 4 to enter the new prompt; repeat to add as many choices as needed.
  3. Click Answer 1 to enter the first possible answer. Click Answer 2 and Answer 3 to enter the others, if necessary. (Optional) Click + Add answer, then click Answer 4 to enter the new answer; repeat to add as many choices as needed.
  4. (Optional) Additional customization options include:
  • Delete a prompt or answer: Hover your cursor over the prompt or answer you want to delete and click the delete icon to the right.
  • Rearrange prompt or answer: Hover your cursor over the prompt or answer you want to move then click and hold the 6 dots to the right; drag the prompt or answer to its new location and drop.
  • Required question: Click the Required toggle if the question has to be answered in order to proceed.
  • Upload image: Click the Upload image icon at the bottom right of the question box.
  • Duplicate or delete question: Click the ellipses … icon at the bottom right of the question box and select your option.
  • Rearrange question: Click and hold the 6 dots at the top of the question box; drag to its new location and drop. This is only visible when multiple questions exist.
  1. (Optional) Click + Add Question to add another question.
Rank Order

Use the rank order format if you want the participant to rank answers using rows and columns.

  1. Click Untitled Question to enter your question.
  2. Click Row 1 to enter the first row choice. Click Row 2 and Row 3 to enter the others, if necessary. (Optional) Click + Add row, then click Row 4 to enter the new row; repeat to add as many choices as needed.
  3. Click Column 1 to enter the first column choice. Click Column 2 and Column 3 to enter the others, if necessary. (Optional) Click + Add column, then click Column 4 to enter the new column; repeat to add as many choices as needed.
  4. (Optional) Additional customization options include:
  • Delete a column or row: Hover your cursor over the prompt or answer you want to delete and click the delete icon to the right.
  • Rearrange column or row: Hover your cursor over the prompt or answer you want to move then click and hold the 6 dots to the right; drag the prompt or answer to its new location and drop.
  • Required question: Click the Required toggle if the question has to be answered in order to proceed.
  • Upload image: Click the Upload image icon at the bottom right of the question box.
  • Duplicate or delete question: Click the ellipses … icon at the bottom right of the question box and select your option.
  • Rearrange question: Click and hold the 6 dots at the top of the question box; drag to its new location and drop. This is only visible when multiple questions exist.

Adjusting your video layout during a virtual meeting

Category: Product features > Participant features > Video

Video layouts

Speaker view

Speaker view will switch the large video window between who is speaking with 3 or more participants in the meeting. If it is just you and one other participant, your video will be smaller at the top and their video will appear below.

Pinning a participant will keep them as the largest video for your view of the meeting, while spotlighting will do the same but for everyone in the meeting.

Gallery view

Gallery view lets you see thumbnail displays of participants, in a grid pattern, which expands and contracts as participants join and leave the meeting. Depending on your CPU, the desktop app can display up to 25 or 49 participants in a single screen of the Gallery view. If more participants than are allowed to be displayed are in the meeting, additional pages are created with your max number of thumbnails on each page. Cycle through the pages and view up to 1,000 thumbnails by clicking the right or left arrows in gallery view to display the next page of participants.

You can rearrange the order of the videos in Gallery view, as well as save the customization for use in later sessions.

When in Gallery view and a participant begins speaking, that active speaker is relocated to the current page you are viewing and is highlighted, making it easier to recognize who is speaking. This functionality is not possible when using a custom gallery order, as the order will remain in place.

Dynamic gallery view

Dynamic gallery is an enhanced version of the gallery view that automatically crops video tiles to focus on faces and best utilize available screen space. This view automatically crops all tiles (including your own) to show more participants. Other participants may still see your full background. To expand or shrink your self view, hover over your video tile, and from the menu , click Expand self view or Shrink self view.

Dynamic gallery view supports up to 25 or 49 participants per screen. You can switch to the next page to view additional participants.

Note: Dynamic gallery view of up to 9 participants requires desktop app for Windows, macOS, or Linux version 6.7.5 or higher. Dynamic gallery of up to 25 or 49 participants requires version 7.0.0 or higher.

Multi-speaker view

Multi-speaker view provides meeting participants a more engaging experience, dynamically adapting to current speakers by highlighting and enlarging their video tiles over others, while still providing a view of other participants in a smaller gallery view below. With 4 or fewer participants, gallery view is used instead, but in a meeting with at least 5 participants, up to 4 active speakers will have their video tile enlarged and made the focus of the meeting. Pinning videos is supported with multi-speaker layout, keeping the pinned video in focus, but spotlighting is not supported, as the spotlighted video tile will take control of the video layout for all.

Note: Multi-speaker layout requires desktop app for Windows or macOS version 6.0.0 or higher.

Immersive view

Immersive view allows hosts to place video participants onto a single virtual background, such as a classroom or boardroom scene. Learn more about using immersive view.

Floating thumbnail window view

The floating thumbnail window allows you to minimize the main Zoom window, but keep the video on top of other applications you have open. You can move the window around your screen as needed, or hide the video entirely.

To switch to floating thumbnail view:

  1. Click on the minimize icon, located at the top-right corner for Windows, or top-left corner for macOS.
  2. Once in mini-window view, you can collapse the video by clicking on the arrow on the left side. Click the arrow again to expand the video thumbnail.
  3. While in this mode, you can also easily mute/unmute yourself or turn on/off your video by clicking the microphone and video icons respectively.
  4. To close the floating thumbnail window and return to the full Zoom window click the Show full meeting window icon on the right side.
Video layouts during screen sharing

When viewing shared content, you will have the following view options:

  • Standard: Similar to Speaker view, where the shared content is below and other videos tiles are along the top. When in fullscreen, the shared content will fill the screen and video tiles will become smaller, movable thumbnails.
  • Side-by-side: Speaker: When in side-by-side mode, the meeting window is split between the shared content and video thumbnails, with the ability to adjust the proportions of the split between the two. Side-by-side: Speaker will only show the active speaker in the portion containing video thumbnails.
  • Side-by-side: Gallery: When in side-by-side mode, the meeting window is split between the shared content and video thumbnails, with the ability to adjust the proportions of the split between the two. Side-by-side: Gallery will display a maximum of 6 (when the shared content is given the most space) or 49 video thumbnails (when the shared content is given the least space) in the portion containing video thumbnails.
  • Side-by-side: Dynamic gallery: When in side by side mode, the meeting window is split between the shared content and video thumbnails, with the ability to adjust the proportions of the split between the two. Side-by-side: Dynamic gallery will display a maximum of 6 (when the shared content is given the most space) or 9 video tiles (when the shared content is given the least space) in the portion containing the video tiles.
  • Side-by-side: Multi-speaker: When in side-by-side mode, the meeting window is split between the shared content and video thumbnails, with the ability to adjust the proportions of the split between the two. Side-by-side: Multi-speaker will dynamically adapt to current speakers by highlighting and enlarging their video tiles over others below.

Any of these views can be used when the meeting window is maximized as well. Learn more about Side-by-Side mode.

How to switch the meeting window to full screen

You can switch any of the layouts (except floating the thumbnail window) to full screen mode by double-clicking your Zoom window.

You can exit full screen by double-clicking again or pressing the Esc key on your keyboard.

How to hide different views of video layouts

Hide participants who have their video turned off

Hiding non-video participants can reduce the number of participants displayed on the screen and draw more attention to those with video on. While this can be controlled through the out-of-meeting client settings, this can also be adjusting during a live session as well.

  1. In the top-right corner of the video window, click View .
  2. Click Hide Non-video Participants to hide all participants without video.
  3. To show non-video participants again, click the View button at the top-right corner of your screen and select Show Non-Video Participants.

You can also stop all incoming video to preserve bandwidth or avoid mental fatigue.

How to hide your view of your own video

When presenting while on video, seeing your own video can be distracting for some. While this can be controlled through the out-of-meeting client settings, this can also be adjusting during a live session as well.

  1. In the top-right corner of the video window, click View .
  2. Click Hide Self View to hide your video.
How to hide the Smart Gallery full room view

If a Zoom Room is participating in your meeting with smart gallery enabled, a camera view of the entire room will accompany the other smart gallery video streams by default. If you want to hide this view and see only the individual video streams, follow these steps:

  1. Start a meeting and wait for the Zoom Room participant to join and enable smart gallery.
  2. Click Participants.
  3. Click More next to the entry for the Zoom Room participant.
  4. Click Hide Room View.
  5. (Optional) If you want to change the setting again, follow steps 2-4 and click Show Room View.

Changing your virtual background image

Category: Product features > Participant features > Video

Recommended setup for virtual backgrounds

  • With a green screen
  • Without green screen

A virtual background with a green screen provides the best virtual background effect and uses fewer system resources during the meeting. This method requires you to have a solid-colored screen, curtain, or wall behind you, and Zoom will replace the selected color with the image or video you selected. This method improves the sharpness and definition of the virtual background effect around you.

For best results:

  • Use a very bright and distinct color, such as a green or blue screen. The contrast in colors makes it easier to distinguish you in the foreground from the bright background.
  • Higher quality cameras result in a better virtual background. See camera recommendations for details.
  • Use uniform lighting and color.
  • Do not wear clothing that is the same color as the virtual background.

Virtual background without a green screen provides the same effect as when using a green screen, only with less sharpness and definition around you. This is because without a solid, contrasting color behind you, the system is less likely to accurately distinguish you in the foreground from the background. This method requires more system resources, so it has higher system requirements.

For best results:

  • Higher quality cameras result in a better virtual background. See camera recommendations for details.
  • Use uniform lighting and color.
  • Make sure not only your face is illuminated, but also some of your background as well, as the contrast can help distinguish you from the background.

Troubleshooting virtual background issues

If you are experiencing issues with virtual background, try the following troubleshooting tips:

  • If you do not have the Virtual background tab in your desktop app settings after enabling it, sign out of the app, sign back in again, and check the settings again.
  • Manually pick the background color to ensure the correct color is selected. This option is only available after you click an image and have I have a green screen selected.

Click the color selector box and the virtual background will disappear temporarily, so that you can click on the color in your background that you want to replace with the virtual background. Zoom will automatically make a best guess as to which color should be replaced, but sometimes there are too many choices to accurately guess the correct one. This is why sometimes the virtual background will cover some of your face, as the color it selected was too close to your own skin tone. - Ensure that the background is a solid color with minimal shadows. Also, ensure the background is uniform in lighting. A 3-point lighting setup is ideal. - Ensure that your green screen color does not match your shirt, hair, or eye color. - Black bars on the sides of your video when virtual background is enabled? Ensure that HD video is enabled in your Video settings. - If you are using VDI, some plugins do not support virtual backgrounds and less powerful thin client machines may also be unable to support the feature. Support for additional VDI platforms is in development and customers should check with their sales representative for updates.

Enabling or disabling blurred background

Category: Product features > Participant features > Video

How to enable or disable blurred background

As a meeting host or participant, or webinar host or panelist, you can use this feature to blur your background either before joining a meeting or webinar or while it is in progress.

Notes:

  • After you enable the blurred background, Zoom saves it as your default video background and automatically applies it to all future meetings until you choose a different background.

  • The Blur option is a variant of the virtual background options that you can configure in the virtual background setting.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux

  • Android | iOS

Enable or disable blurred your background before a meeting or webinar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture or initials, then click Settings.

  4. Click the Backgrounds tab. Note: If you do not have the Backgrounds tab and you haveenabled it on the web portal, sign out of the Zoom Workplace desktop app and sign in again.
  5. Click the Blur icon. Your background will become blurred behind you, obscuring your surroundings.
  6. (Optional) Click None or click a virtual background to disable the blurred background.
Enable or disable blurred background during a meeting or webinar
  1. Join a Zoommeeting as a host or participant orwebinar as a host or panelist from your Zoom Workplace desktop app.

Enhancing your video in Zoom

Category: Product features > Participant features > Video

How to enhance meeting video and picture quality

Use virtual backgrounds

The virtual background feature allows you to display an image or video as your background during a Zoom meeting or webinar. Learn more about changing your virtual background.

Apply avatars

The avatar feature allows you to replace your appearance with a 3D virtual avatar that mimics head movements and facial expressions. When you turn on this feature during a meeting or webinar, Zoom’s technology uses your device’s camera to detect where a face is on the screen and apply the selected avatar effect.

Enable HD video

Zoom’s HD video capabilities allow you to experience high-resolution video conferencing. You can enable HD video to utilize 720p or 1080p (depending on your Zoom plan) for high-quality video when in a meeting or a webinar.

Even when HD video is enabled, your device must meet the bandwidth requirements. Make sure you follow the guidelines on how to enable HD when in a meeting or webinar. HD video uses a higher amount of CPU and bandwidth (~2Mbps up/down). If you are experiencing network or CPU performance issues, you may want to disable use of HD video.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.

  3. Click the Video & effects tab.

  4. Click the Camera tab.

  5. Click the HD video toggle to enable or disable it. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.

  6. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  7. In the bottom-right corner, tap More .

  8. Under Settings, tap Meetings.

  9. Under Video, tap the HD video toggle to enable or disable it.

Adjust lighting

Zoom’s lighting settings allow you to improve video brightness and quality.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
Portrait lighting

Portrait lighting allows the system to dim your background while brightening you in the foreground, making you stand out more when you’re on video.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click the Video & effects tab.
  4. Click the Camera tab.
  5. Click the Portrait lighting toggle to enable or disable it. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.
Low light

Zoom’s low light settings allow you to combat poor lighting conditions during remote video conferences by brightening your video in dark environments.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click the Video & effects tab.
  4. Click the Camera tab.
  5. Click the Adjust for low light toggle. The setting will default to Auto. However, you can select Manual, and adjust the setting to the desired effect. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.
Portrait lighting

Portrait lighting allows the system to dim your background while brightening you in the foreground, making you stand out more when you’re on video.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the bottom-right corner, tap More .
  3. Under Settings, tap Meetings.
  4. Under Video, tap the Portrait lighting toggle to enable or disable it.
Touch up my appearance

The touch up my appearance feature gives your picture display a softer focus and enhances your digital appearance in real-time.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • iOS

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.

  3. Click Video & effects .

  4. Click the Camera tab.

  5. Click the Touch up my appearance toggle to enable or disable it.

  6. If you enabled the setting, use the slider to adjust the effect. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make. Zoom will remember your preference and use it the next time you start or join a meeting on this device.

  7. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  8. In the lower-right corner, tap More .

  9. Under Settings, tap Meetings.

  10. Under Video, tap Touch up my appearance.

  11. Tap the toggle to enable this option.

  12. Use the slider to adjust the effect. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make. Zoom will remember your preference and use it the next time you start or join a meeting on this device.

Apply video filters

Video filters use a variety of overlays, color filters, and other custom video frames during meetings and webinars - all within the Zoom desktop app and mobile app.

When you turn on this feature during a meeting, Zoom’s technology uses your device’s camera to detect the movements and positioning of your face to apply the selected filter effect. Such data does not leave your device, is not retained, is not used to identify you, and is only used to generate the selected effects.

Note: The video filters feature may not be available for all regions and account types. If you do not see a specific feature, you may not have access to use it.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.

  3. Click the Video & effects tab.

  4. Click the Video filters tab.

  5. Select the filter you want to add to your video. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.

  6. (Optional) Below the video filter options, click the Apply to all future meetings toggle to apply this filter as the default for all meetings you join or host.

  7. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  8. In the lower-right corner, tap More .

  9. Under Settings, tap Meetings.

  10. Under Video, tap Background & effects.

  11. Tap the Video filters tab.

  12. Tap the filter you want to add to your video. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.

  13. (Optional) Tap the Apply to all meetings toggle to continue using this filter for all meetings joined on this device.

  14. When finished selecting a filter, in the top-left corner, tap the minimize icon to return to the meeting.

Apply studio effects

The studio effects feature allows you to apply eyebrows, mustache or beard, and lip color filters as part of your video appearance.

When you turn on this feature during a meeting, Zoom’s technology uses your device’s camera to detect the movements and positioning of your face to apply the selected filter effect. Such data does not leave your device, is not retained, is not used to identify you, and is only used to generate the selected effects.

Note: The studio effects feature may not be available for all regions and account types. If you do not see a specific feature, you may not have access to use it.

  • Windows | macOS
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click the Video & effects tab.
  4. Click the Studio effects tab.
  5. Choose options from the Eyebrows, Mustache & beard, and Lip color sections. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.
  6. (Optional) Below the studio effects options, click the Apply to all future meetings toggle to apply this filter as the default for all meetings you join or host.
Auto-frame video

Auto-framing automatically adjusts your camera view to keep you centered during Zoom Meetings. It helps others see you clearly, even if you move, shift in your seat, or sit closer or farther from the camera.

When you turn on this feature during a meeting, Zoom’s technology uses your device’s camera to detect the movements and positioning of your face to apply auto-framing. Such data does not leave your device, is not retained, is not used to identify you, and is only used to automatically adjusts your camera view.

  • Windows | macOS
Enable or disable Auto-framing from the desktop app:
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Home tab then the Settings button . Alternatively, click your profile picture then click Settings.
  3. Click the Video & effects tab.
  4. Click the Camera tab.
  5. Click the Auto-framing toggle to enable or disable it. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.
Enable or disable Auto-framing when joining a meeting:
  1. Join a meeting.
  2. In the join preview screen, click the dropdown for Select a camera.
  3. Select or deselect Auto-frame my video. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.
Enable or disable Auto-framing during a meeting:
  1. While in a meeting, click the arrow next to Start / Stop Video.
  2. Select or deselect Auto-frame my video. Your video preview will change based on the adjustments you make.

Using avatars in meetings and webinars

Category: Product features > Participant features > Video

How to use an avatar in meetings and webinars

Avatars can be used in conjunction with virtual backgrounds and immersive view, allowing you and others to create an even more fun and captivating scene for your participants and attendees.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
Apply an avatar before a meeting or webinar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click Video & effects .
  4. Click the Avatars tab.
  5. Select your avatar or click the add icon to create a custom avatar. Note: The avatar with a star next to it in your settings will be the avatar that’s used. To use a different avatar, click it and the star will change to that selection.
  6. (Optional) Click the Turn on my avatar when I join a meeting toggle to enable or disable this setting.
Apply an avatar during a meeting or webinar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Start or join a Zoom meeting or webinar.
  3. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the arrow icon next to Video .
  4. Click Video & effects settings.
  5. Click the Avatars tab.
  6. Select your avatar or click the add icon to create a custom avatar. Notes:
  • You can only create a custom cartoon avatar during a meeting. Realistic and stylized avatars require identity match and liveness detection and must be created outside of a meeting.
  • The avatar with a star next to it in your settings will be the avatar that’s used. To use a different avatar, click it and the star will change to that selection.
  1. (Optional) Click the Turn on my avatar when I join a meeting toggle to enable or disable this setting.
Create a custom avatar

Instead of selecting from the available animal characters, you can create a custom avatar, typically to recreate your own personal appearance.

Cartoon avatars

The Cartoon avatar allows you to build a custom human avatar by selecting your preferred hair styles, clothing, and facial features from a gallery of options. You can use your cartoon avatar in a meeting with your camera on or off.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click Video & effects .
  4. Click the Avatars tab.
  5. Next to the None option, click the add icon . A new window will appear to create your cartoon avatar.
  6. Go through each tab, selecting your preferred hair styles, clothing, and facial features from a gallery of options. The avatar preview will update as you make selections.
  7. Click Apply. The custom avatar will be displayed at the top of the list. You can create up to 25 cartoon avatars.
Realistic and stylized avatars

Realistic and stylized avatars use an AI model to analyze your photo and generate a 3D avatar. You can only use realistic and stylized avatars in a meeting when your camera is on. It replaces your live video feed with an AI-generated avatar that looks like you and animates in real time to mirror your expressions.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click Video & effects .
  4. Click the Avatars tab.
  5. Next to the None option, click the add icon . A new window will appear to create your cartoon avatar.
  6. Follow the 4-step wizard to complete the avatar creation.
  • Select your avatar’s appearance: Select Realistic or Stylized. Note: Only continue if you allow Zoom to analyze your photo and store your facial geometry to generate and animate your avatar. The analyzed and stored data can be deleted at any time by deleting the avatar or your Zoom account.
  • Provide a photo: You can upload or take a photo. A face-centering guide overlay helps you position your face correctly. Keep your face centered with your shoulders visible, use good lighting since dark environments may prompt you to retry, and avoid covering your face.
  • Match your likeness: Checks for identity match and liveness detection. You will be asked to look at your camera to complete the identity match to confirm if the avatar will look like the person actually using it in meetings. Liveness detection will be performed by going through a short sequence of on-screen prompts such as moving your head or blinking.
  • Select avatar outfit: You can select Photo outfit to use the same outfit you have on your submitted photo, or select an available outfit from a gallery of options. The avatar preview will update as you make selections.
  1. Click Create then Finish. The custom avatar will be displayed at the top of the list. You can create up to 10 AI avatars.

Note: When you use the avatar in a meeting, an AI Avatar watermark appears on your video feed, visible to all participants.

Delete your custom Avatar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click Video & effects .
  4. Click the Avatars tab.
  5. Click the ellipsis icon on top of the custom avatar you wish to delete then click Delete. Note: Deleted avatars can no longer be retrieved.
Duplicate your custom Avatar

The ability to duplicate a custom avatar only applies to cartoon avatars.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click Video & effects .
  4. Click the Avatars tab. Click the ellipsis icon .
  5. Click the ellipsis icon on top of the custom avatar you wish to duplicate then click Duplicate.
Apply an avatar before a meeting or webinar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the top-left corner, tap your profile picture.
  3. Tap Settings.
  4. Tap Video & effects then Background & effects.
  5. Tap the Avatars tab then select your avatar or tap the add icon to create a custom avatar. Note: Realistic and stylized avatars are not yet supported on mobile devices.
  6. (Optional) Tap the Turn on my avatar when I join a meeting toggle to enable or disable this setting.

Note: The avatar with a star next to it in your settings will be the avatar that’s used. To use a different avatar, tap it and the star will change to that selection.

Apply an avatar during a meeting or webinar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Start or join a Zoom meeting or webinar.
  3. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap More then Backgrounds & effects.
  4. Tap the Avatars tab then select your avatar or tap the add icon to create a custom avatar. Note: Realistic and stylized avatars are not yet supported on mobile devices
  5. (Optional) Tap the Turn on my avatar when I join a meeting toggle to enable or disable this setting.

Note: The avatar with a star next to it in your settings will be the avatar that’s used. To use a different avatar, tap it and the star will change to that selection.

Create a custom avatar

The Cartoon avatar allows you to build a custom human avatar by selecting your preferred hair styles, clothing, and facial features from a gallery of options. You can use your cartoon avatar in a meeting with your camera on or off. Note: Realistic and stylized avatars are not yet supported on mobile devices.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the top-left corner, tap your profile picture.
  3. Tap Settings.
  4. Tap Video & effects then Background & effects.
  5. Tap the Avatars tab.
  6. Next to the None option, tap the Add. A new window will appear to create your cartoon avatar.
  7. Go through each tab, selecting your preferred hair styles, clothing, and facial features from a gallery of options. The avatar preview will update as you make selections.
  8. Tap Apply. The custom avatar will be displayed at the top of the list. You can create up to 25 cartoon avatars.
  9. (Optional) Tap the Turn on my avatar when I join a meeting toggle to enable or disable this setting.
Delete your custom Avatar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the top-left corner, tap your profile picture.
  3. Tap Settings.
  4. Tap Video & effects then Background & effects.
  5. Tap the Avatars tab.
  6. Long tap the custom avatar you wish to delete then tap Delete. Note: Deleted avatars can no longer be retrieved.
Duplicate your custom Avatar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the top-left corner, tap your profile picture.
  3. Tap Settings.
  4. Tap Video & effects then Background & effects.
  5. Tap the Avatars tab.
  6. Long tap the custom avatar you wish to duplicate then tap Duplicate.

Using focus mode

Category: Product features > Participant features > Video

How to use focus mode in a meeting

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
  • Web app
Start focus mode
  1. Start a meeting as the host or co-host.
  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the More icon .
  3. Click the Host tools icon .
  4. Click Advanced.
  5. Click the Focus mode toggle to enable it.
  6. Click Start to confirm, or select the Don’t ask me again check box to skip this confirmation moving forward. When focus mode starts, you and the participants are notified with a banner along the top of the meeting window. While focus mode is active, the focus mode icon is visible in the top-right corner of the meeting window.

Participants in focus mode will only see the video of the host, co-hosts, any participants spotlighted by the host, and their own video. They will only see other participants’ names, their nonverbal feedback or reactions, and hear them when unmuted.

Participants’ shared screens are only visible to the host and co-hosts, but the host can allow all other participants to view as well:

  1. In the meeting controls toolbar, to the right of the Share icon , click the up arrow icon .
  2. Click Host tools for share.
  3. In the Shared screens can be seen by section, select All participants.
  4. (Optional) To return to just host and co-hosts viewing shared content, select Host only. Note: These options are only available when in focus mode.
End focus mode
  1. As the host or co-host, in the meeting controls toolbar, click the More icon .
  2. Click the Host tools icon .
  3. Click Advanced.
  4. Click the Focus mode toggle to disable it. When focus mode ends, you and the participants are notified with a banner along the top of the window that focus mode is ending, and participants with their video on will be seen by everyone.
Start focus mode
  1. Start a meeting as the host or co-host.
  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap the More icon .
  3. Tap the Host tools icon .
  4. Tap General.
  5. Tap the Focus mode toggle to enable it.
  6. Tap Start to confirm. When focus mode begins, you and the participants are notified with a banner along the top of the meeting window. While focus mode is active, the focus mode icon is visible in the top-left corner of the meeting window.

Participants in focus mode will only see the video of the host, co-hosts, any participants spotlighted by the host, and their own video. They will only see other participants’ names, their nonverbal feedback or reactions, and hear them when unmuted.

End focus mode
  1. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap the More icon .
  2. Tap the Host tools icon .
  3. Tap General.
  4. Tap the Focus mode toggle to disable it. When focus mode ends, you and the participants are notified with a banner along the top of the window that focus mode is ending, and participants with their video on will be seen by everyone.
Start focus mode
  1. In the Zoom Web App, start a meeting as the host or co-host.
  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the More icon .
  3. Click Start Focus Mode.
  4. Click Start to confirm, or select the Don’t ask me again check box to skip this confirmation moving forward. When focus mode starts, you and the participants are notified with a banner along the top of the meeting window. While focus mode is active, the focus mode icon is visible in the top-right corner of the meeting window.

Participants in focus mode will only see the video of the host, co-hosts, any participants spotlighted by the host, and their own video. They will only see other participants’ names, their nonverbal feedback or reactions, and hear them when unmuted.

Participants’ shared screens are only visible to the host and co-hosts, but the host can allow all other participants to view as well:

  1. In the meeting controls toolbar, to the right of the Share Screen icon, click the up arrow icon .
  2. Under Shared screens can be seen by, select All participants.
  3. (Optional) To return to just host and co-hosts viewing shared content, select Host only. Note: These options are only available when in focus mode.
End focus mode
  1. As the host or co-host, in the meeting controls toolbar, click the More icon .
  2. Click the Stop Focus Mode. When focus mode ends, you and the participants are notified with a banner along the top of the window that focus mode is ending, and participants with their video on will be seen by everyone.

Using annotation tools for collaboration

Category: Product features > Participant features > Zoom Workplace app

How to use annotation tools for collaboration and brainstorming

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android
  • iOS
Annotate if you are screen sharing

After sharing your screen or a classic whiteboard, annotation controls will display. If you don’t see the annotation tools, click Annotate (if you are sharing your screen) or Whiteboard (if you are sharing a classic whiteboard).

Annotate if you are viewing shared content

While viewing a shared screen or shared classic whiteboard, click the pencil icon in the bottom-left corner.

Available annotation tools

You will see these annotation tools:

Note: The Select, Spotlight, and Save options are only available if you started the shared screen or a classic whiteboard.

  • Mouse: Deactivate annotation tools and switch to your mouse pointer. This button is blue if annotation tools are deactivated.
  • Select (only available if you started the shared screen or a classic whiteboard): Select, move, or resize your annotations. To select several annotations at once, click and drag your mouse to display a selection area.
  • Text: Insert text.
  • Draw: Insert lines, arrows, and shapes. Note: To highlight an area of the shared screen or the classic whiteboard, select the following square or circle icon to insert a semi-transparent square or circle.
  • Stamp: Insert predefined icons like a check mark or star.
  • Spotlight / Arrow: Turn your cursor into a spotlight or arrow.
  • Spotlight (only available if you started the shared screen or a classic whiteboard): Displays your mouse pointer to all participants when your mouse is within the area being shared. Use this to point out parts of the screen to other participants.
  • Arrow: Displays a small arrow instead of your mouse pointer. Click to insert an arrow that displays your name. Each subsequent click will remove the previous arrow placed. You can use this feature to point out your annotations to other participants.
  • Vanishing Pen (only available if you started the shared screen or a classic whiteboard): Allows the presenter to annotate on the classic whiteboard or shared screen without having to erase or undo their last addition, as the annotation will fade away within a couple of seconds.
  • Eraser: Click and drag to erase parts of your annotation.
  • Format: Change the formatting options of annotations tools like color, line width, and font.
  • Undo: Undo your latest annotation.
  • Redo: Redo your latest annotation that you undid.
  • Clear: Delete all annotations.
  • Save: Save shared screen / classic whiteboard and annotations as a PNG or PDF. The files are saved to the computer recording location. Note: This option is only available to viewers if the host has allowed others to save.
  • To change the file format, click the downward arrow next to Save and select one of these options:
  • PNG: Save as a PNG file. If there are multiple classic whiteboards, Zoom will save a PNG file for each classic whiteboard.
  • PDF: Save as a PDF. If there are multiple classic whiteboards, Zoom will save a single PDF containing all classic whiteboards.
  • More : Shows the option to dock the toolbar.
Annotation settings

If you started the shared screen or a classic whiteboard, click More in the screen share controls for these annotation settings:

  • Enable/Disable Annotation for Others: Allow or prevent the participants from annotating on your shared screen.
  • Show/Hide Names of Annotators: Show or hide the participants’ names when they are annotating. If set to show, the participant’s name will briefly display beside their annotation.
Annotation shortcuts

Windows:

  • Undo: Ctrl + Z
  • Redo: Ctrl + Y
  • Mouse mode: Right-click anywhere

macOS:

  • Undo: Command + Z
  • Redo: Command + Shift + Z
  • Mouse mode: Right-click anywhere

Linux:

  • Mouse mode: Right-click anywhere
Annotation tools for shared screen or classic whiteboard
  1. Start sharing your screen.
  2. Tap the pencil icon on your screen. This will open the annotation tools.
  3. Tap the pencil icon again to close the annotation tools.

The annotation tools available are dependent on whether you are using a phone or tablet.

  • Annotation : Show or hide annotation tools.

  • Pen / Highlighter: Tap to switch between these tools.

  • Pen : Tap and drag to draw with a pen in the selected color.

  • Highlighter : Tap and drag to highlight parts of the screen in the selected color.

  • Arrow: Tap and drag to draw an arrow in the selected color.

  • Shape (Tablet only): Tap to select from the following shapes.

  • Line: Tap and drag to draw a line in the selected color.

  • Rectangle: Tap and drag to draw a rectangle in the selected color.

  • Oval: Tap and drag to draw an oval in the selected color.

  • Text (Tablet only): Type text in the selected color on the shared screen.

  • Color: Change the color and line width of your annotations.

  • Erase: Tap on your annotations to remove them.

  • Undo (Tablet only): Remove your last changes.

  • Redo (Tablet only): Add the annotations you previously removed.

  • Clear (Tablet only): Clear your own annotations.

  • Save: Save the current shared screen or classic whiteboard with current annotations.

Annotation tools specific to classic whiteboards

If you started sharing a classic whiteboard, you will see the following annotation tools:

  • Close : Hide the annotation tools. Tap the annotate icon to display annotation tools again.
  • Undo : Remove your last changes.
  • Redo : Add the annotations you previously removed.
  • Pen : Draw with a pen.
  • Eraser : Tap on your annotations to remove them.
  • Shape : Tap and drag to draw a line, rectangle, or oval in the selected color.
  • Color : Change the color of your annotations.
  • Text (Tablet only): Tap to enter text on the classic whiteboard. Tap the system back icon to hide the keyboard to see options to bold, italicize, adjust font size, and text color. Tap anywhere else on the classic whiteboard to finish this text box.
  • Line width: Tap to adjust the line width of your lines and shapes.
  • Highlighter (Tablet only): Tap and drag to highlight parts of the screen in the selected color.
  • Spotlight: Display a red dot on the shared screen at all times. Use this to point out parts of the screen to other participants. This is only available for the user sharing their classic whiteboard or screen.
  • Trash bin : Display options to clear annotations.
  • More : Display the following options.
  • Smart Recognition: Tap the toggle to enable or disable smart recognition drawing. If enabled, Zoom will smooth out your lines and auto-convert drawings to shapes immediately after you draw.
  • Save to Album: Download an image of your classic whiteboard to your device.
  • New Whiteboard (displays on the main toolbar if using a tablet in landscape mode): Add a new classic whiteboard page. After adding a page, tap View all Whiteboards or the pages icon to view and delete pages. Up to 12 classic whiteboards can be used in a session.
Annotation settings

You can choose to allow participants to annotate on your shared screen and whether you want participants’ names to appear next to their annotations.

  1. Tap the pencil icon to hide annotation tools.
  2. Tap More in the host controls.
  3. Tap Meeting Settings for these annotation settings under the Content Share section:
  • Annotate: Allow or prevent participants from annotating on your shared screen.
  • Show Names of Annotators: Show or hide the participants’ names when they are annotating on a screen share. If set to show, the participant’s name will briefly display beside their annotation.
Annotation tools for shared screen or classic whiteboards

Note: You cannot annotate when sharing your entire screen into the meeting via iOS device. You can only annotate when sharing a portion of your screen.

  1. Start sharing your screen.
  2. Tap the pencil icon on your screen. This will open the annotation tools.

  • Shape (iPad only): Tap and hold to choose from these shapes:
