Adding, removing, and sharing your pronouns in Zoom

Category: User profile > Updating user profile

How to add, remove, and manage pronouns in your Zoom profile

You can edit your Zoom profile to include your pronouns so they appear on your Zoom profile card and help your Zoom contacts understand how you’d like to be referred to. When you save your pronouns, you’ll also choose how they’re shared when you join meetings or webinars as a host, participant, or panelist.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. (Optional) If you’re not already on your profile page after signing in, click your profile picture or initials in the top-right corner, then click My Account. Your profile page will open in a new browser tab.
  3. In the side menu, click Profile .
  4. On the right side of your name, click Edit.
  5. In the Pronouns field, enter or update your pronouns.
  6. To remove your pronouns, clear the Pronouns field.
  7. In the How would you like to share your pronouns? drop-down menu, choose how your pronouns are shared when you join meetings or webinars as a host, participant, or panelist:
  • Always share in meetings and webinars: Your pronouns will automatically appear next to your display name in your video thumbnail and in the Participants panel.
  • Ask me every time after joining meetings and webinars: You will be asked every time you join a meeting as a host or participant, or webinar as a host or panelist if you want your pronouns to appear next to your display name in your video thumbnail and in the Participants panel. Note: Choose this option if you want to decide on a meeting-by-meeting basis.
  • Do not share in meetings and webinars: Your pronouns will not appear next to your display name in any meetings or webinars. You can manually share them later. Note: Even if you choose not to share your pronouns in meetings or webinars, your pronouns will still appear in your Zoom profile card and be visible to your Zoom contacts if you have entered them in the Pronouns field.
  1. Click Save. Note: Your pronouns and sharing preferences will be updated based on your saved changes. If you cleared the Pronouns field, your pronouns will be no longer appear on your Zoom profile card, be visible to your Zoom contacts, and be available to share during meetings and webinars.

How to share or stop sharing your pronouns during meetings or webinars

If you’ve added pronouns to your Zoom profile, you can control how they’re shared when you join meetings as a host or participant, or webinars as a host or panelist. Depending on your settings, Zoom can automatically share or hide your pronouns, ask whether you’d like to share them each time you join, or let you manually share or stop sharing them at any time during an eligible meeting or webinar.

Notes:

  • Pronouns for webinar attendees are never visible.
  • Only webinar hosts and panelists can share pronouns during webinars.
  • If you choose to share your pronouns in an eligible meeting or webinar, they appear next to your display name in your video thumbnail and next to your display name in the Participants panel.
Share your pronouns when prompted after joining a meeting or webinar

If you selected the Ask me every time after joining meetings and webinars option in the Zoom web portal, you will be asked to confirm if you want to share your pronouns after joining every meeting as a host or participant, or webinar as a host or panelist.

  1. Join a meeting as a host or participant, or join a webinar as a host or panelist. In the main meeting or webinar screen, a prompt will appear to ask you to choose from the Share or Don’t Share options.
  2. To share your pronouns in the meeting or webinar, click Share. Your pronouns will appear next to your display name in your video thumbnail and next to your display name in the Participants panel unless you choose to stop sharing them.
Manually share your pronouns during a meeting or webinar

If you selected the Do not share in meetings and webinars option in the Zoom web portal or previously stopped sharing your pronouns, you can still manually share them at any time when you join meetings as a host or participant, or webinars as a host or panelist without updating your Zoom profile.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS

  1. Join a meeting as a host or participant, or join a webinar as a host or panelist.

  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the Participants icon . The Participants panel will appear.

  3. Hover over your name and click More.

  4. Click Share My Pronouns. Your pronouns will appear next to your display name in your video thumbnail and next to your display name in the Participants panel for the remainder of the meeting or webinar unless you choose to stop sharing them.

  5. (Optional) You can also hover over your video thumbnail, click the More icon in the top-right corner, then click Share My Pronouns.

  6. Join a meeting as a host or participant, or join a webinar as a host or panelist.

  7. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap the Participants icon .

  8. Tap your name.

  9. Tap Share My Pronouns. Your pronouns will appear next to your display name in your video thumbnail and next to your display name in the Participants panel for the remainder of the meeting or webinar unless you choose to stop sharing them.

Stop sharing your pronouns during a meeting or webinar

If you’re already sharing your pronouns during a meeting or webinar, you can unshare them at any time without removing them from your Zoom profile.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  1. Join a meeting as a host or participant, or join a webinar as a host or panelist.
  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the Participants icon . The Participants panel will appear.
  3. Hover over your name and click More.
  4. Click Unshare My Pronouns. Your pronouns will no longer appear next to your display name in the current meeting or webinar.
  5. (Optional) You can also hover over your video thumbnail, click the More icon in the top-right corner, then click Unshare My Pronouns.

Note: Pronouns remain saved to your Zoom profile unless you remove them from the Zoom web portal.

  1. Join a meeting as a host or participant, or join a webinar as a host or panelist.
  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap the Participants icon . The Participants panel will appear.
  3. Tap your name.
  4. Tap Unshare My Pronouns. Your pronouns will no longer appear next to your display name in the current meeting or webinar.

Note: Pronouns remain saved to your Zoom profile unless you remove them from the Zoom web portal.

Changing your display name on Zoom

Category: User profile > Updating user profile

How to change your name on Zoom

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. Click your profile picture, then click Profile.

  3. Click My profile. A new web browser window will open where you can edit your name in the Zoom web portal.

  4. By your account profile name, click Edit.

  5. For your account profile name, enter your First Name and Last Name.

  6. For your Display Name, enter a name (for example, your first name, full name, or nickname) that will be shown to others on Zoom.

  7. Click Save.

  8. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  9. In the top-left corner, tap your profile picture.

  10. Tap My profile.

  11. Under Personal, tap Display name.

  12. For your account profile name, enter your First Name and Last Name.

  13. For your Display Name, enter a name (for example, your first name, full name, or nickname) that will be shown to others on Zoom.

  14. Tap Save.

  15. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.

  16. In the navigation menu, click Profile.

  17. By your account profile name, click Edit.

  18. For your account profile name, enter your First Name and Last Name.

  19. For your Display Name, enter a name (e.g. your first name, full name, or nickname) that will be shown to others on Zoom.

  20. Click Save.

How to change your name on Zoom when joining a meeting

When you join a Zoom meeting (on the desktop app, mobile app, or web app), you can enter the meeting ID number and have the option to update your name.

If you’re signed in, change your name if you don’t want your default name to appear. If you’re not signed in, enter a display name that will appear to other meeting participants.

How to change your name on Zoom during a meeting

When the host has enabled the Allow participants to rename themselves setting, you have the option to rename yourself during a meeting. When hosts disable this setting, you will not see the option to rename yourself.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web

  1. Join a Zoom meeting on the Zoom desktop app.

  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, click Participants .

  3. Hover your mouse over your name, then click the ellipsis icon .

  4. Click Rename. A pop-up box will appear.

  5. In the pop-up box, enter your display name.

  6. Click Change.

  7. Join a Zoom meeting on the Zoom mobile app.

  8. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap Participants .

  9. Tap your name, then tap Rename. A pop-up box will appear.

  10. In the pop-up box, enter your display name.

  11. Tap Done.

  12. Join a Zoom meeting on the web app.

  13. In the meeting controls toolbar, click Participants .

  14. Hover your mouse over your name, then click More.

  15. Click Rename. A pop-up box will appear.

  16. In the pop-up box, enter your display name.

  17. Click Change.

Finding and changing your personal account profile

Category: User profile > Updating user profile

How to locate your personal account profile information

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Profile.
  3. You can view the following sections and edit settings as needed.
Access and change your profile details and picture

In this section, you can update your profile details, including your picture, display name, pronouns, department, job title, and location. This information is visible to other users when they hover over your profile picture in the Zoom desktop app.

Note: If you are unable to make changes, your manager or account admin may have restricted these settings. Contact your account admin for assistance.

  • Profile picture: To the left of your account profile name, click the profile picture avatar to add, change, or delete it. You can also adjust the crop area on your current picture or upload a new one. Learn more about changing or removing your Zoom profile picture.
  • Profile information: Click Edit on the right side to update your profile information. After making any changes, click Save.
  • First Name and Last Name: Your first and last name is the full name on your Zoom account, and will appear to other users on the same account. This can be different than your display name.
  • Display Name: Your display name is the name that appears on your profile across the Zoom platform, such as the default name when joining a meeting or webinar, your profile card, and in meetings and webinars. Up to 10 Chinese characters are supported for the display name. Note: If you are unable to change your display name, your account admin might have prevented you from changing this item. Please contact your account admin to make any changes.
  • Name Pronunciation: Enter the phonetic spelling of your name to be displayed on your profile card.
  • Pronouns: Enter your pronouns and choose whether you want to share them in meetings and webinars. Note: If you are unable to add or change your pronouns, your account admin might have prevented you from changing this item. Please contact your account admin to make any changes.
  • Location: Enter your specific point or area.
  • Company: Enter the company or organization to which you belong.
  • Department: Enter your division or functional area.
  • Job Title: Enter your specific role or position.
  • Manager: Enter your manager’s name.
Access the Personal information section

In the Personal information section, you can manage your personal settings, including your direct contact phone number, time zone, date and time format, and default Zoom language.

  • Phone: Add up to three external phone numbers to your profile. To add a phone number, click Add. When adding an external number, Zoom will prompt you to verify it before it appears in your profile. These phone numbers are your direct contact numbers and will appear on your profile card in the Zoom desktop app and mobile app. Users can view your profile card by hovering over or tapping your profile picture.
  • (Optional) When adding a phone number, click the Select a label drop-down menu to apply a label to the phone number; for example, Mobile, Office, Home, or Fax. Labels are visible to other users when they search for you in the Zoom desktop or mobile app, including Zoom Phone and SMS. Note: If you have Zoom Phone direct numbers, they will automatically display under Direct Number in your profile card in the desktop app or mobile app. You don’t need to add your Zoom Phone numbers to your profile.
  • Zoom Phone: If you have a Zoom Phone license, this section displays your direct phone numbers (if you have one assigned), company number, and extension.
  • Zmail: Create your Zoom Mail account. You can use letters, numbers, periods(.), and special characters (_, =, -).
  • My direct chat link: Copy the URL to initiate a one-on-one conversation in Zoom Chat, making it easy to share with others and start a direct chat session.
  • Language: Edit the default language for the Zoom web portal.
  • Time Zone: Edit the time zone to apply to the Zoom desktop app, mobile app, and provisioned desk phones. This allows your local time to be visible on your profile card.
  • Date Format: Edit the date format for the Zoom web portal. This format also applies to Zoom Phone and Zoom Contact Center, but does not affect the desktop or mobile app.
  • Time Format: Edit the time for the Zoom web portal. This format also applies to Zoom Phone and Zoom Contact Center. Note: If you have a Zoom Phone license, this setting will also be used for Zoom Phone. Make sure you set the correct time zone, as it will affect your call history, recordings, voicemail messages, and business hours.
Access the Meeting section

In the Meeting section, you can view and update your personal meeting ID (PMI), personal meeting link, and host key as needed.

  • Personal Meeting ID: A personal meeting ID (PMI) is a dedicated 10- or 11-digit number that is assigned to each licensed user’s account, and this becomes the user’s personal meeting room. Click Edit on the right side to change your personal meeting ID or select the Use your Personal Meeting ID for instant meetings check box to always use your PMI for instant meetings instead of automatically generating a meeting ID.
  • Personal Link: A personal link is another way to access your personal meeting room. It is a personalized alias for your PMI. If you are a licensed user on a Business, Education, or Enterprise account, you can set and customize a personal link. Click Customize on the right to set one or edit your existing personal link.
  • Host Key: A host key is a 6-digit PIN used to claim host controls in a meeting, such as when you join a meeting by phone. Click the eye icon to view your host key and Edit to change it.
Access the Account section

In the Account section, you can view your assigned licenses and your account number.

  • License: Displays the licenses, permissions, and add-ons assigned to you. If you have a Zoom Phone license, you will see your calling package. This section also displays your meeting capacity and webinar capacity (if applicable). To change this, you will need to purchase and assign different licenses.
  • Account No: This is your account number. You can note this if you call into Zoom Support for assistance, as it will help locate your account faster.
Access the Sign In section

In the Sign In section, you can view your sign-in information, such as email address, password, and any linked accounts used for login. Account owners and admins can restrict sign-in methods for users on the account under the account security settings.

  • Sign-In Email: Click Edit to change your email address and password used to sign in. If you do not have the Edit option or would like additional instructions, learn more about changing your email.
  • Sign-In Phone Number: You can sign in to your Zoom account using your phone number. Click Add to set up and verify a sign-in phone number. If you have already added your sign-in phone number, you can click Edit to change it or click Remove to remove it from your account.
  • Sign-In Password: Click Edit to change your password used to sign in. This option is not available if you sign in using single sign-on (SSO).
  • Two-Factor Authentication: Enable or disable two-factor authentication (2FA) through an authentication app. Learn more about using two-factor authentication.
  • OTP Authentication: Enable or disable the one-time passcode (OTP) security feature. OTP is designed to help keep your account more secure.
  • Linked Accounts: Displays your linked accounts that can be used to sign in. For example, SSO or Google.
Access the Where you’re logged in section

In the Where you’re logged in section, you can view a detailed list of all devices and sessions where your Zoom account is signed in. You will see information about each device or session as applicable, such as device name, hardware type, location, operating system or browser name, timestamp of last login, and more.

  • To sign out of an individual device or session, click the sign out icon , then click Sign out to confirm.
  • To sign out of all sessions, click Sign me out of all sessions, then click Sign out to confirm. This can be useful if you misplace a device that has Zoom installed and signed in.
Access the Others section

In the Others section, you can view your associated groups (if assigned), your calendar and contacts integration, and data transit.

  • User Group: Displays the user groups your account owner or admin has assigned you to.
  • Calendar and Contacts Integration: Set up or change calendar and contacts integration with Google, Office365 or Exchange.

Managing your profile picture on the Zoom web portal

Category: User profile > Updating user profile

How to manage your profile picture on the Zoom web portal

In the Zoom web portal, you can manage your profile picture. Any changes made will reflect across devices where your Zoom account is signed in.

Add a new profile picture
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Profile.
  3. In the section with your name and other personal details, click the pencil icon in the picture frame.
  4. Drag and drop the file or click Choose Files to upload your picture. Note: Select a JPG/JPEG, GIF, or PNG file smaller than 2MB.
  5. (Optional) Adjust the crop area as needed.
  6. Click Save.
Change your existing profile picture
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Profile.
  3. In the section with your name and other personal details, click the pencil icon in the picture frame.
  4. Click Change.
  5. Select your preferred picture and then click Open. Note: Select a JPG/JPEG, GIF, or PNG file smaller than 2MB.
  6. (Optional) Adjust the crop area as needed.
  7. Click Save.
Delete your profile picture
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Profile.
  3. In the section with your name and other personal details, click the pencil icon in the picture frame.
  4. Click Delete, then click Yes.

How to troubleshoot profile picture changes not reflecting in meetings

If the changes you made on your profile picture do not reflect during meetings, you may need to sign out, restart the Zoom app, and sign back in.

For additional troubleshooting, you can also try more methods to troubleshoot your profile picture not appearing in meetings.

Zoom Team Chat

Using Chat Compose with AI

Category: AI features > Features

How to reply to a message using Chat Compose with AI

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Chat tab .
  3. Next to the message you want to respond to, click the ellipsis icon . Additional options for this message will appear.
  4. Click Reply with AI. A window will open to generate a response. The message you are responding to will be the basis for the generated reply.
  5. Tell AI to… (Optional): Provide a draft of what your response would look like, or enter a command for AI. This gives additional context and a sample of your writing style for AI to mimic in its generated reply. This can be up to 1000 characters.
  6. Click Generate. Your generated response will appear. Note: You’ll also see a reminder about the accuracy of AI-generated content when generating a new chat message.
  7. (Optional) If the generated response is not entirely satisfactory, click Try another to have a new response generated. Note: You’ll see a brief notice at the bottom of the Chat Compose area that says, “AI-generated content may be inaccurate.”
  8. (Optional) You can reconfigure the response with the Make Longer, Make Shorter, or Change Tone to… options. Select one of these options, and click Generate for a new response. Add or adjust your drafted response to better guide and influence the rephrased response.
  9. When you are satisfied with the generated response, click Insert or Replace. ** Insert** copies the generated response into the reply compose box without changing any previous drafts you have created. Replace copies the generated response into the reply compose box and overwrites the current draft.
  10. Press Enter or click the send icon .

How to create a message using Chat Compose with AI

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Chat tab .
  3. Click the AI icon in the text compose box, or at the bottom of the window. A window will open to generate a message.
  4. Provide a draft of what your response would look like, or enter a command in the Tell AI to… box. This gives additional context and a sample of your writing style for Zoom AI to mimic in its generated reply. This can be up to 1000 characters.
  5. Click Generate. Your generated response will appear. Note: You’ll also see a reminder about the accuracy of AI-generated content when generating a new chat message.
  6. (Optional) If the generated response is not entirely satisfactory, click Try another to have a new response generated.
  7. (Optional) You can reconfigure the response with the Make Longer, Make Shorter, or Change Tone to… options. Select one of these options, and click Generate for a new response. Add or adjust your drafted response to better guide and influence the rephrased response.
  8. When you are satisfied with the generated response, click Insert or Replace. ** Insert** copies the generated response into the reply compose box without changing any previous drafts you have created. Replace copies the generated response into the reply compose box and overwrites the current draft.
  9. Press Enter or click the send icon .

Dashboard for Chat

Category: Analytics and reporting > Admin analytics > Dashboard

How to access the Chat dashboard

  1. Sign in to the Zoomweb portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Dashboard.
  3. At the top of the Dashboard, click the Chat tab.
  4. In the Usage & Adoption tab, you can have an at-a-glance view of chat usage and adoption at a specified time. Data includes:
  • Active Users: Users who sent messages during the specified time.
  • Message Sent: Number of messages sent based on the specified time.
  • Active Channels: Channels that sent at least one message during the specified time.
  • Number of Channels: Breakdown of public and private channels, including active and inactive channels. This is a point in time, it is not impacted by selected date range.
  • Message volume by chat type: Chat type includes public channel, group chat, private channel, and 1:1 chat.
  • Messages Type: Message type includes text, images, files, GIPHYs, code snippets, and audio.
  • Leaderboard top 10 Channels: Can be sorted by Number of messages sent or Number of Users and by Public Channel, Private Channel, or Channels (All). Data includes channel name, number of users, number of messages sent, and message type.
  1. In the User Activities tab, use the following options to filter or customize the data:
  • Use the drop-down menu and tabs at the top of the page to select a date range.
  • View data as Daily, Weekly, or Monthly.
  • Use the search box to only display metrics for a specific user.
  • Click Export to CSV to download a CSV file containing the filtered data.

Metrics glossary

Use the following list for explanations of the metrics available in the Chat dashboard.

Sent Messages: Total, 1-on-1, and channel/group messages sent. This consists of all message types (text, files, images, code snippet, GIPHYs, audio, and video messages).

  • Total: Total messages sent.
  • 1:1: 1-on-1 messages sent (Messages directly sent to another Zoom user).
  • Channels & Group Chats: Messages sent in a channel or group.

Sent Messages by Type: Messages sent broken down by type (text, files, images, code snippet, GIPHYs, audio, and video messages).

  • Text: Messages sent that only contain text
  • Files: Files sent, which consists of local files and files sent using file sharing integrations (Dropbox, Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, and Microsoft SharePoint)
  • Images: Images sent, which consists of these image formats: PNG, JPG, and screen capture
  • Code Snippet: Code snippets sent.
  • GIPHYs: Animated GIFs (Giphy) sent.
  • Audio: Audio messages sent
  • Videos: Video files sent.

How to use overall metrics

You can also view the overall messages sent in the account on the main Dashboard page.

  1. Sign in to the Zoomweb portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Dashboard.
  3. Under the Meetings heading, click the drop down arrow next to Top 10 Users By or Usage By, then click Chat Sent Messages.

Introducing the new Zoom Chat experience

Category: Features

Key features and improvements

Simplified compose box: A cleaner, more streamlined compose box makes it easier to focus on writing messages. You can personalize it by adding or removing tools based on what you use most, customize the send button, choose whether Enter sends a message or starts a new line, and auto-translate messages directly in the compose box.

Unified expression picker (Emojis & GIFs): Emojis and GIFs are combined into a single picker with global search, making it faster to find the right way to express how you’re feeling, whether that’s a reaction, a visual response, or a bit of fun.

Inline images and files: Compose messages with images and files placed directly inline with your text. You can reorder them as needed, making it easier to reference specific visuals or documents exactly where they matter in your message.

Quick hover message actions: Common message actions are just one click away. React instantly using your recently used emojis without opening the message menu, and customize the quick hover menu to match how you work.

FAQs for the new Zoom Chat experience

How do I access the new Zoom Chat experience?

The updated experience is enabled automatically. If you don’t see it, confirm that your Zoom desktop app is updated to version 7.0.5 or later, and restart your desktop app.

How do I confirm that Zoom works properly with my organization’s security software?

Confirm that Zoom is excluded from antivirus or DLP (Data Loss Prevention) restrictions.

Using AI agents in Zoom Chat

Category: Features

Understanding AI agents in Zoom Chat

AI agents combine multiple capabilities, including the following components:

User experience

Users can interact directly with AI agents through direct messages, or add agents to chat channels. They support:

  • Responses with citation to sources
  • Interactive response options for actions such as creating a task, opening a document, or scheduling a follow-up
Knowledge base

AI agents can be configured to use knowledge base from a variety of sources, including:

  • Chat thread history and replies
  • Meeting transcripts and recordings
  • Zoom Hub and internal knowledge bases
  • Approved public URLs when appropriate
Skills and tools

Users can configure AI agents to leverage skills and tools from a variety of sources. These skills and tools enable AI agents to retrieve content, perform actions, and interact with other systems. Sources may include:

  • Zoom product and services (for example, tools that retrieve meetings, chat messages, recordings, or tasks)
  • Third-party integrations (for example, tools that read content from Jira, Confluence, Google Drive, Box, or Asana)

How to create an AI agent in Zoom Chat

You can create an agent in two ways: by typing in a description of your agent or by using a template.

Create an agent using description
  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. In the toolbar, click the AI agents icon (next to All).
  4. In the upper-right corner, click the + Create button.
  5. (Optional) In the upper right-corner, click the Plus icon button and click AI agent under New.
  6. In the description box, enter a detailed description of the task you want the agent to perform then click Send. Wait for the task to be completed.
  7. In the top menu, select the Configure tab to set up your agent.
  8. Enter the following details:
  • Name: A clear and unique title that reflects the agent’s purpose.
  • Description: A detailed explanation of what the agent does and how it assists users. Be specific about:
  • Responsibilities
  • Capabilities
  • Limitations
  • Example tasks or questions
  • This helps the system generate accurate behavior and more relevant responses.
  • Avatar: A visual representation of the agent. Automatically generated upon creation; users can select from preset options or upload a custom image.
  • Agent instructions: Specific rules and guidelines that define how the agent behaves. This includes tone, response style, limitations, and any step-by-step processes the agent should follow when assisting users.
  • Skills: The set of abilities the agent can use to perform tasks. Selecting the appropriate skills enables the agent to move from reasoning to taking action.
  • Choose the skills your agent will use:
  • Add built-in skills: Add skills pre-built by Zoom that are ready to use out of the box.
  • Add personal skills: Add skills you have created or uploaded to extend your agent’s capabilities.
  • Suggested Prompts: Provide example user inputs to guide interaction. Examples:
  • “Schedule a meeting for tomorrow”
  • “Summarize this chat”
  • “Create a task from this discussion”
  • Tools: Defines the integrations and functional capabilities available to the agent, enabling it to take specific actions beyond standard responses. This includes access:
  • Zoom tools: Provides access to native Zoom functionalities in Zoom products such as Chat, Meetings, Docs, and Tasks
  • Third-party tools: Enables integration with external platforms including Jira, Confluence, and Google Drive
  • Knowledge: Choose the knowledge sources your agent will use to generate responses. Add sources by entering URLs, uploading files, or add/select content from Zoom Hub, and Zoom Chat.
  • Add Zoom assets, enter a URL, or upload files.
  • Websites: Enter or add URL
  • Local Files: Upload up to 100 files (30MB each) in these formats: .pdf, .txt, .md, .docx, .pptx, .csv, .xlsx, .json
  • Meetings: Add Zoom meetings from your meeting history
  • Zoom Hub: Add files and folders from your personal and shared folders
  • Chat: Add chat channels you’re a member of
  1. In the upper right corner, click Done to create the agent.
Create an AI agent using templates (Premade by Zoom)
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. In the toolbar, click the AI agents icon (next to All).

  • Example tasks or questions
  • This helps the system generate accurate behavior and more relevant responses.
  • Avatar: A visual representation of the agent. Automatically generated upon creation; users can select from preset options or upload a custom image.
  • Agent instructions: Specific rules and guidelines that define how the agent behaves. This includes tone, response style, limitations, and any step-by-step processes the agent should follow when assisting users.
  • Skills: The set of abilities the agent can use to perform tasks. Selecting the appropriate skills enables the agent to move from reasoning to taking action.
  • Choose the skills your agent will use:
  • Add built-in skills: Add skills pre-built by Zoom that are ready to use out of the box
  • Add personal skills: Add skills you have created or uploaded to extend your agent’s capabilities
  • Suggested Prompts: Provide example user inputs to guide interaction. Examples:
  • “Schedule a meeting for tomorrow”

  • “Create a task from this discussion”

  • Add Zoom assets, enter a URL, or upload files
  • Websites: Enter or add URL
  • Local Files: Upload up to 100 files (30MB each) in these formats: .pdf, .txt, .md, .docx, .pptx, .csv, .xlsx, .json

How to configure an existing AI agent in Zoom Chat

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. In the toolbar, click the AI agents icon (next to All).
  4. Under Created by me select the agent you want to configure.
  5. In the upper right-corner, click the pencil icon and click the Configure tab.

How to share an AI agent in Zoom Chat

Note: Before sharing an AI agent, an admin must enable sharing permissions.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. Click Agents, then click All Agents.
  4. Click the agent you want to share, then the click the share icon in the upper-right corner.
  5. Under This agent is available to, choose one of the following:
  • Anyone in your organization: This agent will be accessible to everyone in your organization.
  • Specific users in your organization: Users you share this with will have access to this agent.
  • Only you: Only you will be able to access and use this agent.
  1. (Optional) Click Copy link, to copy the share link for the agent.
  2. Click Apply.

How to edit an AI agent in Zoom Chat

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. Under Agents, click All Agents.
  4. Select the agent you want to edit.
  5. Click the edit (pencil) icon.
  6. Update the description, or open the Configure tab to review and adjust settings.
  7. Click Update to save your changes.

How to delete an AI agent in Zoom Chat

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. Under Agents, click All Agents.
  4. Select the agent you want to delete.
  5. Click the three dots (…), then click Delete.
  6. (Optional) Uncheck the Also delete previous chats with this agent checkbox, if you want to keep your previous chats with the agent.
  7. Click Delete.

Notes: After deletion, the agent can’t be restored.

How to add AI agents using add agents option

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. Select the channel where you want to add the agent.
  4. Click the More icon from the upper right corner, then click View Agents & integrations.
  5. Click the Agents & integrations tab.
  6. Under Agents, click Add agents.
  7. Select from the available agents on the list.
  8. Click the + Add to channel button to add the agent.
  9. (Optional) Click the following agent filters to search and add an agent:
  • All
  • My Agents
  • Shared with me
  • Premade by Zoom (if available)

The agent will be added to the channel.

How to add AI agents using the search option

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. Select the channel where you want to add the agent.
  4. Click the More icon from the upper right corner, then click View Agents & integrations.
  5. Click the Agents & integrations tab.
  6. In the search field, enter the name of the agent.
  7. Click Add to channel.
  8. If a verification dialog appears, click Add.

The agent will be added to the channel.

How to add AI agents using mention

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. Select the channel where you want to add the agent.
  4. Type **@** in the chat field to search for an agent and click the plus + icon.
  5. If a verification dialog appears, click Add.

The agent will be added to the channel.

How to add AI agents using sharer or recipient view

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. Select the channel where you want to add the agent.

The agent will be added to the channel.

How to add MCP tool

  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. In the toolbar, click the AI agents icon (next to All).

How to remove AI agents from the channel

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Chat.
  3. Select the channel where you want to remove the agent.
  4. Click the More icon from the upper right corner, then click View Agents & integrations.
  5. Click the Agents & integrations tab.
  6. Under Agents, select the agent that you want to remove and click the three dots and click Remove from this channel.

How to configure or edit chat channel permissions

You can set advanced permissions when creating a new channel or edit them for an existing channel.

Note: Only the channel owner or admin can edit permissions for existing channels.

New channel
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Chat.
  3. Click the plus icon in the upper right corner and click Channel.
  4. Enter the name of the channel.
  5. Click Advance permissions.
  6. Edit the following options:
  • Who can add members
  • All channel members
  • Only the channel owner and admins
  • External users
  • External users can be added
  • Who can send messages
  • Everyone
  • Only the channel owner and admins, plus specific people
  • Only the channel owner and admins
  • Allow everyone to reply
  • Who can use @all
  • Everyone
  • Only the channel owner and admins
  • Disable @all for this channel
  • Who can add, edit and remove tabs
  • All members
  • Only the channel owner and admins
  • Who can add agents
  • All members
  • Only members in your organization
  • Only the channel owner and admins
  • Who can add apps
  • All members
  • Only members in your organization
  • Only the channel owner and admins
  • Workflow Automation
  • Members can use Workflow Automation
  • All members
  • Only the channel owner and admins
  • Instant meetings
  • Allow starting instant meetings with all members
  • Who can start instant meetings
  • All members
  • Only the channel owner and admins
Existing channel
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Chat, then click All.
  3. Click Chats & Channels.
  4. Select the channel you want to edit.
  5. Move your cursor over the channel name at the top and click to More actions.
  6. Click Edit channel, then click the Advanced permissions dropdown menu.
  7. Edit the permissions then click Save changes.

Adding and managing Zoom contacts

Category: Getting started and setting up

How to add a contact

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web app
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  5. Enter the email address of the contact you want to add.

  5. To invite a contact by entering their email address:
  6. Enter the email address of the contact you want to add.
  7. (Optional) Enter a message to include with the contact request.
  8. Tap Send.

  10. Tap Invite with QR code.

Notes:

How to manage contact requests

Before you can meet instantly with a contact or chat with them, the added contact must approve the request. In your Contact requests, you can view all pending, accepted, and declined requests.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. In the navigation bar, click the Contacts tab . Note: If you don’t see the Contacts tab, click the More tab, then click Contacts.

  3. In the left panel, click Contact requests.

  4. Click Accept to add this contact to your list. This contact will appear on the Contacts tab, under External for both users.

  5. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  6. In the navigation bar, tap the Contacts tab . Note: If you don’t see the Contacts tab, tap the More tab, then tap Contacts.

  7. Tap Contact requests.

  8. Tap the pending contact.

  9. Tap Accept to add this contact to your list. This contact will appear on the Contacts tab, under External contacts for both users.

How to manage and organize contacts

Besides meeting and chatting with contacts, you can also star important contacts, block, or delete them. If you want to get more detailed and precise with your sorting of contacts and channels, you can sort them into folders in the Chat tab.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
  • Web app
Star a contact

Starring a contact will add them to the Starred section in Chat, Contacts, and Phone, providing quick access to the contact or chat channel.

To star a contact using search:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Use the search bar to search for the contact.
  3. Click the contact’s name to display the chat thread with that contact.
  4. In the top-left corner of the chat window next to the contact’s name, click the star icon . The contact will appear in the Starred sections under the Phone, Chat, and Contacts tabs.

To star a contact using the contacts directory or the Chat side panel:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation bar, click the Contacts tab or Chat tab . Note: If you don’t see either tab, click the More tab, then click Contacts or Chat.
  3. Locate the contact you want to star.
  4. Hover over their name, then click the ellipsis icon .
  5. Click Star this contact. The contact will appear in the Starred sections under the Phone, Chat, and Contacts tabs.

You can also star chat groups and channels. If you have a Zoom Phone license, you can star contacts using your call history.

Add a contact to your VIP Contacts list

If VIP Delegation is enabled for your contact and you are a delegator, you can add contacts to your VIP Contacts list to prioritize calls from those contacts. You can also assign a delegate to manage your VIP Contacts list. Learn more about using VIP delegation.

Block a contact

Blocking a user will prevent them from chatting with you, and if they are not already a contact, will also prevent them from sending you a contact request.

To block someone by using the contacts directory or the Chat side panel:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation bar, click the Contacts tab or Chat tab . Note: If you don’t see either tab, click the More tab, then click Contacts or Chat.
  3. Locate the contact you want to block.
  4. Hover over their name, then click the ellipsis icon .
  5. Click Block contact. A confirmation dialog will appear.
  6. Confirm you want to block the contact by clicking Block. The contact will now show a blocked icon and label next to their name.

Note: To unblock a contact, follow the steps to block them, but choose Unblock contact, which replaces the Block contact option.

Delete a contact

Deleting a contact will prevent them from being able to continue chatting with you, but unless blocked, they can request to be a contact again.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation bar, click the Contacts tab or Chat tab . Note: If you don’t see either tab, click the More tab, then click Contacts or Chat.
  3. Locate the contact you want to delete.
  4. Hover over their name, then click the ellipsis icon .
  5. Click Delete contact. A confirmation dialog will appear.
  6. Confirm you want to delete the contact by clicking Delete.

  2. In the navigation bar, tap the Contacts tab . Note: If you don’t see the Contacts tab, tap the More tab, then tap Contacts.
  3. Locate the contact you want to star, then tap their name.
  4. In the top-right corner, tap the star icon . The contact will appear in the Starred sections under the Phone, Chat, and Contacts tabs.

You can also start chat groups and channels. If you have a Zoom Phone license, you can star contacts using your call history.

  3. Note: If you don’t see the Contacts tab, tap the More tab, then tap Contacts.
  4. Locate the contact you want to delete, then tap their name.
  5. In the top-right corner, tap the ellipsis icon .
  6. Tap Delete contact. A confirmation dialog will appear.
  7. Confirm you want to delete the contact by tapping Delete.
Star a contact

Starring a contact will add them to the Starred section in Chat, Contacts, and Phone, providing quick access to the contact or chat channel.

To star a contact using search:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  2. Use the search bar to search for the contact.
  3. In the search results, hover over the contact’s name, then click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Click Star this contact.
  5. The contact will appear in the Starred sections under the Phone, Chat, and Contacts tabs.

To star a contact using the contacts directory or the Chat side panel:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  2. In the navigation bar, click the Contacts tab or Chat tab . Note: If you don’t see either tab, click the More tab, then click Contacts or Chat.
  3. Locate the contact you want to star.
  4. Hover over their name, then click the ellipsis icon .
  5. Click Star this contact. The contact will appear in the Starred sections under the Phone, Chat, and Contacts tabs.

You can also star chat groups and channels. If you have a Zoom Phone license, you can star contacts using your call history.

Block a contact

Blocking a user will prevent them from chatting with you, and if they are not already a contact, will also prevent them from sending you a contact request.

To block someone by using the Chat side panel:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  2. In the navigation bar, click the Chat tab . Note: If you don’t see the Chat tab, click the More tab, then click Chat.
  3. Locate the contact you want to block.
  4. Hover over their name, then click the ellipsis icon .
  5. Click Block contact. A confirmation dialog will appear.
  6. Confirm you want to block the contact by clicking Block. The contact will now show a blocked icon and label next to their name.

Note: To unblock a contact, follow the steps to block them, but choose Unblock contact, which replaces the Block contact option.

Delete a contact

Deleting a contact will prevent them from being able to continue chatting with you, but unless blocked, they can request to be a contact again.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  2. In the navigation bar, click the Chat tab . Note: If you don’t see the Chat tab, click the More tab, then click** Chat**.
  3. Locate the contact you want to delete.
  4. Hover over their name, then click the ellipsis icon .
  5. Click Delete contact. A confirmation dialog will appear.
  6. Confirm you want to delete the contact by clicking Delete.

Creating and using Zoom Chat channels

Category: Getting started and setting up

How to view and join channels

  • Windows | macOS
  • Linux
  • Android | iOS
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Chat tab to see a list of channels, group chats, chat folders, and 1:1 conversations you currently belong to. The chat list will indicate if a channel is public or private , while 1:1 chats will show the user’s profile picture or initials.
  3. At the top of the panel, click the down arrow icon next to Chat, and click Join a Channel. A window will appear with a list of channels you can join or search for a specific channel.
  4. Use the search bar to find a channel. Hovering your cursor over the channel names provides the following options:
  • Preview: View more information about the channel, including channel description, members, and recent messages (if previous messages are allowed to be viewed by new channel members). Click Join Channel to join the channel, or Close to exit this preview.
  • Join: Immediately join the selected channel.

  3. Hover your cursor over the Recents chat category, click the more button , and then select Join a Channel. A window will appear with a list of channels you can join or search for a specific channel.

  4. Use the search bar to find a channel. Hovering your cursor over the channel names provides the following options:

  5. Preview: View more information about the channel, including channel description, members, and recent messages (if previous messages are allowed to be viewed by new channel members). Click Join Channel to join the channel, or Close to exit this preview. Note: This preview is only available for public channels.

  6. Join: Immediately join the selected channel.

  7. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  8. Tap the Contacts tab .

  9. At the top of the screen, Tap the Channels section to see a list of channels you currently belong to.

  10. In the top-right corner, tap the plus icon + and then tap on Join a Channel.

  11. Use the search bar to find a public channel. Note: To join a private channel, you must be added to that channel by an existing member. Private channels cannot be searched for and joined.

  12. Tap the channel to view more information about the channel, including channel description, members, and recent messages (if previous messages are allowed to be viewed by new channel members). Note: This preview is only available for public channels.

  13. Tap Join Channel to continue joining the channel.

How to create a new chat channel

If a chat channel suiting your needs doesn’t exist, you can easily create a new channel specific to your needs.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Zoom Web App
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Chat tab .
  3. At the top of the panel, click the down arrow next to Chat, and click Create a Channel. Note: If this option is grayed out, your account admin has prevented your group from adding channels.
  4. Enter the following required details to create a new channel:
  • Channel Name: Enter a display name to help others identify your channel.
  • Channel Type: Select the channel type.
  • Public: Anyone in your organization can join your channel.
  • Private: Only invited people can join your channel. Private channel creation can be disabled in Chat by account owners and admins. If the private channel setting is disabled, the shared space creation setting is also automatically disabled. Note: If one of these options is grayed out, your account admin has prevented your group from creating that type of channel.
  • Add Members: Enter a name to search for contacts, then click the name to add them to the invite list. Note: You can invite individual users, or you can select an existing channel to invite all members of that channel. You must be a member of the channel to invite all of its members. Inviting all members of a channel is only available for Windows and macOS.
  • Advanced Permissions: Click to view additional channel permissions.
  • Who can add members:
  • Everyone: Any channel members can add additional users.
  • Owner and admins only: Only the channel owner and any designated channel admins can add additional users.
  • External users can be added: If checked, users not in your organization can be added to the channel. Note: If you enable this option, make sure to review the channel privileges of external users.
  • By all channel members: Members internal and external to your organization can add external members.
  • By members in your organization: Only members internal to your organization can add external members.
  • Only by the channel owner and admins: Only the channel owner and any designated channel admins can add additional external users.
  • Who can send messages: Select which channel members are allowed to post in the channel.
  • Everyone: All channel members can post in the channel.
  • Owner and admins, plus specific people: Only the channel owner, designated admins, and specified members can post in the channel.
  • Owner and admins only: Only the channel owner and designated admin can post in the channel.
  • Who can use @all: Select which channel members are allowed to use the @all mention in the channel.
  • Everyone: All channel members can use the @all mention in the channel.
  • Owner and admins only: Only the channel owner and designated admin can use the @all mention in the channel.
  • Disable @all for this channel: Disable the use of the @all mention for this channel. Use of @ mentions for specific users or defined mention groups, are unaffected.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Linux

Information regarding external contacts

Users added to your contact list who are not on the same account as yours will be labeled as External.

For a 1:1 chat with that contact, External will be listed under their name at the top of the chat window:

For a group chat, External will be listed next to the name of any participants who are not a part of the account:

When composing a message in a channel with external users present, a notification above the compose box will appear, warning that there are 1 or more external users present in the group chat or channel.

Details on how channels are ordered in the chat panel

Channels on the desktop app can be organized by sections (folders, 1:1 and group chats, channels, meeting chats, etc), or organized by folders, with those not assigned to a folder being listed under Recents.

With either organization, channels are listed dynamically based on the last modification or notification. This means when a channel receives a new notification, it is moved to the top of the list in that section. This behavior can be changed through the Organize by section and Keep all unread messages on top in chat and channel lists settings on the desktop app.

Folder organization

Group chats, 1:1s, and other channels within a folder are listed by when they were added to the folder, unless manually re-ordered. Any new channels added to a folder are added to the bottom of the list.

Information regarding external contacts

Users added to your contact list who are not on the same account as yours will be labeled as External.

For a 1:1 chat with that contact, External will be listed under their name at the top of the chat window:

For a group chat, External will be listed next to the name of any participants who are not a part of the account:

When composing a message in a channel with external users present, a notification above the compose box will appear, warning that there are 1 or more external users present in the group chat or channel.

Getting started with Zoom Chat

Category: Getting started and setting up

Understanding 1:1 chats, group chats, and channels

You can send chat messages to 3 different recipient groups: a single contact directly, a group of contacts, or an established chat channel with multiple contacts.

One-on-one chats

1:1 chats with other Zoom contacts are the quickest and easiest way to message someone outside of a Zoom Meeting. These conversations will remain available and searchable, even if the other contact is deactivated or deleted. Also, any one-on-one side chats that occur within a meeting are automatically saved to chats (if settings allow).

Group chats

Group chats function like 1:1 chats but include multiple participants and are designed for quick, short-term team discussions. Group chats stay within the chats tab, cannot be named, and are searchable by the names of the members involved. They do not have owners, and any internal member can add or remove participants.

Chat channels

Chat channels are best suited for long-term projects or teams, as they are created with a name, a channel admin, and can be private or public.

  • Private channels cannot be searched for and found by users not already a member of the channel, and current members must add additional members to give them access.
  • Public channels are searchable and joinable by all members of an account, and do not need any special invitation to join.

Channels are also great for announcements.You can designate specific members to have the ability to post, while everyone else can only view and react to messages.

How to use Zoom Chat

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Zoom Web App
  • Android | iOS
How to start a new 1:1 or group chat

To begin messaging with one or more Zoom users:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the** Chat** tab . Note: If you do not see the Chat tab, click the More tab, then click Chat.
  3. In the Chat sidebar, click the plus sign icon , then click Message.
  4. Enter the name or email address of the Zoom contact you want to chat with. Add additional names or email addresses as needed.
  5. Enter your message, then press the Enter key or click the send icon in the lower-right corner of the chat compose box.
How to join a public channel
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the** Chat** tab . Note: If you do not see the Chat tab, click the More tab, then click Chat.
  3. In the Chat sidebar, click the plus sign icon , then click Join channel.
  4. Use the search bar to find a channel.
  5. (Optional) While hovering the cursor over the channel details, click Preview to see the channel description, members, and recent messages.
  6. While hovering the cursor over the channel details, click Join. You will join the channel and can begin messaging those members.

Learn more about joining, creating, and using channels.

How to view your recent history of chats, groups, and channels

When messaging between multiple contacts, chat groups, and channels, it can be difficult to quickly find and return to a previous chat. You can view the 10 previous chat contacts, groups, and channels that you accessed, and jump back to those with a click.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the app header, next to the search bar, click the** **history icon . The 10 previous chat contacts, groups, and channels you’ve viewed will be listed.
  3. Click on a listing to return to that chat.
How to add an external contact

If you’re part of an organization that uses Zoom, everyone in your organization is typically included in your contacts directory automatically, allowing you to begin chatting with anyone in your contacts directory. If you need to chat with someone outside of your organization, you will need to manually add them as a Zoom contact.

Follow these steps to add external Zoom users to your contacts. You can do this even if the other contact does not yet have a Zoom account.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Contacts tab . Note: If you do not see the Contacts tab, click the More tab, then click Contacts.
  3. Click the add icon .
  4. Click Invite a new contact.
  5. Enter one email address at a time.
  6. (Optional) You can send the contact request with personalized message.
  7. Click Send.
  • If the person has a Zoom account, they’ll receive a contact request within Zoom Chat. After they accept the request, you can start chatting with them.
  • If the person doesn’t have a Zoom account, they’ll receive an invitation email to create a Zoom account so they can connect with you. Once they sign up for Zoom, they should click on the link in the email again to confirm the connection.

Learn more about managing your contacts.

How to adjust notifications for chats

You can adjust chat notifications for all chat and channels at once, as well as at the individual chat level. This allows you to prioritize chats and channels that need your immediate attention when there is an update, while setting defaults for new channels you are added to.

Adjust default notification settings for all chats

You can customize how you’re notified of unread messages and whether you receive push notifications for new messages. Follow these steps for basic settings to get you started:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click the** Chat** tab .
  4. Adjust the following settings to manage your notifications:
  • Unread messages
  • When viewing unread messages in a channel:
  • Start at the first unread: Choose this option if you want to go directly to the first unread message in the channel.
  • Start at the latest unread: Choose this option if you want to go to the most recent unread message in the channel.
  • Move messages with new replies to the bottom of the chat: Messages that have received additional replies since you last checked are moved to the bottom of the chat.
  • Read receipts: Indicate when others have seen your messages, for chats and channels with less than 20 members. Others will also see when you have seen their messages.

Learn more about other available chat notification settings.

Adjust notification settings for specific group chats and channels

You can also change notification settings for specific group chats and channels. Follow these steps to get you started:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the** Chat** tab . Note: If you do not see the Chat tab, click the More tab, then click Chat.
  3. Hover your cursor on the chat channel or group chat where you want to adjust notifications, then click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Hover over Notifications to change these settings:
  • Message preferences
  • All messages: Get notified for all message activity in chats.
  • Mentions and replies: Only get notified when someone mentions you (in a group or direct message) or replies to your message.
  • Off: Turn off all chat notifications.
  • Unread message indicator
  • Count unread messages: Shows the number of unread messages beside the chat or channel.
  • No count displayed: Hides the unread message count, though messages will still be marked unread until opened.
How to search for contacts, group chats, channels, or specific messages

You can use the global search bar at the top of the desktop app to search for chats.

How to send files, video or voice messages, screenshots, emoji, animated GIFs, or code snippets

In addition to regular chats, you can use the chat compose box to send additional types of messages or files to enhance your Zoom Chat experience. Some options listed below may not be available, depending on your personal settings in the desktop app or any admin settings at the account or group level.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the** Chat** tab . Note: If you do not see the Chat tab, click the More tab, then click Chat.
  3. Select a chat.
  4. In the chat compose box, click one of the following options:
  • Emoji : Display a list of emojis. Click an emoji to add it to your message.

GIF : Display a list of GIFs. Click GIF to add an animated GIF to your message. Click the heart icon to view your favorite GIFs.

  • File : Display options to attach a file to the message. Click Your Computer or any 3rd-party file services to send a file on Zoom Chat. Note: If sending a video file, recipients will be able play the video directly in the chat window.

  • Screenshot : Minimize the Zoom window and capture a portion of your screen by clicking and dragging the capture box. Once you take the screenshot, you can add arrows, shapes, and text to the image. Note: Click the down arrow icon next to Screenshot to choose if you want to hide the Zoom Chat window in the screenshot.

  • Voice Message : Start recording an audio message to attach to your message.

  • Video Message : Start recording a video message to attach to your message.

  • Code Snippet : Start adding a code snippet to attach to your message.

How to invite chat members to a meeting

You can easily start a meeting from any chat conversation, which will automatically invite all members in a group chat or channel to a meeting.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the** Chat** tab .
  3. Select a chat.
  4. In the top-right corner of the chat window, click the video icon .
  5. (Optional) Click the down arrow icon next to the video icon to decide if you want to meet with video or not. This is the default for the meeting and participants can enable their videos after joining.
  6. Click Yes to confirm inviting all members of the chat group or channel to a meeting.
