Using Webinar Backstage

Category: Product features > Host features > Hosting Webinars

How to use Backstage in a webinar

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Zoom Rooms

When joining a webinar with Backstage enabled, panelists will join the backstage area automatically, whether the webinar is open to attendees or not. This avoids late arrivals appearing in front of attendees before they are ready.

While in the backstage area, the screen is split horizontally, with the live webinar above and everyone in the backstage area below. The ratio of how much space each area occupies in the meeting window can be adjusted by clicking-and-dragging the slider between the two areas. Before the webinar officially starts, the area for the live webinar will display a clear OFF AIR image, to make it clear that no attendees are viewing the webinar yet.

Note: When using dual monitor mode, one screen will display the standard backstage view, while the other is dedicated to the live webinar view.

Just as with a Practice Session, the host will need to start the webinar when they are ready to allow attendees to join and begin viewing the presentation. The host will click the Start Webinar button located on the small banner at the top of the screen. Zoom recommends having at least one panelist in the live webinar area before starting the webinar for attendees, otherwise attendees will see a The host will be right back message. All panelists, in either the live webinar or backstage area, will see a notification that the webinar has started.

Move yourself between the live webinar and backstage area

As the host or a panelist, you can move between the two areas freely, even after the webinar has started.

Note: The host can disable the ability for panelists to move between areas freely, so you may need to contact the host or co-host to be moved. A message will appear if you attempt to move to an area and are not allowed to do so.

To move into the live webinar and be visible to webinar attendees:

  1. On the meeting toolbar, click the Webinar button and then confirm by clicking Go to Webinar. You will be immediately moved to the live webinar area.

To move into the backstage area and continue viewing the live webinar:

  1. On the meeting toolbar, click the Backstage button and then confirm by clicking Go Backstage.

You will be moved immediately to the backstage area.

Move panelists between areas as the host or co-host

The host and any co-hosts can move an individual panelist, a group of panelists, or all panelists in an area between the areas as needed, but the moved panelist(s) is presented with a 5-second countdown if moving to the live webinar.

The host can also prevent panelists from moving themselves between areas, if they prefer that themselves or a co-host handle the timing of those movements.

Notes:

  • Panelists who join from a version older than the minimum version will be prompted to update to the minimum version or higher.
  • Webinar attendees will be prompted to update if being promoted to panelist.
Preventing panelist moving themselves between areas
  1. In the webinar controls, click Participants .
  2. At the top of the participants panel, click the Panelists tab.
  3. At the bottom of the participants panel, click More and, under Allow Panelists to, select Move between Webinar and Backstage. The checkmark to the left of the option indicates whether the option is enabled or disabled. Note: Allowing panelists to move between webinar and backstage is enabled by default.

When viewing the list of Panelists in the Participants panel, panelists are divided by their current location, either under the Webinar section or Backstage section of the list.

Moving an individual panelist
  1. In the webinar controls, click Participants .
  2. At the top of the participants panel, click the Panelists tab.
  3. Hover your pointer over the panelist name and click the button.
  4. Click Move to Backstage or Move to Webinar, depending on which area they are currently in.
Moving multiple panelists at once
  1. In the webinar controls, click Participants .
  2. At the top of the participants panel, click the Panelists tab.
  3. To move panelists from:
  4. …the Webinar to the Backstage, click the button next to the right of the Webinar section.
  5. …the Backstage to the Webinar, click the button next to the right of the Backstage section.
  6. Click Select Panelists… to choose which panelist you want to move.
  7. Select the check box next to each panelist to select to be moved. If there are 8 or more panelists to choose from, a search bar will appear to make finding particular panelists easier.
  8. Click Move to confirm the selection and have those panelists moved. Note: Remember, if moving panelists from Backstage to the live webinar, each panelist will have a 5-second countdown before being moved. There is no countdown for moving to Backstage.
Moving all panelists in an area
  1. In the webinar controls, click Participants .
  2. At the top of the participants panel, click the Panelists tab.
  3. To move panelists from:
  4. …the Webinar to the Backstage, click the button next to the right of the Webinar section.
  5. …the Backstage to the Webinar, click the button next to the right of the Backstage section.
  6. Click Move all to Webinar or Move all to Backstage to move all panelists currently in that area.
  7. (Optional) Select the check box next to Include myself to also be moved with other panelists. This option only appears if you are in the same area as the panelists you are moving.
  8. Click Move All to confirm and have the panelists moved. Note: Remember, if moving panelists from Backstage to the live webinar, each panelist will have a 5-second countdown before being moved. There is no countdown for moving to Backstage.
Control volume and closed captioning in Backstage
Controlling the volume of the audio from the live webinar

While in Backstage, panelists can view the live video feeds and shared content from the live webinar, although audio from the live webinar is muted by default. Each panelist can unmute the audio and adjust the volume as they need. This can be helpful for knowing when your turn presenting in the live webinar is drawing near, starting polling, or when other assistance is needed.

  1. In the live webinar portion of the video window, hover your pointer over the muted volume button . The volume slider will appear.
  2. Click and drag the volume slider as needed to raise or lower the volume.
  3. (Optional) Click the volume button directly to quickly mute or unmute the audio from the live webinar.
Enabling closed captions on video from the live webinar

If captions are enabled in the live webinar, panelists can enable them in the backstage area. This can be useful if you need to keep an eye on what is being discussed, but are chatting with other panelists backstage.

  1. In the live webinar portion of the video window, click the closed caption button to show or hide captions.
End the webinar for attendees only

When at the end of the scheduled time, the host can end the webinar for all attendees, while retaining the panelists for a debrief or recap session. To end the webinar for just attendees:

  1. On the webinar toolbar, click End.
  2. Click End Webinar for Attendees and click End Webinars for Attendees again to confirm. All attendees will be removed from the webinar as if the webinar has ended, while all panelists will remain. All panelists will all be moved to a common area for a private debriefing session.

When joining a webinar with Backstage enabled, panelists will join the backstage area automatically, whether the webinar is open to attendees or not. This avoids late arrivals appearing in front of attendees before they are ready.

While in the backstage area, panelists will only see the live webinar video and shared content. Before the webinar officially starts, the area for the live webinar will display a clear OFF AIR image, to make it clear that no attendees are viewing the webinar yet.

Just as with a practice session, the host will need to start the webinar when they are ready to allow attendees to join and begin viewing the presentation. The host will tap the Start Webinar button located on the small banner at the top of the screen, then tap Start to confirm. All panelists, in either the live webinar or backstage area will see a notification that the webinar has started.

Move yourself between the live webinar and backstage area

As the host or a panelist, you can move between the two areas freely, even after the webinar has started.

Note: The host can disable the ability for panelists to move between areas freely, so you may need to contact the host or co-host to be moved. A message will appear if you attempt to move to an area and are not allowed to do so.

To move into the live webinar and be visible to webinar attendees:

  1. On the meeting toolbar, tap More and then tap Go to Webinar .
  2. Tap Go to Webinar to confirm.
  3. You will have a 5-second countdown before you are moved to the webinar.

To move into the backstage area and continue viewing the live webinar:

  1. On the meeting toolbar, tap More and then tap Go to Backstage .
  2. Tap Go to Backstage to confirm.
  3. You will be moved immediately to the backstage area.
Move panelists between areas as the host or co-host

The host and any co-hosts can move an individual panelist, a group of panelists, or all panelists in an area between the areas as needed, but the moved panelist is still presented with a 5-second countdown if moving to the live webinar. The host can also prevent panelists from moving themselves between areas, if they prefer that themselves or a co-host handle the timing of those movements.

Notes:

  • Panelists who join from a version older than the minimum version will join as a normal attendee, not as a panelist. They must be promoted by the host to a panelist, but cannot be moved Backstage in any case. If they are not needed any longer during the live webinar, they can be demoted back to attendee to continue viewing, put on hold, or can leave the webinar entirely.
  • If the host or co-host promotes an attendee to panelist and that attendee has joined using the minimum version client or higher, the host/co-host can optionally promote them directly to the Backstage area, rather than the live webinar.
Preventing panelist moving themselves between areas
  1. In the webinar controls, tap More .
  2. In the additional options, tap Webinar Settings .
  3. Under the Allow Panelists to section, tap the toggle next to Move between Webinar & Backstage. Note: Allowing panelists to move between webinar and backstage is enabled by default.
Moving an individual panelist
  1. In the webinar controls, tap Participants . The list of panelists is divided by their current location, either the Webinar section or Backstage section.
  2. Tap the name of the participant you want to move.
  3. Tap Move to Backstage or Move to Webinar, depending on which area they are currently in.
Moving multiple panelists at once
  1. In the webinar controls, tap Participants . The list of panelists is divided by their current location, either the Webinar section or Backstage section.
  2. At the top of either section, tap the three dots . To move panelists from…
  3. …the Webinar to the Backstage, tap the button next to the right of the Webinar section.
  4. …the Backstage to the Webinar, tap the button next to the right of the Backstage section.
  5. Tap the name of each panelist you want to move.
  6. At the top-right of the window, tap Move to confirm the selection and have those panelists moved. Note: Remember, if moving panelists from Backstage to the live webinar, each panelist will have a 5-second countdown before being moved. There is no countdown for moving to Backstage.
Moving all panelists in an area

  1. Tap on one of the following options:

  2. Move All: Moves all panelists in this area to the other. If you are also in that area, this option will exclude yourself.

  3. Move all & include myself: Moves all panelists, including yourself, in this area to the other. This option only appears if you are in the same area as the panelists you are moving.

Note: Remember, if moving panelists from Backstage to the live webinar, each panelist will have a 5-second countdown before being moved. There is no countdown for moving to Backstage.

  1. In the webinar controls, tap Participants . The list of panelists is divided by their current location, either the Webinar section or Backstage section.

  2. To move panelists from…

  3. …the Webinar to the Backstage, tap the button next to the right of the Webinar section.

  4. …the Backstage to the Webinar, tap the button next to the right of the Backstage section.

  5. Tap Move all to Webinar or Move all to Backstage, depending on the section you selected.

Control volume and closed captioning in Backstage
Controlling the volume of the audio from the live webinar

While in Backstage, panelists view the live audio and video feeds and shared content from the live webinar. Each panelist can unmute the audio as they need. This can be helpful for knowing when your turn presenting in the live webinar is drawing near, starting polling, or when other assistance is needed.

  1. In the video window, tap the volume button to mute or unmute.
  2. To adjust the volume, use the volume buttons or controls on your mobile device.
Enabling closed captions on video from the live webinar

If captions are enabled in the live webinar, panelists can enable them in the backstage area. This can be useful if you need to keep an eye on what is being discussed, but are chatting with other panelists backstage.

  1. In the video window, tap the closed caption button to show or hide captions.
End webinar for attendees only

When at the end of the scheduled time, the host can end the webinar for all attendees, while retaining the panelists for a debrief or recap session. To end the webinar for just attendees:

  1. In the top-right corner, tap End.
  2. Tap End Webinar for Attendees and then tap End Webinars for Attendees again to confirm. All attendees will be removed from the webinar as if the webinar has ended, while all panelists will remain. All panelists will be moved to the Webinar area.

When joining a webinar with Backstage enabled, panelists will join the backstage area automatically, whether the webinar is open to attendees or not. This avoids late arrivals appearing in front of attendees before they are ready.

While in the backstage area, panelists will only see the live webinar video and shared content. Before the webinar officially starts, the area for the live webinar will display a clear OFF AIR image, to make it clear that no attendees are viewing the webinar yet.

Just as with a practice session, the host will need to start the webinar when they are ready to allow attendees to join and begin viewing the presentation. The host will tap the Start Webinar button located on the controller or touch display, then tap Start to confirm. All panelists, in either the live webinar or backstage area will see a notification that the webinar has started.

Move yourself between the live webinar and backstage area

As the host or a panelist, you can move between the two areas freely, even after the webinar has started.

Note: The host can disable the ability for panelists to move between areas freely, so you may need to contact the host or co-host to be moved. A message will appear if you attempt to move to an area and are not allowed to do so.

To move into the live webinar and be visible to webinar attendees:

  1. Tap Go to Webinar on the controller or touch display.
  2. Tap Enter Webinar to confirm.
  3. You will have a 5-second countdown before you are moved to the webinar.

To move into the backstage area and continue viewing the live webinar:

  1. Tap Go Backstage on the controller or touch display.
  2. Tap Enter backstage to confirm.
  3. You will have a 5-second countdown before you are moved to the webinar.
Move panelists between areas as the host or co-host

The host and any co-hosts can move an individual panelist, a group of panelists, or all panelists in an area between the areas as needed, but the moved panelist is still presented with a 5-second countdown if moving to the live webinar. The host can also prevent panelists from moving themselves between areas, if they prefer that themselves or a co-host handle the timing of those movements.

Notes:

  • Panelists who join from a version older than the minimum version will join as a normal attendee, not as a panelist. They must be promoted by the host to a panelist, but cannot be moved Backstage in any case. If they are not needed any longer during the live webinar, they can be demoted back to attendee to continue viewing, put on hold, or can leave the webinar entirely.
  • If the host or co-host promotes an attendee to panelist and that attendee has joined using the minimum version client or higher, the host/co-host can optionally promote them directly to the Backstage area, rather than the live webinar.
Preventing panelist moving themselves between areas
  1. Tap Participants on the controller or touch display.
  2. Tap More, then tap Allow panelists to move between webinar and backstage. Note: Allowing panelists to move between webinar and backstage is enabled by default.
Moving an individual panelist
  1. Tap Participants on the controller or touch display. The list of panelists is divided by their current location, either the Webinar section or Backstage section.
  2. Tap the ellipses icon to the right of Webinar or Backstage, then tap Select panelists to move.
  3. Tap the panelist, then tap Move.
Moving multiple panelists at once
  1. Tap Participants on the controller or touch display. The list of panelists is divided by their current location, either the Webinar section or Backstage section.
  2. Tap the ellipses icon to the right of Webinar or Backstage, then tap Select panelists to move.
  3. Tap multiple panelists to select them, then tap Move. Note: Remember, if moving panelists from Backstage to the live webinar, each panelist will have a 5-second countdown before being moved. There is no countdown for moving to Backstage.
Moving all panelists in an area
  1. Tap Participants on the controller or touch display. The list of panelists is divided by their current location, either the Webinar section or Backstage section.
  2. Tap the ellipses icon to the right of Webinar or Backstage, then tap Move all to Backstage or Move all to Webinar.
  3. Tap the toggle next to Include myself (on by default), then tap Move All. Note: Remember, if moving panelists from Backstage to the live webinar, each panelist will have a 5-second countdown before being moved. There is no countdown for moving to Backstage.
Control volume and closed captioning in Backstage
Controlling the volume of the audio from the live webinar

While in Backstage, panelists view the live audio and video feeds and shared content from the live webinar. Each panelist can unmute the audio as they need. This can be helpful for knowing when your turn presenting in the live webinar is drawing near, starting polling, or when other assistance is needed.

  1. Use the volume slider on the controller or touch display to adjust the volume.
Enabling closed captions on video from the live webinar

If captions are enabled in the live webinar, panelists can enable them in the backstage area. This can be useful if you need to keep an eye on what is being discussed, but are chatting with other panelists backstage.

  1. On the controller or touch display, tap the Captions ** icon. You may need to tap the More** icon first to see the option.
End webinar for attendees only

When at the end of the scheduled time, the host can end the webinar for all attendees, while retaining the panelists for a debrief or recap session. To end the webinar for just attendees:

  1. On the controller or touch display, tap End.
  2. Tap End Webinar for Attendees and then tap End Webinars for Attendees again to confirm. All attendees will be removed from the webinar as if the webinar has ended, while all panelists will remain. All panelists will be moved to the Webinar area.

Using Webinar practice session

Category: Product features > Host features > Hosting Webinars

How to enable a webinar practice session

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. Do one of the following:
  • Schedule a webinar.
  • Click the title of a webinar that’s already scheduled, then click Edit.
  1. In the** Options** section, do one of the following:
  • Select the Enable Practice Session checkbox. You will see this option if you only have a Webinars license assigned.
  • Select the Before webinar starts, hosts and panelists can access checkbox, then choose Practice session. You will see this option if you have a Zoom Events or Webinars Plus license assigned.
  1. Click Schedule if you’re scheduling a new webinar, or click Save if you’re editing an existing webinar.

How to start a webinar practice session

Only the host, alternative host, and panelists can join practice sessions. There can only be one active practice session for each webinar. For example, if the host starts a practice session and then an alternative host starts one, they will be in the same practice session.

  • Web
  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. On the Upcoming tab, do one of the following:
  • Hover over the webinar with a practice session enabled and click Start Practice Session.
  • Click the title of the webinar, then in the top-right corner, click Start Practice Session. Note: If the options say Start or Start this Webinar, then the practice session is not enabled for the webinar. After clicking Start Practice Session, you will have the option to launch the Zoom Workplace app.

  1. Continue to open the app to start the practice session from your desktop or mobile app. The host, alternative host, and panelists will see a banner at the top of Zoom window that lets them know they are in a practice session.

  2. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  3. At the top of the app, click the Home tab or click the Meetings tab or Calendar tab . Note: If you have set up the calendar and contacts integration to connect your calendar, you will have the Calendar tab. If you haven’t connected your calendar, you will have the Meetings tab.

  4. Click the webinar you want to start the practice session for. The host, alternative host, and panelists will see a banner at the top of Zoom window that lets them know they are in a practice session.

How to start a webinar from within a practice session

  1. Start a webinar practice session.
  2. In the top banner, click Start webinar. A pop-up will appear, informing you that once you click start, attendees can join the webinar.
  3. Click Start to begin the webinar and allow attendees to join. The host and other panelists will see a banner at the top of the Zoom window that lets them know the webinar is now live.

Note: This will not change the original start time that you set when scheduling the webinar. We recommend coordinating with panelists when you wish to join the practice session ahead of the scheduled start time so that the practice session does not go into the scheduled start time.

Hosting a webinar with pre-recorded content

Category: Product features > Host features > Simulive

How to set up a webinar with simulive capability

Create a simulive webinar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. On the right, click Schedule a Webinar.
  4. Next to Webinar Type, choose Simulive.
  5. (Optional) Select the Transition to live afterwards toggle to automatically transition to a live session once simulive playback ends. Note: To transition a simulive webinar to live, a host must be present at the time of the transition.
  6. Next to Recorded Webinar, click Add recording to choose a previously-recorded personal cloud recording to add to simulive, then click Save. Note: If the Transition to live option is enabled, the session duration will remain unchanged. Otherwise, it will automatically adjust to match the length of the content. If the webinar hasn’t transitioned to live yet, you can still manually adjust its duration.
  7. (Optional) In the top-right corner of the video tile, click the edit icon to change the recording. Click the trash icon to remove the recording. Click the video icon to preview the recording.
  8. Select webinar settings as needed.
  9. (Optional) If you want create a recurring series, do the following:
  10. Select the Recurring webinar check box.
  11. Set the recurrence schedule, repetition pattern, and end date. Notes:
  • A recurring series for simulive webinars can’t be No Fixed Time recurrences. They must be daily, weekly, or monthly recurrences.
  • Hosts can set a webinar series to be either live or simulive webinars. You can’t make a single occurrence within a series to be simulive and the other occurrences live.
  • All sessions in a webinar series will use the same recording. It’s not possible to change the recording for individual occurrences.
  1. Click Schedule. The simulive pre-recorded webinar will start automatically at the time(s) selected.

Once you’ve scheduled a simulive webinar, you can edit a session at any time up until the session starts and modify any webinar options. You cannot edit a simulive webinar while it’s in progress.

Note: You cannot delete a cloud recording that is scheduled to be used or actively running in a simulive webinar. However, it is possible to delete the recording after the webinar has ended, once the lock is lifted at the end of the webinar.

Convert a scheduled live webinar to a simulive webinar

Hosts can easily convert a previously-scheduled live webinar to a simulive webinar. This allows you to set up and start registration as soon as you know you want to conduct a webinar, but don’t have the content ready yet. Once the recording is ready, you can edit a webinar session and change it from live to simulive. You can also change a simulive webinar to a live webinar at any point before the scheduled start time.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. Hover over the webinar you want to convert, then click Edit.
  4. Next to Webinar Type, choose Simulive.
  5. Follow the steps to create a simulive webinar.
Modify webinar options
Set up webinar Q&A auto-response

Before the session starts, you can set up an auto-response for Q&A, which is helpful when the host or panelists may not be present. When enabled, attendees will get an auto-response when they ask questions during the session. An example of an auto-response could be, “Thank you for your question, we will get back to you shortly.”

Note: If Q&A is enabled for the webinar, you can also manage the auto-response during the webinar.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. Click the topic of the simulive webinar.
  4. At the top, click the Q&A tab.
  5. In the Auto-Response section, click Edit, then do the following:
  6. Choose if you want to set up an auto-reply to attendees when you are not present. If enabled, attendees will get an auto response when they ask questions during the session. You can turn it off if you join the session to answer manually, or choose to leave it on and view the Q&A report later.
  7. Enter your auto-response, then click Save.
  8. (Optional) In the Settings section, click Edit, and modify other webinar Q&A settings as needed.
Set up a follow-up email to attendees with a link to the recording

You can choose to send a follow-up email to webinar attendees, which is a great way to recap the recording that was used in the simulive webinar.

To copy the recording link to use in the email template:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Recordings.
  3. Locate the same recording that you added to the simulive webinar.
  4. Click Share.
  5. Next to the Shareable Link, click Copy.
  6. (Optional) Adjust any sharing settings as needed, then click the close icon ✖.

To add the recording link to the follow-up email:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. Click the topic of the simulive webinar.
  4. At the top, click the Email Settings tab.
  5. In the Follow-up Email to Attendees section, click Edit.
  6. Modify the email settings as needed.
  7. In the text box at the bottom, paste the recording link.
  8. Click Save. When the simulive webinar ends, attendees will receive a follow-up email at the specified time with a link to the recording.
Customize additional webinar settings

Once you’ve scheduled a simulive webinar, you can customize any options as needed. Learn more about the following webinar customization options:

  • Customize webinar registration
  • Add panelists to a webinar
  • Customize webinar email settings
  • Customize webinar branding
  • Customize polls or quizzes
  • Add a post-webinar survey
  • Add webinar resources
Invite attendees to your simulive webinar

You can invite attendees to your simulive webinar the same way you would invite them to a live webinar. Learn more about inviting webinar attendees.

How to host a simulive webinar session

Simulive webinars will start automatically at the scheduled time, so hosts aren’t required to be there at the start. To control webinar host functions, join the simulive webinar as the host. During the session, you can conduct Q&A, polls, chat with attendees or other panelists, and promote attendees to panelists to help answer attendee questions.

Additionally, hosts have the option to transition a simulive webinar to a live session after the recording finishes playback. The simulive session must be set up in advance to transition to live; this decision cannot be made during the webinar itself unless it was already chosen during setup. To make the transition, a host must be present at the time of the switch.

Transition to live disabled

To host a simulive webinar without transitioning to a live session, follow these steps:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. Hover over the webinar you want to join as the host of, and click Join.
  4. Follow the on-screen prompts to join the session.
  5. The webinar will automatically end once the recording has finished playing.
Transition to live enabled

To host a simulive webinar and transition to a live session after playback ends, follow these steps:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. Hover over the webinar you want to join as the host of, and click Join.
  4. Follow the on-screen prompts to join the session.
  5. During the simulive playback, you and your panelists can join the backstage area to prepare for the live portion. You will receive visual notifications before the transition to live.
  6. Once transitioned, the webinar functions as a regular live session.
  7. (Optional) If your recording has extra content (like a long after show) that wasn’t trimmed, or if you decide not to continue with the current recording, you can start the live session early with these steps:
  8. In the top-right corner, click SIMULIVE.
  9. Click the 3 dots .
  10. Select Start live session early.
  11. Click Start now to confirm. This will end the playback early, and immediately starts the live session.

How to generate simulive webinar reports

Reporting for simulive webinars is the same as live webinar reports. Learn how to generate webinar reports.

Conducting polls in webinars

Category: Product features > Host features > Surveys and polls

How to create a poll for a webinar

Hosts can create polling questions before or during a live webinar session. During the webinar, all questions under a single poll will be asked when launched. You can create additional polls to ask questions at different times during the webinar.

Create a poll before a webinar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Webinars.
  3. Click the name of the webinar you want to add a poll to or click the Schedule a Webinar button to schedule a new webinar.
  4. If you are editing an existing webinar, scroll to the bottom of the page and click the Polls/Quizzes tab. If you are scheduling a new webinar, click Save, then scroll to the bottom of the page and click the Polls/Quizzes tab.
  5. Click + Create.
  6. Click the title Untitled Poll… to give the poll a name.
  7. Review the question types and configuration options, then select the question type for the first question.
  8. (Optional) Click + Add Question to add another question to the poll.
  9. (Optional) Click gear icon at the top right to configure the following options:
  • Require answers to be anonymous
  1. (Optional) Click the preview icon to see a preview.
  2. (Optional) Click the arrow icon next to Save at the top right to Save as draft.
  3. (Optional) Click Save to allow the quiz to be started during webinars.
Create a poll during webinar
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Start a webinar as the host.
  3. In the webinar controls, click Polls/Quizzes .
  4. Do one of the following:
  • Click Create if there are no polls created yet.
  • In the top-right corner, click the plus icon to add more polls to the existing ones.
  1. Click the title Untitled Poll… to give the poll a name.
  2. Review the question types and configuration options, then click the arrow to the right of the question title to select the question type.
  3. (Optional) Click + Add Question to add another question to the poll.
  4. (Optional) Click the ellipses at the bottom left of the creation window, then click Settings to configure the following options:
  • Require answers to be anonymous
  1. (Optional) Click the ellipses at the bottom left of the creation window, then click Preview see a preview.
  2. (Optional) Click Save to allow the poll to be started during webinars.

How to use the Surveys & Polls library

You can manage a central library of polls for webinars.

How to launch a poll in a webinar

Polls are not immediately available to webinar attendees, as the host needs to launch a poll for attendees to respond to. Hosts can create polls before or during the webinar.

During the webinar, all questions under a single poll will be asked when launched. You can create additional polls to ask questions at different times during the webinar.

  1. Start the scheduled webinar.
  2. In the webinar controls, click Polls/Quizzes .
  3. In the Polls/Quizzes window, click the name of the poll to open the details.
  4. (Optional) Click the ellipses icon to access the following options:
  • Click Edit to modify questions and answers to the poll, then click Save.
  • Click Allow panelists to vote to choose if panelists can participate in the polling.
  1. Click Launch. The attendees in the webinar will now be prompted to answer the polling questions. The host will be able to see the results live.
  2. Once you would like to stop the poll, click End Poll.
  3. Click the ellipses icon to access the following options:
  • Re-launch Poll: Launches the poll again. Note: If a poll is relaunched in a webinar, the poll report will only display the last poll occurrence. If you know you will need to launch the same poll twice and want both sets of data, consider creating a second poll with the same questions as the original to avoid relaunching.
  • Download Results: This will launch your default web browser so that you can download the entire poll report, which shows what each attendee chose, instead of the percentages of each choice.
  • View Results from Browser: Launches your default web browser and displays the same polling results on the web page.
  • Allow Panelists to vote: Click this option to change the setting, which will take effect if you re-launch the poll.
  1. Click Share Results to share the results with the attendees in the webinar, then click Stop Sharing when needed.

Using post-webinar surveys

Category: Product features > Host features > Surveys and polls

How to add a survey

To create a survey for attendees (and potentially panelists too) to take when the webinar ends:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Click Webinars.
  3. Click the name of the webinar you want to add a survey to or click the Schedule a Webinar button to schedule a new webinar. Note: If scheduling a webinar with registration or without registration, first configure the webinar’s settings, and then click Schedule before proceeding.
  4. If you are editing an existing webinar, scroll to the bottom of the page and click the Survey tab. If you are scheduling a new webinar, click Save, then scroll to the bottom of the page and click the Survey tab.
  5. Click + Add Survey, then choose from the following options:
  • Create Survey: This option takes you to the survey builder to create a new survey.
  • Choose from Library: This option allows you to choose from existing surveys in your survey library. You can manage your survey library from Survey & Poll Management.

Notes:

  • If you do not have the option to create a survey, please ensure the feature has been enabled in settings.
  • The host and other panelists may be included as recipients of the survey, depending on the choice made in web settings regarding Who can participate and if they are internal or external to the account.
  • If you would like to use a survey outside of Zoom, click + Use a 3rd party survey.

How to create a survey

You can use different question formats to get feedback on what’s most important to you.

Select the question format that you want after creating a new survey from the Survey tab or the survey library.

  1. Click the title Untitled Survey… to give the survey a name.
  2. Review the question types and configuration options, then select the question type for the first question.
  3. (Optional) Click + Add Question to add another question to the survey.
  4. (Optional) Click gear icon at the top right to configure the following options:
  • Require answers to be anonymous
  • Numbered questions
  • Show question type
  • Feedback after submission
  1. (Optional) Click the color palette icon to customize the survey’s colors.
  2. (Optional) Click the preview icon to see a preview.
  3. (Optional) Click the ellipses icon at the top right to Save as draft.
  4. (Optional) Click Save to allow the survey to be sent after webinars.

How to use survey options

To control how attendees and panelists receive the survey when the webinar ends:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Click the Webinars tab.
  3. Click the name of the webinar you want to edit the survey settings for.
  4. Click the Survey tab.
  5. Next to Survey Options, click Edit.
  6. (Optional) Select Show in the browser when the webinar ends.
  7. Select Show the link on the follow-up email. Note: To ensure a follow-up email is sent, click the Email Settings tab of the webinar settings and enable the follow-up email to Attendees option. Learn more about modifying email settings for a specific webinar.
  8. Click Save.

To preview how the survey will look to attendees and panelists, click Preview on the right side of the page.

How to change the assigned survey

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Click the Webinars tab.
  3. Click the name of the webinar you want to edit the survey settings for.
  4. Click the Survey tab.
  5. Click Change on the right side of the page, select a different survey, then click Confirm.

How to delete a survey

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Click the Webinars tab.
  3. Click the name of the webinar you want to edit the survey settings for.
  4. Click the Survey tab.
  5. Click Remove on the right side of the page, then click Remove to confirm.

How to use a 3rd-party survey

Notes:

  • The survey you want to use must be prepared on the 3rd-party service prior to linking for post-webinar use.
  • Ensure that the Allow host to use a 3rd-party survey link option is enabled at the account level.
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Click the Webinars tab.
  3. Click the name of the webinar you want to edit the survey settings for.
  4. Click the Survey tab.
  5. Click Use a 3rd party survey.
  6. Enter the link to the survey you want to use.
  7. Click Save.

Note: Any valid link will work; links do not have to redirect to a 3rd-party survey to work.

Similar to a post-attendee URL, you can use the link to redirect the attendees and panelists to:

  • Watch a video of a working prototype
  • Your company’s website
  • An order form

How to view survey results

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Click Surveys & Polls.
  3. Locate the row of the survey you want to view results for the, then click the report icon on the right.

How to download a report on your survey

Note: You must have account owner/admin privileges or be a user with access to usage reports to view and download reports.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation panel, click Account Management then Reports.
  3. Click the Usage Reports tab.
  4. Click Webinar.
  5. In Select Report Type, select Survey Report.
  6. Narrow the webinar search field by:
  • Filtering the search dates
  • Searching for a specific webinar ID
  1. Click the circle to the left of the webinar you want to select.
  2. Click Generate CSV Report.

Chatting in Zoom webinars

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in webinars

How to enable or disable webinar chat from your personal settings

Beforescheduling a webinar, as a host, you can choose whether attendees can send chat messages during your webinar by enabling or disabling chat in the webinar settings.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Settings.
  3. Click the Webinar tab.
  4. Under In Webinar, click the Chat toggle to enable or disable it. If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change. Notes:
  • If you disable Webinar chat or Allow users to save chats from the webinar is OFF, the Webinar chat - Auto-save feature will also be disabled.
  • If the option is grayed out, it has been locked at either the group, account level, or user level. You need to contact your Zoom admin.
  1. Select one of the following for Panelists can chat with:
  • Everyone: Allow the panelists to chat with everyone.
  • Hosts and all panelists: Allow panelists to chat only with the host and other panelists, not with attendees.
  1. Select one of the following for Attendees can chat with:
  • Everyone: Allow attendees to chat with everyone.
  • Hosts and all panelists: Allow attendees to chat with just the host and panelists.
  • No one: Prevent attendees from chatting with anyone.
  1. Select Allow panelists to send direct messages to other panelists, to allow panelists to chat with each other only.
  2. Select one of the following under Allow users to copy and save chats from the webinar:
  • Host and co-hosts: Allow participants to save the chat communication between hosts and co-hosts on their computers.
  • Host and all panelists: Allow participants to save the hosts’ and panelists’ chat communication on their computers.
  • Everyone: Allow participants to save everyone chat communication on their computers.
  • Only users in your account: Allow participants who belong to your account to save their chat communication on their computers.
  1. Select Only users in your account can chat: Allow only users from the account to use webinar chat. This applies regardless of whether the webinar is hosted by a regulated user’s organization or an external organization.
  2. Click Save. Note: To automatically save messages during a webinar, you can review the meeting and webinar auto-saving chats article.

How to chat in Zoom webinars

Webinar chat permissions depend on your role in a webinar and what the host’s settings are:

  • Webinar hosts, co-hosts, and panelists can send messages to each other, to a specific host or panelist, or to everyone in the webinar if enabled by the host.

  • Webinar attendees can send messages to hosts, panelists, and everyone in the webinar if enabled by the host. If the host disables webinar chat for attendees, attendees can’t send messages but can still view messages from the host and panelists. Note: Attendees can’t send private messages to other webinar attendees. Learn more about attendee controls in a webinar.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux

  • Android | iOS

  • Web client

  1. Start or join a webinar.
  2. In the webinar controls toolbar, click Chat . If you’re in full screen mode, the Webinar chat window will appear as a movable and adjustable window. If not, it will appear on the right side of your screen.
  3. In the bottom-left corner of the Webinar chat window, next to the To: section, click the drop-down icon to choose the message recipient.
  4. In the Type your message here… field, enter the message you want to send.
  5. (Optional) If enabled by the host, use the following options according to your needs:
  • File : Click to send a file in the webinar chat.
  • Emoji : Click to add emojis to your message.
  • Note: Alternatively, enter a colon followed by at least 2 characters to find matching emojis. For example, typing :jo will provide:
  • :joy:
  • :joy_cat:
  • :joystick:

  1. Press Enter on your keyboard to send your message.

  2. Start or join a webinar.

  3. At the bottom of your screen, tap Chat . The Webinar chat screen will open.

  4. In the bottom-left corner of the Webinar chat screen, next to the Send to: section, tap the drop-down icon to choose the message recipient.

  5. In the Tap here to chat field, enter the message you want to send.

  6. (Optional) If enabled by the host, tap Emoji to open the emoji panel and add emojis to your message. Note: Alternatively, enter a colon followed by at least 2 characters to find matching emojis. For example, typing :jo will provide:

  • :joy:
  • :joy_cat:
  • :joystick:

  1. Tap the send icon .

  2. Start or join a webinar.

  3. In the webinar controls toolbar, click Chat . If you’re in full screen mode, the Webinar Chat window will appear on the right side of your screen. If not, it will open in a movable and adjustable window.

  4. In the bottom-left corner of the Webinar Chat window, next to the to: section, click the text with blue background to choose the message recipient.

  5. In the Type your message here… field, enter the message you want to send.

How to manage chat during a webinar

During a webinar, hosts can change webinar chat options to control who panelists can chat with, who attendees can chat with, and save in-webinar chat messages as a text file.

    1. Start a webinar.
  2. In the webinar controls toolbar, click Chat . The Webinar chat window will appear.
  3. In the bottom-right corner of the Webinar chat window, click the more icon . A small window will appear, giving you control over these settings:
  • Save chat: Click to save in-webinar chat messages as a text file and store them in the same location as your computer recordings.
  • Panelists can chat with:
  • Host and panelists: Panelists can only chat with each other and the host, not with attendees.
  • Everyone: Panelists can chat with everyone in the webinar, including attendees.
  • Attendees can chat with:
  • No one: Attendees can’t chat with anyone.
  • Host and panelists: Attendees can only chat with hosts and panelists.
  • Everyone: Attendees can chat with everyone in the webinar, including other attendees.

Joining and participating in Zoom Webinars

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in webinars

How to join a webinar

Join a webinar through an invitation link

To join the webinar, find the link that the host provided or that you received in the confirmation page after you registered. If the host sent a registration confirmation email, the link can also be found there. Once you have the link, choose from any of these options:

  • Click the link.
  • Copy the link, then paste it in your web browser.
Manually join a webinar
  1. Locate the meeting ID/webinar ID from your registration email. It may appear at the end of the phone dial-in information, or it will be in the join link, just after *https://zoom.us/w/*
  2. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app or mobile app. Note: You do not need to be signed in to the Zoom client, but if not, you will need to provide a name and email address to join. If registration is required, you will need to complete registration and use the link to join the webinar.
  3. Click or tap Join.
  4. Enter the webinar ID, and click or tap Join.
  5. If prompted, enter your name and email address, then click or tap Join.

Note: If joining a simulive webinar, the webinar will automatically open in a desktop browser. Supported browsers include Chrome, Safari, and Chromium Edge.

Wait for the host to start the webinar

If the host hasn’t started broadcasting the webinar or is preparing using a practice session, you’ll receive one of the following messages depending on your device type: Please wait for the host to start this webinar or Waiting for the host to start the webinar.

If you receive a message showing the date and time of the webinar, check the date and start time of the webinar including the time zone. Make sure to join when the webinar starts.

How to use webinar attendee controls

  • Windows | macOS
  • Linux
  • Android
  • iOS

Audio Settings (only visible if the host hasn’t granted you permission to talk): Change your audio settings. You can also click the upward arrow (^) next to change your speaker.

Unmute / Mute : If the host gives you permission, you can unmute and talk during the webinar. All participants will be able to hear you. If the host allows you to talk, you will receive a notification about staying on mute or unmuting. Note: You can still access the audio settings by click on the ^ arrow next to the Unmute/Mute button.

Chat : Open webinar chat, allowing you to send chat messages to the host, panelists, and attendees (if permitted).

Raise Hand : Raise your hand in the webinar to indicate that you need something from the host. The host may instruct you on how they plan to use this. Many webinar hosts use this feature to know if an attendee has a question and would like to speak out loud.

Q&A : Open the Question and answer window, allowing you to ask questions to the host and panelists. They can either reply back to you via text in the Q&A window or answer your question live.

To ask a question:

  1. Enter your question into the Q&A box, then click Send. Notes:
  • Select Send Anonymously if you do not want your name attached to your question in the Q&A.
  • If you see a prompt that your message has triggered a Chat Etiquette policy, you are either warned or blocked from sending the message based on what your account admin has configured. The Chat Etiquette Tool does not send additional message information, like data, metadata, and event information, to the account admin, to Zoom, or to any 3rd party services, whether the message triggers Chat Etiquette policies or not.
  1. If the host replies via the Q&A, you will see a reply in the Q&A window. The host can also answer your question live (out loud). You will see a notification in the Q&A window if the host plans to do this.

As an attendee you can also like or comment on other attendee’s questions. This helps the host or participant identify popular questions, especially in a webinar with many attendees.

  1. Click the thumbs up icon to like a comment. Tip: The number beside the icon is the total number of likes the question has received so far.
  2. Click the red thumbs up icon to unlike the comment.
  3. Click Comment to write a reply to an existing question.
  4. Enter your comment and click Send. Your comment will appear beneath the question.

Transcript: Open the Transcript window, allowing you to search and save transcripts.

Show captions / Hide captions : Click to show or hide captions. You can also access the caption and translation settings by click on the ^ arrow next to the Show captions / Hide captions button.

Leave meeting: Click Leave meeting to leave the webinar at any time. If you leave, you can rejoin if the webinar is still in progress, as long as the host has not locked the webinar.

Polls and Quizzes: Polls and quizzes may be launched by the host or presenters, which will appear on your screen. These are an optional way to interact with the host, presenters, and their presentation.

For users on multiple screens, the location of the window will vary slightly.

  • On Windows devices, the polls and quiz windows will appear on the initial screen the webinar was located when the poll was launched. So, if the Zoom Webinar window was on screen 1 when the host launched the poll, then all poll windows will appear on screen 1, unless the attendee moves the poll window to a different location, which becomes the new default location.
  • On macOS devices, the poll will appear on the active screen, regardless of the location of the Zoom Webinar window.

Participating in webinar breakout rooms

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in webinars

How to join a breakout room

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  1. Join a Zoom Webinar. The host will need to invite you to join the breakout room.
  2. Click Join.
  3. (Optional) Click Not Now to not immediately join a breakout room. You can join by clicking Breakout Rooms in your webinar controls, then clicking Join a Breakout Room.
  4. Confirm joining the breakout room by clicking Join.

Upon joining the webinar breakout room, participants will have the same audio, video, and screen share capabilities as they would typically have in a Zoom Meeting.

Upon returning to the main webinar session, they will return to the standard view- and listen-only webinar attendee role.

  1. Join a Zoom Webinar. The host will need to invite you to join the breakout room.
  2. Tap Join.
  3. (Optional) Tap Not Now to not immediately join a breakout room. You can join the breakout room by tapping Join Breakout Room in the top left corner.
  4. Confirm joining the breakout room by clicking Join.

Upon joining the webinar breakout room, participants will have the same audio, video, and screen share capabilities as they would typically have in a Zoom Meeting.

Upon returning to the main webinar session, they will return to the standard view- and listen-only webinar attendee role.

How to self-select a breakout room

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS

If the host has allowed participants to self-select and join breakout rooms of their choosing, participants will be able to view and select from a list of breakout rooms the host has created. They will be able to enter and leave breakout rooms freely.

Note: Participants not joined with the desktop or mobile app will not be able to self-select a breakout room, and as such, the host will need to facilitate moving these participants manually.

  1. In the webinar controls, click Breakout Rooms .
  2. Click Choose Room to Join. This will display the list of open breakout rooms created by the host.
  3. Hover your cursor over the number to the right of the breakout room you wish to join, click Join, then confirm by clicking Join.
  4. Repeat as necessary to join other breakout rooms, or click Leave Room to return to the main session.

If the host has allowed participants to self-select and join breakout rooms of their choosing, participants will be able to view and select from a list of breakout rooms the host has created. They will be able to enter and leave breakout rooms freely.

Note: Participants not joined with the desktop or mobile app will not be able to self-select a breakout room, and as such, the host will need to facilitate moving these participants manually.

  1. In the top-left corner of the webinar window, tap Join Breakout Room .
  2. You may be prompted to confirm joining breakout rooms. If so, tap Choose Room. This will display the list of open breakout rooms created by the host.
  3. Tap the Breakout Room you wish to participant in and then tap Join.
  4. Repeat as necessary to join other breakout rooms, or click Leave Room to return to the main session.

How to leave the breakout room

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS

If allowed by the host, you can leave the breakout room and return to the main webinar session, or you can leave the webinar entirely from the breakout room.

  1. Click Leave.
  2. Choose if you want to leave the breakout room or the entire webinar.
  3. Alternatively, when the host ends the breakout rooms, you will be notified and given the option to return to the main room immediately, or after a brief period set by the host.

If allowed by the host, you can leave the breakout room and return to the main webinar session, or you can leave the webinar entirely from the breakout room.

  1. Tap Leave.
  2. Choose Leave Breakout Room.
  3. Alternatively, when the host ends the breakout rooms, you will be notified and given the option to return to the main room immediately, or after a brief period set by the host.

How to participate by telephone

When joining a webinar by telephone audio only, you do not need to do anything to join. Once the host assigns you to a breakout room and starts the breakout rooms, you will hear an audio notification that you have been added to a breakout room.

Note: Currently, this audio prompt for dial-in attendees only supports English.

Participate in the breakout room

You will be able to mute and unmute like you can in the main session. Use *6 to mute or unmute.

Return to the main room

When the host has ended the breakout rooms, you will hear an audio notification that you will be returning to the main room in 60 seconds. Press # to join the main room immediately.

Type Feature title Description Platforms
New or enhanced feature Multiple subscription license assignment for webinar hosts Account owners and admins can assign Zoom Webinars host licenses from any of the available subscriptions within the account. When an account holds more than one subscription, admins can select which subscription’s license to assign to a webinars host and what the license’s start and end dates would be. The unique license identifier reflects both the license type and its associated subscription. Switching licenses between subscriptions does not affect the core webinar experience for hosts or attendees. Web portal
Host features
New or enhanced feature Reorder webinar resources in web portal Webinar hosts can customize the display order of their webinar resources through the Zoom web portal. Hosts can manually rearrange resource links, documents, and speakers to display in their preferred order rather than the default chronological sequence based on when items were added Web portal
New or enhanced feature Customized start times for simulive webinars Hosts can configure simulive sessions to start up to 15 minutes early using the renamed “Customized Start” setting, which replaces the previous “Delay Start” functionality. The feature maintains all existing delayed start capabilities while adding early start options. Sessions can automatically begin broadcasting at the configured time, with attendee communications continuing to display the original scheduled event time. Web portal
Webinar features
New or enhanced feature Zoom Webinars cancellation experience update When an Online account host cancels a Zoom Webinars license, the product displays in-product messages at each stage of the cancellation lifecycle. During pending cancellation, hosts retain full paid access and are prompted to reactivate before their billing cycle ends. After cancellation, a 30-day grace period restricts access to previously generated webinar assets—recordings, whiteboards, reports, and summaries are grayed out with hover-state disclaimers explaining the restriction and customer support retrieval options. Repurchasing the license within the grace period can restore access to existing assets, but purchasing the license after those 30 days do not recover deleted data. Web portal
New or enhanced feature Pause subscription option for standalone Zoom Webinars licenses Pausing a subscription becomes an available option to Online users on monthly recurring standalone single Zoom Webinars licenses as an alternative to cancellation, with the pause taking effect at the end of the billing cycle. While paused, hosts can’t view webinars, can’t perform any webinar actions such as creating, starting, editing, or uploading, and attendees are blocked from joining via existing registration links. Assets generated from previous webinars, including recordings, whiteboards, and summaries, remain viewable but can’t be shared, downloaded, or edited; reports are accessible for both viewing and downloading. The Zoom Webinars interface displays a pause status indicator with a hyperlink that directs users to billing management to manually resume their subscription. This option is not applicable to annual or one-month plans. Web portal

Changed feature Enhancements to webinar scheduler 1080p video option visibility The 1080p video setting is an available option that allows organizers to enable high-definition video on a per-webinar basis. This change aligns the 1080p video setting with the existing scheduling logic used for other webinar features. If the setting is off and unlocked, it will be visible on the webinar scheduling page, allowing the webinar host to enable it for their webinar. The enhancement provides customers with full access to the premium video quality features they are paying for through their Webinars Plus and Zoom Events subscriptions. Web portal

New or enhanced feature Production Studio Video Scenes automatically start webinars when video begins Event producers and hosts can enable a setting in Production Studio’s Video Scene configuration to automatically start the live broadcast when pressing Play on pre-recorded video content within a video scene. This setting eliminates the manual two-step process of starting the broadcast and playing the video separately. When enabled, the Start Broadcast button remains disabled until the host clicks Play on the configured video scene in the Program / Live section. Production Studio provides a clear visual indicator near the Play button to warn hosts that this action will also start the live broadcast. This feature ensures seamless, synchronized transitions for professional-grade events. Web portal

Admin features
New or enhanced feature Production Studio toggle for webinar setup Account owners and admins can enable or disable Production Studio for webinars through a toggle switch in event setup. When disabled, the feature allows integration with third-party production tools while still broadcasting through Zoom Webinars. Previously, Production Studio was automatically enabled when one or more scenes were created. This toggle provides webinar producers with the flexibility to use their preferred professional production applications. This feature must be enabled by Zoom. Web portal
Events features
New or enhanced feature Production Studio Gallery Scene automatically hides panelists with cameras off Production Studio Gallery Scenes automatically display only participants with active video feeds, creating professional broadcast compositions for live events. Event Producers don’t need to manually manage layouts or compromise on visual quality when panelists turn their cameras on or off during broadcasts. The filtering functionality updates scene compositions in real-time, ensuring that only video-enabled participants appear in the produced output. This new standard behavior applies automatically to all Gallery Scenes without requiring configuration settings or toggles. Web portal
General features
New or enhanced feature Reduced stream key expiration time for webinars Stream keys for RTMPS expire 4 hours after the scheduled end time of webinars, replacing the previous 4-day expiration period. When a webinar ends before its scheduled end time, the stream key will still expire 4 hours after the originally scheduled end time. If a webinar runs longer than scheduled, the expiration time automatically resets to 4 hours after the actual end time. This enhancement provides improved security by significantly reducing the window of potential unauthorized access to streaming credentials. Web portal
Host features
New or enhanced feature Real-Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP) datacenter location visibility Hosts can view the specific datacenter locations for their primary and secondary RTMP streams in the metrics panel. This information shows which Zoom datacenter locations the stream connects to when establishing the media stream connection. The feature provides visibility into both primary and backup stream routing to help hosts understand their stream’s geographic distribution. This transparency allows hosts to better evaluate their streaming redundancy and connection paths. Web portal
New or enhanced feature Enhancements to webinar templates with alternative host support Hosts can add alternative hosts to webinar templates and have them automatically applied when scheduling new webinars. Alternative hosts that are configured in the original webinar will be saved as part of the template. When users apply the template to create a new webinar, the alternative hosts will be automatically populated, eliminating the need to remember to add them manually. This feature streamlines the webinar scheduling process by preserving all host configurations within templates.Note: This feature is scheduled for release shortly after October 20 and may not be available at this time. Web portal
New or enhanced feature Enhancements to webinar host emails with calendar files Hosts and alternative hosts receive ICS calendar files in their webinar email notifications. Previously, ICS files were only included in attendee webinar emails but were missing from host and alternative host communications. When hosts and alternative hosts receive webinar emails, the messages will include ICS calendar files that can be imported into their calendar applications. Web portal
New or enhanced feature Automated poll scheduling for simulive webinars Event organizers can schedule polls to automatically appear at specific times during simulive webinars. They can set the exact timing for when polls are pushed to attendees, specify when polls disappear, and schedule when poll results are shared after the poll ends. Web portal
User features
New or enhanced feature Enhancements to webinar start time messaging Users viewing webinar details will see unified and grammatically correct text strings for webinar start times. The system displays consistent date and time formatting whether users are viewing regular webinars or simulive webinars. Same-day webinars show only the start time, while webinars scheduled for future dates include the day and date information. The updated verbiage clearly distinguishes simulive webinars while maintaining formatting consistency. This improvement provides users with clearer, more professional webinar scheduling information. Web portal
New or enhanced feature Enhancements to webinar email unsubscribe experience Users can unsubscribe from webinar emails through an improved experience that removes personal details from email footers and provides clearer context. When users click the unsubscribe link in webinar emails, they are directed to a dedicated page that explains which account they are receiving emails from and allows them to unsubscribe from that specific account’s webinar communications. Users also have the option to globally unsubscribe from all Zoom webinar emails, with clear explanations of what this action includes. Confirmation emails are sent after successful unsubscription, and users can easily resubscribe if needed. Web portal
