  3. In the left navigation of the media menu, select an option:
  • AI images : Generate an image using AI using prompts. You can also select a specific Model, Style, and Image Ratio when generating the image. Note: Using this feature will use AI Credits. Learn more aboutusing Zoom AI credits.
  • Images : Select an image available from Pexels.
  • Icons : Select an icon from either Remix Icon or Lucide.
Upload an image to a slide
  1. Create or open a presentation.
  2. In the top toolbar, click the Media icon .
  3. In the bottom left corner of the media menu, click Upload.
  4. Select the desired image from your computer.

How to manage an image added to a slide

  1. Within a slide, click on the desired image.
  2. The Media toolbar will appear with the following options:
  • AI : Use AI to edit the image. Note: Using this feature will use AI Credits. Learn more aboutusing Zoom AI credits.
  • Crop : Crop an image to the desired dimensions.
  • Crop to shape: Crop the image to a desired shape. Note: Click Remove Crop to reverse the cropping.
  • Add a comment : Add a comment to the image.
  • More : Will open the Design tool with additional image options.
Manage an image with the Design tool

To manage an image using the Design tool:

  1. Within a slide, click on the image.
  2. In the toolbar, click Format options.
  3. The following options will be available:
  • Size & Position: Adjust the size and position of the image within the slide, including the alignment within the slide.
  • Border: Select the border style, including Theme colors, as well as the Border Style and Border Weight. In addition, click the More icon to modify the Join type.
  • Shadow: Select the shadow effect for the image. In addition, you can modify the shadow effect’s Color, Distance, Blur, and Angle.
  • Crop to shape: Crop the image to a desired shape. Note: Click Remove Crop to reverse the cropping.
  • Radius: Select the radius of the image. Note: The maximum radius is 286 degrees.

Adding tables in Zoom Slides

Category: Product features > User features

How to add a table to a slide

  1. Create or open a presentation.
  2. In the top toolbar, click the Table icon .
  3. Select the number of desired rows and columns. A new table will be added to the list.
  4. Click within a cell to add or remove content to it.

How to manage a table

  1. Within a slide, click on the desired table.
  2. The table toolbar will appear with the following options:
  • Text size: Select the size of the text within all cells in the table.
  • Text color : Select the color of the text within all cells in the table.
  • Align : Select the alignment for text within all cells in the table.
  • Add a comment : Add a comment to the table.
  • More : Will open the Design tool with additional table options.
Manage a table with the Design tool

To manage a table using the Design tool:

  1. Within a slide, click on the desired table.
  2. In the toolbar, click the More icon . Alternatively, to the right of the slide, click the Design tool.
  3. The following options will be available:
  • Size & Position: Adjust the size and position of the table within the slide, including the alignment within the slide.
  • Columns: Set the number of columns within the table.
  • Rows: Set the number of rows within the table.
  • Fill: Select the fill color for the table. In addition to selecting colors, users can also have the ability to use gradients, upload images, or use a custom pattern.
  • Border: Select the border style, including Theme colors, as well as the Border Style and Border Weight.
  • Table highlight: Select rows and/or columns that will be highlighted in the table.
  • Font: Select the font type, font style, font size, line and letter spacing, and alignment. Note: Click the More icon to access additional formatting settings.
  • Text color: Select the text color. In addition to selecting colors, users can also have the ability to use gradients, upload images, or use a custom pattern.
  • Text outline: Select the text style, including Theme colors, as well as the Border Style, Border Weight, and Join Type.

How to manage a cell

  1. Within a slide, click on the desired cell.
  2. The table toolbar will appear with the following options:
  • Text size: Select the size of the text within the cell.
  • Text color : Select the color of the text within the cell.
  • Align : Select the alignment for text within the cell.
  • Fill : Select the fill color for the cell. In addition to selecting colors, users can also have the ability to use gradients, upload images, or use a custom pattern.
  • More : Will open the Design tool with additional table options.
Manage a cell with the Design tool

To manage a table using the Design tool:

  1. Within a slide, click on the desired table.
  2. In the toolbar, click the More icon . Alternatively, to the right of the slide, click the Design.
  3. The following options will be available:
  • Size & Position: Adjust the size and position of the cell within the table, including alignment.
  • Fill: Select the fill color for the cell. In addition to selecting colors, users can also have the ability to use gradients, upload images, or use a custom pattern.
  • Border: Select the border style, including Theme colors, as well as the Border Style and Border Weight.
  • Font: Select the font type, font style, font size, line and letter spacing, and alignment. Note: Click the More icon to access additional formatting settings.
  • Text color: Select the text color. In addition to selecting colors, users can also have the ability to use gradients, upload images, or use a custom pattern.
  • Text outline: Select the text style, including Theme colors, as well as the Border Style, Border Weight, and Join Type.

Presenting a slide show with Zoom Slides

Category: Product features > User features

How to present a slide show
  1. Open a presentation.
  2. In the top right corner, click the Present icon .
  3. Select how you want to share the presentation:
  • Present now: Opens the slide deck within the window for presentation.
  • Present with speaker view: Opens the slide deck in the window and a secondary window with slide controls and speaker notes.
  • Share with AI narration: Presents the slide within the window, with generated audio of the speaker notes. Note: Click Copy link to create a link to the narrated presentation for sharing.
How to use slide controls during a presentation
Slide controls available in Present now
  1. Open a presentation.
  2. In the top right corner, click the Present icon .
  3. Click Present now. The following controls will be available during the presentation:
  • Next / Previous : Allows the navigation between slides. Note: Clicking the slide number also allows you to type the desired slide number to go directly to it.
  • Presenter view: Switch the presentation style to Present with speaker view.
  • Fullscreen : Expand the presentation window to full-screen mode.
  • Laser pointer : Allows the use of a laser pointer during the presentation. Note: To select a different laser color, hover over the icon to open the Laser color menu.
  • More :
  • Restart from first slide: Restarts the presentation from the first slide.
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Displays thelinkkeyboard shortcuts for managing a presentation.
  • In the top right corner, click Stop presentation to close the presentation.
Slide controls available in Present with speaker view
  1. Open a presentation
  2. In the top right corner, click the Present icon .
  3. Click Present with speaker view. The current slide will be displayed on the left with the upcoming slide on the right. In addition, the speaker notes will be displayed at the bottom of the window. The following controls will be available during the presentation:
  • Next / Previous : Allows the navigation between slides. Note: Clicking the slide number also allows you to type the desired slide number to go directly to it.
  • Laser pointer : Allows the use of a laser pointer during the presentation. Note: To select a different laser color, hover over the icon to open the Laser color menu.
  • More :
  • Restart from first slide: Restarts the presentation from the first slide.
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Displays the keyboard shortcuts for managing a presentation.
  • In the top right corner, click Stop presentation to close the presentation.

In addition to the presentation controls, in the left navigation of the presentation window, you can select a specific slide to move to.

In the speaker notes, click the Decrease font size (-) or Increase font size (+) buttons to change the size of the speaker note text.

Slide controls available in Share with AI narration
  1. Open a presentation
  2. In the top right corner, click the Present icon .
  3. Click Share with AI narration. The presentation slide will be displayed, and AI will start generating a voice-over for the speaker notes. Once complete, the narration will start playing for the first slide. The following controls will be available during the presentation:
  • Play/Pause: Start or stop the narration.
  • Voice over: Select the voice-over voice and language.
  • Volume : Adjust the volume of the voice-over.
  • Next / Previous : Allows the navigation between slides. Note: Clicking the slide number also allows you to type the desired slide number to go directly to it.
  • Turn off captions / Turn on captions : Disables or enables closed captions for the narration.
  • Enter fullscreen / Exit fullscreen: Enter or exit full-screen mode.
  • More :
  • Restart from first slide : Restarts the presentation from the first slide.
  • Keyboard shortcuts : Displays the keyboard shortcuts for managing a presentation.
  • Copy link : Copy the link to the presentation.

Using Zoom Slides

Category: Product features > User features

How to create a presentation

Follow the steps below to create a presentation using the web portal or desktop app. You can alsouse AI to create presentations.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Web

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.

  2. Click the Slides** tab. Note: If you do not see the Slides** tab, click the More tab, then click Slides.

  3. Click Blank. A new blank presentation will open.

  4. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.

  5. In the top-right corner, click the Zoom Products icon .

  6. In the Zoom Products menu, click Slides. Slides will open in a new browser tab.

  7. Click Blank. A new blank presentation will open.

How to edit a slide in Zoom Slides

Add a text box

You can add and customize text boxes within your presentation slides to enhance content organization and visual appeal. Learn more about using text boxes within your slides.

Add an image

You can add and customize images within your presentation slides to enhance visual appeal and support your content. Learn more aboutusing images within your slides.

Add a chart

You can add and customize charts within your presentation slides to visualize data and enhance understanding. Learn more about using charts within your slides.

Add a table

You can add and customize tables within your presentation slides to organize data and present information in a structured format. Learn more aboutusing tables within your slides.

Manage elements within a slide

When multiple elements overlap on a slide, you can adjust their stacking order to control which elements appear in front of or behind others. To adjust the order of elements on a slide:

  1. Open a presentation.
  2. Right-click on the desired element.
  3. Click Order and then select the desired action:
  • Bring to front: Moves text box, image, shape, chart, or table to the front of the slide.
  • Bring forward: Moves the text box, image, shape, chart, or table one layer forward in the stacking order.
  • Send backward: Moves the text box, image, shape, chart, or table one layer backward in the stacking order.
  • Send to back: Moves the text box, image, shape, chart, or table to the back of the slide.

How to manage slides in Zoom Slides

Add a slide
  1. Create or open a presentation.
  2. In the navigator, click the New slide button [+].
  3. Click the desired slide type from either the Templates tab or the Layouts tab.
  4. A new slide will be added to the presentation.

Alternatively, you can right-click on a slide and click + New Slide or use the hot keys (Ctrl+M or ^M) to create a new slide.

Duplicate a slide
  1. Open a presentation.
  2. In the navigator, right-click on the desired slide and click Duplicate .
  3. A copy of the slide will be created.

Alternatively, you can use hot keys (Ctrl + D or ⌘ D) to duplicate the slide.

Delete a slide
  1. Open a presentation.
  2. In the navigator, right-click on the desired slide and click the Delete .
  3. The slide will be deleted.

Alternatively, you can use hot keys (Delete / Backspace) to delete a slide.

Hide a slide
  1. Open a presentation.
  2. In the navigator, right-click on the desired slide and click the Skip .
  3. The slide will be hidden in the slide navigator and will not be displayed during a presentation.
Rearrange slides
  1. Open a presentation.
  2. In the navigator, click and hold the desired slide, then drag the slide to the desired position.

In addition to dragging slides, you can Cut/Copy, and Paste slides in your desired order.

Add a transition to a slide
  1. Open a presentation.
  2. In the left navigation, select the desired slide.
  3. In the right toolbar, click the Transition icon.
  4. Select the desired transition:
  • Fade: Smoothly transitions between slides by gradually fading out the current slide while fading in the next one.
  • Push: Slides the current slide off the screen while pushing the next slide into view from the side.
  • Split: Divides the current slide and reveals the next slide by splitting from the center outward or edges inward.
  • Random bar: Transitions between slides using randomly appearing vertical or horizontal bars that reveal the next slide.
  • None: Instantly switches to the next slide without any transition effect.
  1. (Optional) Click Apply to all slides to apply the transition to all slides within a presentation.

How to add speaker notes

To add speaker notes to a presentation:

  1. Open a presentation.
  2. At the bottom of the slide window, in the Speaker notes text box, enter desired text.
  3. (Optional) Click Generate to have AI generate speaker notes based on the slide(s).

How to present slides in Zoom Slides

Zoom Slides offers presentation modes to suit your needs, with multiple different presentation modes, including AI-based voice-over presentations. Learn more aboutpresenting slides with Zoom Slides.

How to share a presentation in Zoom Slides

Once you create your presentation, you can easily share it with others, enabling collaboration. Sharing the presentation allows collaborators to edit and comment on slides within the presentation. Learn more about Zoom Slides user permission types.

To share a presentation:

  1. Open your presentation.
  2. On the top right of your presentation, click Share.
  3. In the Share window, the following options will be available:
  • In the search box, enter the contact(s), channel(s), or email address(es) you desire to share the presentation with, then select one of the following permission levels:
  • Note: When using this method to share a presentation, by default, your contact will be notified via email and will be granted the Commenter permission level.
  • Co-owner: Allow your contact to have the same permissions as the original owner, including sharing, editing, commenting, and deleting.
  • Editor: Allow your contact to make changes to the presentation and comment as necessary.
  • Commenter: Allow your contact to comment only on your presentation.
  • Viewer: Allow your contact to view only your presentation.
  • (Optional) Select Notify in chat if you have this feature and would like to notify your contact via chat. Enter a message, then click Send.
  • Your user(s) will receive a notification in Team Chat.
  • Under General Access, select one of the following:
  • Only you can access: This is selected by default, giving you only the ability to work on the presentation.
  • Collaborators only:Add collaborators, and the default link access will be updated to allow collaborators access to the presentation.
  • Anyone in [Name of your organization]: Allow anyone in your organization’s Zoom account to search for the presentation and access it by link.
  • Anyone with link: Allow anyone with the link to view the content. However, to comment or edit, users need to be signed in to their Zoom account or app.
  • Note: This feature can only be enabled by your account admin. Contact your admin if this option is greyed out and you cannot select it.
  • Click one of the social media buttons to share the presentation to that social media platform.
  • Note: When using the social media buttons, the presentation’s access level will be set to Anyone with a link, and the platform will be redirected with a reference to the presentation link.
  • Click Copy Link to manually share the link of the presentation with others.

You can also share a presentation directly from Zoom Hub. Learn more about how to manage assets in Hub.

How to comment in Zoom Slides

  1. Open a presentation.
  2. Click on an element in your slide, then click the Comment icon .
  3. Alternatively, right-click on the slide and click Comment or use the hot keys (Ctrl+Shift+M or ⌘+Shift+M).
  4. In the Comment box, enter a comment, then click the Send icon .
  5. (Optional) At the bottom left of the comment box, click one of the following icons:
  • Tag icon : Tag a specific user(s) to your comment.
  • Note: You can tag a user that you didn’t share the presentation with, and the presentation will automatically be shared with them.
  • Emoji icon : Add an emoji to your comment.
  • Attach icon : Attach a file from your computer to your comment.
View and reply to comments in Zoom Slides
  1. Open your presentation.
  2. On the top right of the presentation, click the Comment icon .
  3. or Unread to show new comments on your presentation.
  4. Click on your comment.
  5. In the Reply box, enter your reply.
  6. Click the Send icon .
  7. (Optional) Click the More icon , then click Copy link, to manually send a link of your comment to others.
Resolve or delete comments in Zoom Slides
  1. Open your presentation.
  2. On the top right of the Zoom Slides, click the Comment icon or on the right, click the comment with number icon.
  3. Click on your comment, then on the right of the window, click one of the following:
  • Resolve icon : To resolve the comment(s).
  • More icon : Select Delete thread to delete the comment(s).

Using Zoom Slides during a meeting

Category: Product features > User features

How to share a presentation during a meeting

  1. Start orjoin your Zoom Meeting.
  2. In the meeting control, click Hub. Note: If you don’t see that option, click More, then Hub.
  3. Click Slides.
  4. Search for the desired presentation.
  5. Hover over the presentation, and click Share in meeting.
  6. Next Meeting participants’ access to this presentation, select the desired permission level for the participants:
  • Can edit: Allows participants to edit and comment.
  • Can comment: Allows participants to comment.
  • Can view: Participants can only view.
  1. (Optional) Select the Keep signed-in meeting participants’ access to the presentation after the meeting ends checkbox to allow participants to retain their access to the presentation.
  2. Click Start collaborating.
  3. The presentation will be displayed in speaker view. Learn more aboutcontrolling presentations in speaker view.
  4. (Optional) Next to [#]/[#] participants are following you, click the dropdown arrow, and use one of the following options:
  • Allow others to move through slides: Enabled to allow participants the ability to navigate through the slides, independently of the presenter.
  • Switch to next presenter: Allows the presenter to select a participant to have control of the presentation.

Using Canvas sentence completion with AI

Category: AI features > Features

How to use AI to complete a sentence in Zoom Canvas

  1. Create or access your document.
  2. In the top-right corner, click the more icon .
  3. Click Auto-suggest.
  4. Click the toggle next to Auto-complete to enable it for your document.
  5. Start typing in the body of the page. You may receive predictive writing suggestions as you type.
  6. Press the Tab key on your keyboard to accept the suggestion.

Using Zoom Canvas content generation and revision with AI

Category: AI features > Features

How to initiate AI in Zoom Canvas

  1. Create or open a Zoom doc, then do one of the following actions:
  • At the top of the document, in the toolbar, click the plus icon , then click Open AI chat icon .
  • In the body of your document, do one of the following:
  • Click Ask AI.
  • On an empty line, press the space key on your keyboard to start AI. Note: If you are unable to start AI by pressing your space key, in the top-right corner of your page, click the more icon , click Shortcut to AI, then click the toggle to enable the shortcut.
  • To the left of a line, click the Ask AI icon .
  • Highlight content in your document, then click the Ask AI icon .

How to generate content using AI in Zoom Canvas

After initiating AI in Zoom Canvas, a dialog box will appear. Click Continue to see this message each time you use AI , or select Don’t ask me again to prevent the dialog box from appearing in the future after you have read the Generate content with AI dialog box.

Use AI to generate new content in Zoom Canvas
  1. Initiate AIin a blank Zoom doc.
  2. Do one of the following:
  • In the text box, provide a prompt of what you’d like AI to help you write.
  • Below the text box, select a suggestion from one of the categories and provide a prompt to help tailor the content.
  1. Click the send icon .
  2. (Optional) Click Stop while the content is being generated if you change your mind or want to enter a different instruction.
  3. Review the proposed content, then click one of the following:
  • Improve the result box and enter your own instructions to improve the result, or select any of the following:
  • Shorter: To shorten the proposed content.
  • Longer: To lengthen the proposed content.
  • More formal: To write the content in a formal tone.
  • More casual: To write the content in a casual tone.
  • (Optional) To the right of the Ask AI box, click the left or right arrow to navigate to the proposed content you want to keep.
  • Click Keep to keep the proposed content.
  • Click the Try again icon to regenerate the proposed content.
  • Click the Discard icon to delete the proposed content.
Use AI in existing content in Zoom Canvas
  1. Initiating AIin a Zoom doc with existing content.
  2. Do one of the following:
  • In the Ask AI box, provide a prompt of what you’d like AI to help you do and click the send icon .
  • Under Revise selection, select an out-of-the-box suggestion.
  • Under Generate from selection
  • Select Translate to, enter the desired language, and click the send icon .
  • Select Convert to a list.
  • Under Help me understand, select Explain or Summarize.
  1. Review the generated content, then click:
    • Replace to replace the existing proposed content with the generated content.
  • Insert to insert the generated content within the existing proposed content.
  • The Try again icon to regenerate the proposed content.
  • The Discard icon to delete the proposed content.
Use AI to generate content from your Zoom meetings

If meeting summary is enabled on your account, you can use AI to generate meeting content in Zoom Canvas. Your admin must enable this feature. Learn more about enabling meeting summary.

  1. Initiate AIin a Zoom doc.
  2. Under Suggested, click Create from meeting, select an out-of-the-box suggestion, enter a prompt + @, or click the paperclip icon. A list of your past meetings will be displayed.
  3. (Optional) In the Meetings pop-up, click the calendar or filter icon to search for a specific meeting.
  4. Select a meeting with the meeting summary you want to reference.
  5. Click the send icon .
  6. (Optional) Click Stop while the content is being generated if you change your mind or want to enter a different instruction to improve the result.
  7. Review the proposed content, then click one of the following:
  • Improve the result box, enter your own instructions to improve the result, then select any of the following:
  • Shorter: To shorten the proposed content.
  • Longer: To lengthen the proposed content.
  • More formal: To write the content in a formal tone.
  • More casual: To write the content in a casual tone.
  • (Optional) To the right of the Ask AI box, click the left or right arrow to navigate to the proposed content you want to keep.
  • Click Keep to keep the proposed content.
  • Click the Try again icon to regenerate the proposed content.
  • Click the Discard icon to delete the proposed content.

Enabling or disabling Canvas content generation and revision with AI

Category: AI features > Settings

How to enable or disable Canvas content generation and revision with AI

Enable or disable Canvas content generation and revision with AI for the entire account

This setting allows account owners or admins to enable or disable Canvas content generation and revision with AI for all users in the account.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin with the privilege to edit account settings.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture or initials, then click Admin Center.
  3. In the side menu, click Settings .
  4. Click Zoom AI.
  5. Under Canvas, click the Canvas content generation and revision with AI toggle to enable or disable it.
  6. If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change.
  7. (Optional) To prevent all users in your account from changing these settings, click the lock icon , and then click Lock to confirm the setting.
Enable or disable Canvas content generation and revision with AI for a group of users

This setting allows account owners or admins to enable or disable Canvas content generation and revision with AI for a specific group of users. Changes apply only to users in the selected group.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin with the privilege to edit groups.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture or initials, then click Admin Center.
  3. In the side menu, click Users .
  4. Click Groups.
  5. Click the applicable group name from the list.
  6. In the General configuration section, click** Edit product settings**.
  7. Click the Zoom AI tab.
  8. Under Canvas, click the Canvas content generation and revision with AI toggle to enable or disable it.
  9. If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change.

Getting started with Zoom Canvas

Category: Getting started and setting up

Creating Zoom Canvas

You can create Zoom Canvas using the:

  • Zoom web portal
  • Zoom Workplace desktop app
  • Zoom Workplace mobile app
  • Zoom Web App
  • Zoom Meetings
  • Zoom Hub

Navigating Zoom Canvas

Homepage left sidebar

The left sidebar contains several sections for you to explore. Apart from the features listed below, we are continuously adding more.

  • My Profile: For account management, signing out, and personal settings.
  • Search: Allows you to search docs by titles and contents.
  • Various Tabs: Access your docs, shared docs, and favorites, among others.
  • Settings: Change your page settings.
  • Trash: Shows pages and docs you’ve deleted in the last 30 days. You can restore them within this period.
Tabs on the homepage
  • Notifications: Access your comment notifications and documents where you were mentioned.
  • Recent: Shows pages and docs you’ve recently viewed.
  • My Meetings: Access a list of your latest Zoom meetings and generate a document to collaborate with your participants for eligible meetings.
  • My Docs: Display and access all the docs you own.
  • Shared with Me: Shows docs owned by others and documents where you are a collaborator.
  • Starred: Access your most-used documents. To star a page or document, click on the star icon .

Adding a page

Your doc will start with one page. You can add more pages by clicking the + Add page** **icon in the top-left corner.

After adding pages, a page list appears on the left-hand side. You can add more pages by clicking the + Add icon at the bottom of this list.

You can also add a subpage to an existing page by clicking on the … icon beside the page title and choosing Add page, or by typing / anywhere on your current page and choosing Add subpage. Learn more about using Zoom Canvas.

Sharing a doc

You can share a doc to allow others to view and collaborate with the appropriate permissions. Click Share in the top-right corner and enter the name of the Zoom user you would like to share with. From the Share menu, you can also change who can access the doc and copy a link to share outside of Zoom. Learn more about Zoom Canvas sharing permission types.

You can also share a doc directly from Zoom Hub. Learn more about how to manage docs in Hub.

Using doc shortcuts

Zoom Canvas shortcuts can help you save time and improve your productivity when using the solution. Knowing the most common shortcuts can make navigating your docs easier and help you stay focused on the content. Learn more about using keyboard and mouse shortcuts with Canvas.

Adding media or files to Zoom Canvas

Category: Product features > User features

How to add images, audio, video, or files to your Zoom Canvas

You can attach up to a total of 2GB of media or files in your Zoom Canvas.

  1. Create your Zoom Canvas.
  2. On the top of the page, on the toolbar, click the plus icon or use the slash / menu.
  3. Under Media, select one of the following:
  • Image: Add an image from your computer, Unsplash, or GIPHY, with a maximum size of 30M.
  • Audio: Upload an audio file from your computer, with a size limit of 1GB.
  • Video: Upload a video file from your computer, with a size limit of 1GB.
  • File: Upload a file from your computer, with a size limit of 1GB.
  1. (Optional) Highlight your media, click the more icon , then click Delete to remove it from the doc.

Adding tables to Zoom Canvas

Category: Product features > User features

How to create a basic table in Zoom Canvas

You can create a basic table to provide a basic organization of data without analytical functions.

  1. Create your document.
  2. In an empty line, type / from the Slash menu or from the text editor toolbar click the plus icon +, then select Table. A table with 3 columns and 3 rows will be displayed.
  3. (Optional) Hover over the table, click the drag icon , and select Convert to Data Table to upgrade the basic table to a data table.
Manage a cell
  • Click within a cell to add or remove content to it.
Manage a row
  • Click a row, then click one of the following:
  • The merge cells icon to merge or split cells within the row. The cell colors icon to color the row.
  • The text alignment icon to align the text in the row.
  • The trash icon to delete the row.
  • The comment icon to leave a comment.
Manage a column
  • Click a column, then click one of the following:
  • The merge cells icon to merge or split cells within the column.
  • The cell colors icon to color the column.
  • The text alignment icon to align the text in the column.
  • The trash icon to delete the column.
  • The comment icon to leave a comment.
Manage the entire basic table
  1. To the top left of the table, click the drag icon to move the table.
  2. Click the six dots vertical to do the following:
  • Use AI to help write the content.
  • Change the color of the table.
  • Distribute the columns.
  • Copy the link of the Zoom Canvas.
  • Comment on the table
  • Insert content above the table.
  • Insert content below the table.
  • Copy the table.
  • Delete the table.

How to create a Data table in Zoom Canvas

You can create a data table to collect, organize, and track data, making it useful for project management, task and progress tracking, and managing various data assets.

  1. Create your document.
  2. In an empty line, type / from the Slash menu or from the text editor toolbar click the plus icon +, then select Data table. A table with 3 columns and 3 rows will be displayed. Note: Make sure there’s no empty space or indentation on that line.
  3. (Optional) Hover over the table, click the drag icon , and select Convert to Table to simplify the data table to a basic table.
Manage a cell

Click within a cell to add or remove content to it.

Manage a row

To manage a row, do the following:

  • To the left of the row, click the six dots vertical or check its number, to expand it, add a comment, duplicate it, delete it, etc.
  • At the bottom of the last row, click the plus icon to add a new row.
Manage a column

To manage a column, do the following:

  1. Select a column.
  2. Double-click a column header to do the following under:
  • Name: Enter a text.
  • Type: Select a type such as number, currency, multiple select, formula, date, etc.
  • More options: Provide a description and other options.
  1. Click Save.
  2. To the right of the column header, click the down arrow to edit it, duplicate it, sort it, etc.
  3. To the right of the last column, click the plus icon to add a new column.
Add a formula to your data table as an example
  1. Double-click the header of a column of the data table you created.
  2. Under Type, select Formula.
  3. Under Formula editor, click the box to edit the formula, then click Save.
  4. Under More options, add a Description as desired.
  5. Click Save.
  6. (Optional) Double-click an empty cell to edit the formula, then click Save. Note: You can type or select reference columns in the table.
Manage the entire Data table
  1. To the top left of the table, click the drag icon to move the table.
  2. Click the six dots vertical to do the following:
  • Use AI to help write the content.
  • Copy the link of the Zoom Canvas.
  • Insert content above or below the table.
  • Comment on the table
  • Copy the table.
  • Delete the table.
Change the Data table view
  1. On the top left of the Data table, click the plus icon , select one of the following:
  • Table view, to display a grid view or list view in a structured, tabular format.
  • Board view, to display the data as cards organized into columns, representing different stages of your process.
  • Calendar view, to display a calendar to your doc.
  • Gallery view, to display galleries to your doc.
  1. (Optional) On the top of the table, click on the view, then click the more icon , then select one of the following:
  • Rename: Rename the view.
  • Change view to: Change the view to a different view type.
  • Copy link to view: Copy the link of the view.
  • Duplicate: Duplicate the view.
  • Delete: Delete the view.

How to create a table from a spreadsheet

  1. Open your document in Zoom Canvas and your spreadsheet.
  2. From your spreadsheet, copy the content, then paste it into your document. A table will be created in your document with the pasted content.
  3. (Optional) On the top left corner of the table, click the six dots vertical , to manage it.

Creating Zoom Canvas

Category: Product features > User features

How to create Zoom Canvas

Follow the steps below to create Zoom Canvas using the web portal, desktop app, mobile app, or web app.

Create a doc in the Zoom web portal
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Click Canvas in the left sidebar.
  3. At the top of the page, click New document .
Create a doc in the Zoom Workplace desktop app
  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. Click the Canvas tab .
  3. At the top of the page, click New document .
Create a doc in the Zoom Workplace mobile app
  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace mobile app.
  2. At the bottom of the screen, tap More.
  3. Tap Canvas .
  4. In the bottom-right corner, click the plus icon .
Create a doc in the Zoom Web App
  1. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  2. Click the Canvas tab .
  3. At the top of the page, click New document .
Create a doc in a Zoom meeting
  1. Start or join your Zoom meeting.
  2. In the meeting toolbar, click Canvas. Note: If you don’t see that option, click More, then Canvas.

Create a doc in Zoom Hub

Learn about how to create Canvas docs and other assets in Zoom Hub.

Embedding links or pages within Zoom Canvas

Category: Product features > User features

How to embed a link or page into your document

  1. Create or access your document.
  2. In the body of the document, type /Embed, then select one of the following to embed:
  • Youtube: A Youtube video link.
  • X (formerly Twitter): An X thread link.
  • Figma: A Figma content link.
  • Google Drive: A Google Drive file link. Note: You will be required to connect to your Google Drive account if you are not connected.
  1. In the Link or page dialog box, enter or paste the page’s URL, then click Save.
  2. Highlight the displayed view, then in the toolbar, select one of the following to change how the page is embedded in your document:
  • Embed view: Displays the content in a window within the document. Notes:
  • The link or page will display the Embed view by default.
  • You can preview PDF content within your Zoom Doc.
  • Link view: Displays the content as a standard clickable hyperlink. Note: If you copy and paste a link in the doc, the link or page will display the Link view by default.
  • Card view: Shows a card with the title, a short description, and a link to the content.
  • Preview: Preview the content in a window within the document. Notes:
  • This functionality is available for Google Drive files connected to your Google Drive account.
  • Google Drive content shared to Zoom Canvas is visible to anyone who has access to the Zoom doc regardless of the content’s permissions or settings.

Managing Zoom Canvas

Category: Product features > User features

How to access your Zoom Canvas

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal or your Zoom app, then do one of the following:
  • From the Zoom app, on the top menu bar, click Docs.
  • From the Zoom web portal, on the left, in the navigation menu, under PERSONAL, click Docs.
  1. On the left of the page, follow the steps in the sections below according to what you want to do.

How to search for Zoom Canvas

You can search Zoom Canvas using keywords, by title, or author.

  1. Click the Search box. A search window will display.
  2. In Search, enter keywords or the title of the Zoom Canvas you are looking for, and/or do the following:
  • Date: Select a date range for your search.
  • Owner: Select or search the name of the author of the document.
  • Title only: Select this option if you want to search using title only.
  1. Identify the related Zoom Canvas, then click on it. The content of the Zoom Canvas will be displayed.
  2. (Optional) While on your doc, on the top left of the page, hover over Back to view your recently accessed documents, then click on the desired one to open it.

How to view comments on Zoom Canvas

  1. Click Notifications, then in the new windows do one of the following:
  • Click the All tab, to view all comments on a document, as well as any documents where you’ve been invited to leave comments.
  • Click the Unread tab, to view unread comments on the document.
  • Click the Mentions tab, to view all comments you were tagged on the document.
  1. (Optional) On the top right, click one of the following:
  • Mark all as read icon : Mark all messages as read.
  • The setting icon : Access the Zoom Canvas settings in the Zoom web portal to make any changes.

How to view recent activity in Zoom Canvas

  1. Click Recent, then view the following:
  • Name: Title of the doc.
  • Owner: Name of the author of the doc.
  • Last viewed: Minute, hour, day, week, month, or year ago the doc was last viewed.
  1. (Optional) Highlight the doc, then click the following icon:
  • Star : Add or remove the doc from your favorite list.
  • Link : Manually share the link with others.
  • Open : Open the doc to edit it.
  • On the far right of a doc, click the more icon to:
  • Copy the link, to manually share the link with others.
  • Open, to edit it.
  • Add or Remove it to/from your favorite list.
  • Hide from recent list, to hide it from your recent list.
  • Delete it if you are the author.

How to view meeting summaries in Zoom Canvas

All meeting summaries generated from meetings you own are stored in the Meeting summaries folder. Meeting summaries support viewing, commenting, and editing Zoom Canvas features.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal or the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Docs.
  3. In the left sidebar, click My docs, then Meeting summaries.

Notes:

  • The Meeting summaries folder is automatically created the first time a meeting summary is generated where you are the owner.
  • Only one Meeting summaries folder is created per user, and it will remain visible even if all summaries are deleted.

How to delete meeting summaries in Zoom Canvas using the desktop app

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Docs. Note: If you are unable to find the Docs option, click More to locate it.
  3. In the navigation menu, click My docs, then click Meeting summaries folder.
  4. Select the meeting summary you want to delete and click the 3 dots next to the document name.
  5. Click Delete .

How to delete meeting summaries in Zoom Canvas using the web portal

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Docs.
  3. In the new browser tab, click My docs in the navigation menu.
  4. Click the Meeting summaries folder.
  5. Select the meeting summary you want to delete and click the 3 dots next to the document name.
  6. Click Delete .

How to access your meeting templates

You can use your meeting templates to generate content with AI. Follow these steps to access your meeting templates.

  1. Click My meetings, then click a filter for the following:
  • All meetings: Filter All meetings you joined or Meetings you hosted.
  • Date: Filter the meeting date.
  1. On the far right of the meeting, identify the Create doc for the meeting template.

How to access Zoom Canvas you created

  1. Click My Docs, then view the following:
  • Name: Title of the doc.
  • Last viewed: Minute, hour, day, week, month, or year the doc was last viewed.
  1. (Optional) Highlight the doc, then click the following icon:
  • Star : Add or remove the doc from your favorite list.
  • Link : Manually share the link with others.
  • Open : Open the doc to edit it.
  • On the far right of a doc, click the more icon to:
  • Copy the link, to manually share the link with others.
  • Open the doc, to edit it.
  • Add or Remove it to/from your favorite list.
  • Delete it if you are the author.

How to access Zoom Canvas shared with you

  1. Click Shared with me, then view the following:
  • Name: Title of the doc.
  • Shared by: Name of the person who shared the doc with you.
  • Shared time: Minute, hour, day, week, month, or year ago the doc was shared with you.
  1. (Optional) Highlight the doc, then click the following icon:
  • Star : Add or remove the doc from your favorite list.
  • Link : Manually share the link with others.
  • Open : Open the doc to edit it.
  • On the far right of a doc, click the more icon to:
  • Copy the link, to manually share the link with others.
  • Open, to edit it.
  • Add or Remove it to/from your favorite list.
  • Delete it if you are the author.

How to view the list of your favorite Zoom Canvas

  1. Click Starred, then view the following:
  • Name: Title of the doc.
  • Owner: Name of the doc’s author.
  • Last modified: Minute, hour, day, week, month, or year ago the doc was updated.
  1. (Optional) Highlight the doc, then click the following icon:
  • Star : Add or remove the doc from your favorite list.
  • Link : Manually share the link with others.
  • Open : Open the doc to edit it.
  • On the far right of a doc, click the more icon to:
  • Copy the link, to manually share the link with others.
  • Open in browser, to edit it.
  • Remove it from your favorite list.
  • Delete it if you are the author.

How to access your Zoom Canvas

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal or your Zoom app, then do one of the following:
  • From the Zoom app, on the top menu bar, click Docs.
  • From the Zoom web portal, on the left, in the navigation menu, under PERSONAL, click Docs.
  1. On the left of the page, follow the steps in the sections below according to what you want to do.

How to access deleted Zoom Canvas

  1. At the bottom left of the page, click the trash icon , then view the following:
  • Title: The title of the document.
  • Deleted by: The name of the person who deleted the document.
  • Deleted at: The time the document was deleted.
  1. (Optional) On the far right, click one of the following icons:
  • Restore : To remove the deleted list.
  • Trash : To permanently delete the doc before the 30 days period.

Note: Deleted docs are permanently deleted after 30 days and cannot be recovered.

Using Zoom Canvas

Category: Product features > User features

How to create a new doc from Zoom Canvas

You can easily create a new doc from either your Zoom app or the web portal. Once created, you can access and work on your Zoom Canvas in those environments as needed.

  • Zoom web portal
  • Zoom Workplace desktop app
  • Zoom Workplace mobile app
  • Zoom Web App
  • Zoom Meetings
  • Zoom Hub

How to use the Slash menu

While editing your Zoom Canvas, you can type slash / to insert the following types of items:

  • Basic: Text, headers, bulleted lists, etc.
  • Featured: Ask AI to write and Data table.
  • Display: Table, Callout, Quote, etc.
  • Media: Image, Audio, Video, etc.
  • Page: Subpages and links to pages.
  • Mention: Person, date, file.
  • Embed: YouTube, X, Google Drive file, Figma, etc.
  • Actions: Copy link, insert above, insert below, etc.

How to use the Zoom Canvas text editor toolbar

The text editor toolbar provides you with easy access to various formatting and editing tools.

At the top of your document the following tools are available to help you with the following: Note: Highlighting a text gives you access to the same tools. You can use different shortcuts for basic editing if you want to perform different actions straight from your keyboard.

  • Undo : Undo the last action.
  • Redo : Redo the last action.
  • Bold : Bold the selected text.
  • Italicize : Italicize the selected text.
  • Underline : Underline the selected text.
  • Strikethrough : Striketh through the selected text.
  • Text Color: Changes the text color for the selected text.
  • Link : Adds a hyperlink to the selected text.
  • Mark as code : Changes the selected text into a code block.
  • Create equation : Change the selected text to an inline block equation.
  • Text Alignment : Align the selected text in either left, right, or center alignment, increase or decrease indent.
  • Comment : Adds a comment to the selected text.
  • (Optional) More:Click More, if some options are not viewable to view them. Note: Visible only from the Zoom app.
  • Plus : Access advanced editing tools.

How to use the advanced editing tools

In addition to the basic editing, clicking the plus sign icon allows you to access many featured actions, layouts, and styles when highlighting a text. You can select the following options:

Featured
  • Data Table: Insert a data table.
Layout & Style
  • Table: Insert a basic table.
  • Callout: Insert a callout text in the doc.
  • Quote: Turns the selected text into a block of quoted text.
  • Web card: Allows the insertion of a web card based on a URL, which includes the page title, a preview of the page text, and the URL itself.

How to add a page to your Zoom Canvas

  1. From your document, on the top left of the page, click the Add page icon.
  2. Add a title to the page.
  • (Optional) On the left of the page, to the right of the name of your page, click the more icon , then click Add page to add a sub-page to your page.
  1. Use the Slash / menu as desired.
  2. On the top right of the new page, click the more icon and click Delete to delete the page. The page will be deleted as well as any sub-pages.
  3. (Optional) Under your new page, click + Add, to add a new page.

How to manage the layout of a Zoom Canvas

You can organize the content of your Zoom Canvas by using the Page options setting and dragging and dropping what you need as described in the following sections below.

Access a Zoom Canvas page options
  1. Open your document.
  2. On the right, click the more icon then Page options.
  3. In the Page options window, select any of the following options:
  • Cover: Add or remove a cover to your document.
  • Icon: Add or remove an icon to the header of your document.
  • Title: Display or hide the title section of your document.
  • Author: Display or hide the author of your document.
  • Last Updated: Display or hide the date the document was last updated.
  • Outline: Display or hide the outline of your document.
  • Font style: Change the font style of your document.
  • Page width: Change the page width of your document.
  1. On the top right of the Page Options window, click the X icon to exit the window.
Drag and drop content in Zoom Canvas

You can effortlessly arrange content on your page by using the drag-and-drop feature. This allows you to move text, images, and other objects to achieve your desired layout with ease.

  1. Open your document.
  2. On the left of your text, image, or other object, click the drag icon , then drag and drop it anywhere within the document.

How to share your Zoom Canvas

Once you create your document, you can easily share it with others, enabling collaboration. Sharing the document allows everyone to work together, comment on any part of the document, and tag specific people in the comments. Learn more about Zoom Canvas user permission types.

  1. Open your document.
  2. On the top right of your Zoom Canvas, click Share.
  3. In the Share window, the following options will be available:
  • In the search box, enter the contact(s), channel(s), or email address(es) you desire to share the document with, then select one of the following permission levels: Note: When using this method to share a document, by default your contact will be notified via email and will be granted the Commenter permission level.
  • Co-owner: Allow your contact to have the same permissions as the original doc owner, including sharing, editing, commenting, and deleting.
  • Editor: Allow your contact to make changes to the document and comment as necessary.
  • Commenter: Allow your contact to comment only on your document.
  • Viewer: Allow your contact to view only your document.
  • (Optional) Select Notify in chat, if you have this feature and would like to notify your contact via chat. Enter a message, then click Send. Your user(s) will receive a notification in Chat.
  • Under General Access, select one of the following:
  • Only you can access: This is selected by default, giving you only the ability to work on the document.
  • Collaborators only:Add collaborators and the default link access will be updated to allow collaborators access to the document.
  • Anyone in [Name of your organization]: Allow anyone in your organization’s Zoom account to search for the document and access it by link.
  • Anyone with link: Allow anyone with the doc link to view the content, however, to comment or edit, users need to be signed in to their Zoom account or app. Note: This feature can only be enabled by your account admin. Contact your admin if this option is greyed out and you cannot select it.
  • Click one of the social media buttons to share the doc to that social media platform. Note: When using the social media buttons, the doc’s access level will be set to Anyone with a link, and the platform will be redirected with a reference to the doc link.
  • Click Copy Link, to manually share the link of the document with others.

You can also share a doc directly from Zoom Hub. Learn more about how to manage docs in Hub.

How to comment on your Zoom Canvas

  1. Open your document.
  2. Highlight a text in your document, then in the toolbar that appears, click the comment icon .
  3. In the Comment box, enter your comment, then click the send icon .
  4. (Optional) At the bottom left of the comment box, click one of the following icons:
  • Tag icon : Tag a specific user(s) to your comment. Note: You can tag a user that you didn’t share the document with and the document will automatically be shared with them.
  • Emoji icon : Add an emoji to your comment.
  • Attach icon : Attach a file from your computer to your comment.
View and reply to comments on your Zoom Canvas
  1. Open your document.
  2. On the top right of the Zoom Canvas, click the comment icon or Unread to show new comments on your document.
  3. Click on your comment.
  4. In the Reply box, enter your reply.
  5. Click the send icon .
  6. (Optional) Click the more icon , then click Copy link, to manually send a link of your comment to others.
Resolve or delete comments from your Zoom Canvas
  1. Open your document.
  2. On the top right of the Zoom Canvas, click the comment icon or on the right, click the comment with number icon.
  3. Click on your comment, then on the right of the window, click one of the following:
  • Resolve icon : To resolve the comment(s).
  • More icon : Select Delete thread, to delete the comment(s).

How to manage your Zoom Canvas

Follow this guide to manage your Zoom Canvas.

Using Zoom Canvas during a meeting

Category: Product features > User features > Zoom Workplace app

How to access Zoom Canvas during a meeting

  1. Start or join your Zoom Meeting.
  2. In the meeting control, click Docs. Note: If you don’t see that option, click More, then Docs.
  3. In the Share docs window, do one of the following:
  4. Create a doc.
  5. Share an existing doc.
  6. Proceed to the appropriate section in this article according to what you desire to do.
Create Zoom Canvas during a meeting

While you are in a Zoom Meeting, you can create docs to help you create a list of action items, start a project plan, or others. Use the Slash menu/ to help you access those items and quickly format your content. All docs created in the meeting will be owned by the meeting host.

  1. Click + New, to create a new Zoom Canvas.
  2. In your Zoom Canvas page, start typing. You can add content such as the following amongst many:
  • Add a date using /date.
  • Add tasks using /To-do list.
  • Add a Data table to create a project management plan using /Data table.
  1. (Optional) Change your collaborators’ permission to the doc as desired.
Share Zoom Canvas during a meeting

If you already created a doc, you can share the document while in a meeting.

  1. In the Share docs window, do one of the following:
  • In the search box, enter the title, then click Share.
  • Highlight the Zoom Canvas, then on its right, click Share. The content of the Zoom doc will be displayed and the URL will be accessible to all participants in the meeting chat.
  1. (Optional) On the top right of the Zoom Canvas, click Share to allow your participants to collaborate on it as needed.
  2. On the top right of the Zoom Canvas, click the X icon to stop sharing it.
Take notes using Zoom Canvas during a meeting

You can follow this guide to use Zoom Canvas to take meeting notes.

Give permission to Zoom Canvas during a meeting

When sharing a doc during a meeting, you can give other meeting participants permission to collaborate on a doc during your meeting.

  1. Create or share an existing doc.
  2. On the top right of the doc, click Share.
  3. Under Collaborators to this doc, do the following:
  • Under Temporary, select:
  • Persistent access: Participants can access the doc during and after the meeting ends.
  • Temporary access: Participants can access the doc only during the meeting. Note: Temporary access is selected by default.
  • Under Commenter, change the permission to:
  • Editor: Can edit, manage pages via the page list, manage the doc’s permission, and leave and check comments.
  • Commenter: Can only comment on the doc and cannot edit.
  • Viewer: Can only view the doc and cannot edit or comment. Note: By default, anonymous meeting participants who are not signed into the Zoom app have view-only permission.
Advanced Zoom Canvas sharing options during a meeting

You can change your Zoom Canvas sharing options during your meeting to make sure the appropriate participants can share those documents.

Note: Anonymous users are meeting participants who are not signed into the Zoom app.

  1. On the meeting controls menu, hover over the Docs icon, then click the up arrow . The Advanced Sharing Options window will be displayed.
  2. Enable or disable the following:
  • Allow participants to share docs.
  • If enabled, under Who can start sharing when someone else is sharing?, select:
  • Host only: Only the meeting host can share Zoom Canvas during the meeting.
  • All participants (exclude anonymous users): All participants signed in to the Zoom app can share Zoom Canvas during the meeting. Participants not signed in to the Zoom app cannot share those documents.
  • Under Who can create a doc in this meeting? Select:
  • Host only: Only the meeting host can create Zoom Canvas during the meeting.
  • Internal users only: Only participants within the organization can create Zoom Canvas during the meeting.
  • All participants (exclude anonymous users): All participants signed in to the Zoom app can create Zoom Canvas during the meeting. Participants not signed in to the Zoom app cannot create documents.

How to quickly meet in a Zoom Meeting while working in Zoom Canvas

While working or being on a doc, you can quickly meet with your collaborators as needed to speed up what needs to be done.

  1. Create your docs if you haven’t created one or access it if you already have one.
  2. On the top right of the page, click the camera icon .
  3. Click Meet now. You may be requested to open your Zoom application.
  4. In the Open zoom.us dialog box, click Open zoom.us. Your meeting window will be displayed and your Zoom Canvas will be automatically shared.
  5. Invite your participants to the meeting.

How to schedule a Zoom Meeting while working on a Zoom Canvas

While working or being on Zoom Canvas, you can quickly schedule a meeting with your collaborators as needed.

  1. Create your doc if you haven’t created one or access it if you already have one.
  2. On the top right of the page, click the camera icon .
  3. Click Schedule meeting. You may be requested to open your Zoom application.
  4. In the Open zoom.us dialog box, click Open zoom.us. Your meeting window will be displayed.
  5. In the scheduled meeting window, adjust what you need as required. Under Attachments, your Zoom Canvas will be attached to your scheduled meeting.
  6. Click Save.

Using Zoom Canvas to take notes while in a meeting

Category: Product features > User features > Zoom Workplace app

How to take notes using Zoom Canvas during a meeting

  1. Start or join your Zoom Meeting.
  2. In the meeting control, click Docs. Note: If you don’t see that option, click More, then Docs.
  3. In the Share Zoom Canvas window, click Take notes. A personal meeting note page will be displayed on the right of the meeting window.
  4. On the top right of the note page, click one of the following icons:
  • More : To open your note page in your default browser or copy its link.
  • Share to meeting : To share your notes in the meeting to allow meeting participants to comment on it. Note: Anonymous users cannot comment on your personal meeting notes.
  • Pop-up : To pop your note page out of the meeting window. Note: On the top right of your pop-up note window, click the Pop-in icon to return the note page to the meeting window.
  • Close : To close your note page.

August 30, 2024
New and enhanced features
  • In-meeting features
  • Search docs using URL links for in-meeting shared docs Users can now search for and share documents using their URL links directly within a Zoom meeting. Previously, document searches were limited to titles within Zoom Docs.
  • User features
  • Calendar view for visualizing and scheduling dates Users can display data in a calendar-style view to efficiently visualize and schedule dates. They can see feature release dates, task timelines, and other date-related information. The calendar automatically adjusts for multiple items on the same day, and users can navigate between months, search, and edit dates directly. This feature enhances scheduling efficiency and provides a clear overview of upcoming events and deadlines.
  • Gallery view for visual data presentation Users can present data visually in a grid layout using the new gallery view feature in Zoom Docs. The gallery view is designed for scenarios where there are many records in a table, and users want to present the data through visual information. For example, HR professionals can build an employee directory, marketing professionals can create a library of competitors’ marketing activities, and users can create a trip wishlist or build a landing wiki. With the gallery view, users can easily generate a creative layout to present and manage media content.
  • Enhancements to doc return experience Users can quickly access recently visited Zoom Docs and pages by hovering over the return button. This feature loads a list of recent documents and pages, allowing users to easily navigate back to their previous work. The improved return experience streamlines the process of switching between different documents and pages, enhancing productivity and efficiency. This feature is enabled by default.
  • Import Notion documents into Zoom Docs Users can import Notion documents into Zoom Docs by exporting the Notion page as an HTML file and uploading the downloaded zip file. The import process is handled asynchronously, and users can track the progress through notifications. Upon successful import, users can choose to create a new document or add the imported content as subpages to an existing document. If the import fails, an error message is displayed with the reason for the failure. This feature enhances the document collaboration capabilities by allowing users to seamlessly integrate content from Notion into Zoom Docs.
Resolved issues
  • Minor bug fixes
August 5, 2024
  • Introducing Zoom Docs Zoom Docs allows users to collaborate and track projects easily and seamlessly. Users can draft, organize, and share materials and documents whether they are in a meeting or not. To make the most of their meetings, users can transform past and present meetings into actionable documents, wikis, and projects using Meeting AI templates. Zoom’s AI Companion features further enhance efficiency by generating and translating content. While creating materials, users have access to basic editing tools, block actions, and various content types that can be added or embedded. In addition, documents can be shared directly with other users or through Team Chat channels. The feature can be enabled or disabled at the account or group level.

Managing Zoom Canvas default access permissions

Category: User Management > Roles and permissions

How to enable or disable Canvas Access

Enable or disable Canvas Access at the account level
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Click Account Management, then Account Settings.
  3. Click the Canvas tab.
  4. Click Canvas Access to navigate to the section.
  5. Under Who can access your account’s docs, click one of the following:
  • Only users in your organization: Allow only users within your account to access newly created documents.
  • Users in your account and outside your organization: Allow users within and outside your account to access newly created documents. Note: Depending on the default doc link access configuration, defined in step 7 below, users may be able to view documents without signing in to their Zoom account.
  1. Click the Allow users to collaborate on other organizations’ docs toggle to enable or disable the option. Note: If disabled, your account’s users will not be able to access docs owned by other organizations.
  • If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change.
  • (Optional) To prevent all users in your account from changing these settings, click the lock icon , and then click Lock to confirm the setting.
  1. Under Default Access Level, click one of the following:
  • Collaborators only: Allow only documents’ collaborators to access newly created document links.
  • Anyone in organization: Allow all users within your account to access newly created document links.
  • Anyone with link: Allow anyone to access newly created document links and view the content. Note: Users can view the content of documents but need to sign in to their Zoom account or app to comment or edit them.
  1. Click Save.
Enable or disable Canvas Access at the group level
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click User Management then Groups.
  3. Click the applicable group name from the list.
  4. Click the Canvas tab.
  5. Click Canvas Access to navigate to the section.
  6. Click the Allow users to collaborate on other organizations’ Canvas toggle to enable or disable the option. Note: If disabled, users will not be able to access docs owned by other organizations.
  • If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change.
  1. Under Default Access Level, click one of the following:
  • Collaborators only: Allow only documents’ collaborators to access newly created document links.
  • Anyone in organization: Allow all users within your account to access newly created document links.
  • Anyone with link: Allow anyone to access newly created document links and view the content. Note: Users can view the content of documents but need to sign in to their Zoom account or app to comment or edit them.
  1. Click Save.
Enable or disable Canvas Access at the user level
  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click User Management then Users.
  3. Click the name of the user from the list.
  4. Click the Settings tab, then select Canvas.
  5. Click Canvas Access to navigate to the section.
  6. Under Default Access Level, click one of the following:
  • Collaborators only: Allow only documents’ collaborators to access newly created document links.
  • Anyone in organization: Allow all users within your account to access newly created document links.
  • Anyone with link: Allow anyone to access newly created document links and view the content. Note: Users can view the content of documents but need to sign in to their Zoom account or app to comment or edit them.
  1. Click Save.

Zoom Canvas User permission types

Category: User Management > Roles and permissions

User permission types for Zoom Canvas

  • Owner: A user who created the Zoom Canvas. The Owner has permission to edit, comment, assign sharing permissions to others, and delete the document. The Owner can also transfer the ownership of the document to another user.
  • Co-owner: A user who shares the same rights as the owner. A Co-Owner can edit, comment, assign sharing permissions to other users, and delete the document.
  • Editor: A user who can view the content of the document. An Editor can edit and comment on it.
  • Commenter: A user who can view the content of Zoom Canvas. A Commenter can comment on that doc.
  • Viewer: A user who can only view the content of Zoom Canvas.
Privilege Owner Co-owner Editor Commenter Viewer
Invite users Yes Yes Yes No No
Remove users Yes Yes Yes No No
Change user roles Yes Yes Yes No No
Assign co-owner, Editor, Commenter, Viewer Yes Yes Yes but cannot assign co-owner No No
Add/delete/modify contents Yes Yes Yes No No
Add/reply to a comment Yes Yes Yes Yes No
Edit comment Yes Yes Yes Yes No
Delete comment Yes Yes Yes Yes No
Add page Yes Yes Yes No No
Print page Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
Delete page Yes Yes Yes No No
Delete Zoom Canvas Yes Yes No No No
Permanently delete Zoom Canvas from Trash Yes Yes No No No

Using AI task creation and management with Zoom Tasks

Category: AI features > Features

How to view tasks generated for a meeting within a Meeting Summary

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. Locate the desired Meeting Summary.
  3. Under Next Steps, tasks that were recommended from the Meeting Summary will be displayed. Note: Depending on the host’s settings, you may also be able to view the task even if you were not the assignee.

How to view tasks generated for a phone call within a Call Summary

When Automatically generate tasks from phone call summary is enabled, you can receive AI-generated task recommendations based on your call summaries. You can create tasks manually using a dedicated button that opens the task creation dialog. The feature includes right-click functionality for direct task creation on calls and displays all generated tasks when viewing the call history. Call participants can be automatically added as task collaborators based on admin configuration.

Learn more about managing and generating Tasks for Call Summary.

How to view tasks generated for a meeting within Zoom Calendar

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. Click the Calendar tab .
  3. Click a past calendar event to see more details.
  4. Under Next Steps, tasks that were recommended from the Meeting Summary will be displayed.
  5. If a task has been assigned to you already, you can click on the task to view more details, or click the checkbox to complete to the task. Note: Depending on the host’s settings, you may also be able to view the task even if you were not the assignee.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.

  2. Click the Tasks tab .

  3. In the Tasks navigation menu, click Recommended.

  4. Tasks generated via AI will be displayed and grouped by the associated Meeting.

  5. (Optional) Click the dropdown to select Group by source or Group by topic.

  6. (Optional) Click the add button to add an Assignee.

  7. Click Accept to add the task.

  8. (Optional) To delete a task, click the More button , then click Delete.

  9. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace mobile app.

  10. Tap the Tasks tab . Note: If you do not see the Tasks tab, tap the More tab, then tap Tasks.

  11. Tap Recommended.

  12. Click the add button to accept the task.

  13. (Optional) To delete the task, click the remove button .

  14. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.

  15. In the navigation menu, click Tasks.

  16. In the Tasks navigation menu, click Recommended.

  17. Tasks generated via AI will be displayed and grouped by the associated Meeting.

  18. (Optional) Click the dropdown to select Group by source or Group by topic.

  19. (Optional) Click the add button to add an Assignee.

  20. Click Accept to add the task.

  21. (Optional) To delete a task, click the More button , then click Delete.

How to generate details for a task

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace app.

  2. Click the Tasks tab . Note: If you do not see the Tasks tab, click the More tab, then click Tasks.

  3. Select My Tasks, All Tasks, Starred Tasks, or a Personal List.

  4. Click on the desired task.

  5. At the bottom of the task details, click Generate task details. AI will generate details for the task, including the Task Description, Due date, and Priority, based on the Task title.

  6. (Optional) Click Regenerate results to regenerate the task details.

  7. (Optional) Click Undo to remove the generated description.

  10. Select My Tasks, All Tasks, Starred Tasks, or a Personal List.

  13. (Optional) Tap Regenerate results to regenerate the task details.

  14. (Optional) Tap Undo to remove the generated description.
