How to have AI suggest steps to complete a task

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. Click the Tasks tab .
  3. In the Tasks navigation menu, click My Tasks, All Tasks, Starred Tasks, or a Personal List.
  4. Hover your mouse over the task name and click the AI actions button.
  5. Select an action from the menu:
  • Under Suggested action, click the suggested action item for the task.
  • Under Other actions, click an action that was not suggested.
  • Click Ask AI to have AI suggest additional ways to complete the task.

Enable task creation and management with AI

Category: AI features > Settings

How to enable Task creation and management with AI

Enable or disable Task creation and management with AI for the entire account

This setting allows account owners or admins to enable or disable Task creation and management with AI for all users in the account.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin with the privilege to edit account settings.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture or initials, then click Admin Center.
  3. In the side menu, click .
  4. Click Zoom AI.
  5. Under Tasks, enable Task creation and management with AI.
  6. If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change.
  7. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate recommended actions to complete tasks for AI to suggest actions for completing a task.
  8. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate tasks from meeting summaries for tasks to be created for Meeting Summaries after they have been generated.
  9. Under Automatically add meeting participants as task collaborators, select who will be automatically added as task collaborators:
  • Meeting host only: Only the meeting host will be added as a collaborator.
  • Meeting host and participants from your account who are assigned tasks: The meeting host and all internal participants assigned tasks will be added as collaborators to the tasks.
  • Meeting host and participants from your account: The meeting host and all internal participants will be added as collaborators, whether they were assigned or not assigned a task.
  1. (Optional) Enable Automatically assign tasks generated from the meeting summaries to eligible collaborators to have the generated tasks assigned automatically.
  2. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate tasks from phone call summary to allow automatic Zoom Task creation from AI-generated call summaries, with options to configure collaborator settings for call participants.
  3. Under this setting, select who will automatically be added as task collaborators:
  • Automatically add phone call participants from your organization as task collaborators: The phone call participants from your organization will be added as collaborators.
  • Automatically assign tasks generated from the phone call summary to eligible collaborators: Have the generated tasks assigned automatically.
  1. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate tasks from voicemail transcription to enable automatic Zoom task creation from AI-generated voicemail transcription. Note: This feature currently supports English transcriptions only.
  2. (Optional) To prevent all users in your account from changing this setting, click the lock icon, and then click Lock to confirm the setting.
Enable or disable Task creation and management with AI for a group of users

This setting allows account owners or admins to enable or disable Task creation and management with AI for a specific group of users. Changes apply only to users in the selected group.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin with the privilege to edit groups.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture or initials, then click Admin Center.
  3. In the side menu, click Users .
  4. Click Groups.
  5. Click the applicable group name from the list.
  6. In the General configuration section, click Edit product settings.
  7. Click the Zoom AI tab.
  8. Under Tasks, enable Task creation and management with AI.
  9. If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change.
  10. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate recommended actions to complete tasks for AI to suggest actions for completing a task.
  11. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate tasks from meeting summaries for tasks to be created for Meeting Summaries after they have been generated.
  12. Under Automatically add meeting participants as task collaborators, select who will be automatically added as task collaborators:
  • Meeting host only: Only the meeting host will be added as a collaborator.
  • Meeting host and participants from your organization: The meeting host and all participants will be added as collaborators.
  • Meeting host and all internal participants from your organization: The meeting host and only participants who are users on the same account as the host will be added as collaborators.
  1. (Optional) Enable Automatically assign tasks generated from the meeting summaries to eligible collaborators to have the generated tasks assigned automatically.
  2. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate tasks from phone call summary to allow automatic Zoom Task creation from AI-generated call summaries, with options to configure collaborator settings for call participants.
  3. Under this setting, select who will automatically be added as task collaborators:
  • Automatically add phone call participants from your organization as task collaborators: The phone call participants from your organization will be added as collaborators.
  • Automatically assign tasks generated from the phone call summary to eligible collaborators: Have the generated tasks assigned automatically.
  1. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate tasks from voicemail transcription to enable automatic Zoom task creation from AI-generated voicemail transcription. Note: This feature currently supports English transcriptions only.
  2. (Optional) To prevent all users in the group from changing this setting, click the lock icon, and then click Lock to confirm the setting.
Enable or disable Task creation and management with AI for your personal account

This setting allows individual users to enable or disable Task creation and management with AI for their personal account. You do not need admin permissions to change the setting, unless it is locked by an admin for the entire account or a group of users.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture or initials, then click My account.
  3. In the side menu, click Settings .
  4. Click Zoom AI.
  5. Under Tasks, enable Task creation and management with AI.
  6. If a verification dialog appears, click Enable or Disable to verify the change. Note: If the option is grayed out, it has been locked at either the group or account level. You need to contact your Zoom admin.
  7. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate recommended actions to complete tasks for AI to suggest actions for completing a task.
  8. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate tasks from meeting summaries for tasks to be created for Meeting Summaries after they have been generated.
  9. Under Automatically add meeting participants as task collaborators, select who will be automatically added as task collaborators:
  • Meeting host only: Only the meeting host will be added as a collaborator.
  • Meeting host and participants from your organization: The meeting host and all participants will be added as collaborators.
  • Meeting host and all internal participants from your organization: The meeting host and only participants who are users on the same account as the host will be added as collaborators.

  2. (Optional) Enable Automatically generate tasks from phone call summary to allow automatic Zoom Task creation from AI-generated call summaries, with options to configure collaborator settings for call participants.
  3. Under this setting, select who will automatically be added as task collaborators:
  • Automatically add phone call participants from your organization as task collaborators: The phone call participants from your organization will be added as collaborators.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace app.
  2. Click the Tasks tab . Note: If you do not see the Tasks tab, click the More tab, then click Tasks.
  3. In the top left corner, click the Add icon .
  4. Enter the Title of the task.
  5. Under Due Date, set the date by which the task needs to be completed.
  6. Under Assignees, select the users to be assigned to the task. Note: By default, you will be listed as an Assignee.
  7. Under Description, enter the description of the task. Additionally, the following formatting options are available:
  • Undo : Undo the last action.
  • Redo : Redo the last action.
  • Text format: Change the selected text to either Paragraph, Heading 1, or Heading 2 style.
  • Bold : Bold the selected text.
  • Italicize : Italicize the selected text.
  • Underline : Underline the selected text.
  • Strikethrough : Strikethrough the selected text.
  • Text Color: Changes the text color for the selected text.
  • Numbered list : Add a numbered list to the text.
  • Bulleted list : Add a bulleted list to the text.
  • Add link : Add a hyperlink to the selected text.
  • Quote text : Turns the selected text into a quote text block.
  • Add image : Upload an image to the description.
  • Clear formatting : Clears the text formatting.
  • Add emoji : Add emojis to text.
  1. (Optional) Under Attachments, click + Add Attachments to add any files for reference.
  2. (Optional) Under Status, select the starting status for the task. Note: By default, the Status will be set to To Do.
  3. Under Visibility, select one of the following:
  • Only assignees and collaborators: Only those added as assignees or collaborators will be able to view the task.
  • Anyone at [Organization name]: All users within an organization will be able to view the task.

  7. Under Due Date, set the date by which the task needs to be completed.

  8. Under Assignees, select the users to be assigned to the task. Note: By default, you will be listed as an Assignee.

  9. Under Description, enter the description of the task. Additionally, the following formatting options are available:

  • Undo : Undo the last action.
  • Redo : Redo the last action.
  • Text format: Change the selected text to either Paragraph, Heading 1, or Heading 2 style.
  • Bold : Bold the selected text.
  • Italicize : Italicize the selected text.
  • Underline : Underline the selected text.
  • Strikethrough : Strikethrough the selected text.
  • Text Color: Changes the text color for the selected text.
  • Numbered list : Add a numbered list to the text.
  • Bulleted list : Add a bulleted list to the text.
  • Add link : Add a hyperlink to the selected text.
  • Quote text : Turns the selected text into a quote text block.
  • Add image : Upload an image to the description.
  • Clear formatting : Clears the text formatting.
  • Add emoji : Add emojis to text.
  1. (Optional) Under Attachments, click + Add Attachments to add any files for reference.
  2. (Optional) Under Status, select the starting status for the task. Note: By default, the Status will be set to To Do.
  3. Under Visibility, select one of the following:
  • Only assignees and collaborators: Only those added as assignees or collaborators will be able to view the task.
  • Anyone at [Organization name]: All users within an organization will be able to view the task.
  1. (Optional) Under Collaborators, click the Add icon to add contacts as collaborators.
  2. Click Create.

How to create a task in Zoom Chat

Users can create tasks from Chat messages or specific text within a chat message. Learn more about creating tasks in Zoom Chat.

How to create a task in Zoom Mail

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS

  1. Click the Mail tab .

  2. Click an email to open it.

  7. Tap the Mail tab . Note: If you do not see the Mail tab, tap the More tab, then tap Mail.

ZoomMate and Zoom AI Companion

Using the AI dashboard

Category: Analytics and reporting

How to access the AI tab in the Dashboard

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an account owner or administrator.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture or initials, then click Admin Center.
  3. In the navigation menu, click Dashboard.
  4. At the top of the Dashboard, click the AI tab.
  5. The dashboard is organized into 4 tabs:
  • AI
  • Custom AI
  • Agent
  • ROI

The dashboard displays multiple sections showing adoption, usage metrics, and trends.

View the adoption funnel

The adoption funnel section provides a visual representation of AI, Custom AI, and Agent adoption across your organization. This section displays three key metrics:

  • Licensed users: The total number of unique licensed users on the current day.
  • Active users: The total number of unique active users in the last quarter (last 90 days).

The funnel visualization helps you understand the progression from licensing to actual usage, identifying potential adoption barriers.

Filter dashboard data

The dashboard provides several filtering options to customize your view and focus on specific data segments.

Group filtering
  1. Click the Groups filter field.
  2. Select one or multiple groups from the list.
  3. The filter supports both primary and secondary groups.

Click the Clear filters option to reset the filters.

Department filtering
  1. Click the Department filter field.
  2. Search for or select specific departments.

Click the Clear filters option to reset the filters.

Note: Filtering options apply to all sections below the adoption funnel, including KPIs, historical trends, and the leaderboard.

Understanding the usage metrics

Account owners and admins can access comprehensive usage data for AI, Custom AI, and Agent through the AI dashboard. The dashboard presents key performance indicators and allows admins to filter data while analyzing historical trends across customizable time periods. Advanced filtering options and top user analytics offer deeper insights into feature utilization patterns.

The Key Performance Indicators (KPI) section displays the number of users who have used the given feature and the number of user interactions with that feature.

You can also filter the metrics to view them from a specific timeframe (under KPI date range), department, or group (under Global filters). To adjust the timeframe of these metrics, click the drop-down menu above this section and choose from the following options:

  • Daily: View the current day’s usage metrics.
  • Weekly: View the past week’s worth of usage metrics. This includes the present day and the 6 previous days.
  • Monthly: View the past month’s worth of usage metrics. This includes the present day and the 27 previous days, regardless of whether the month has 30 or 31 days.
AI

The following metrics may be available, depending on which AI features are enabled on the account:

  • Active Users: The number of unique users who completed at least one action with AI in the specified timeframe.
  • AI chat panel active users: The number of unique users who completed at least one action with AI chat panel in the specified timeframe.
  • AI chat panel queries: The number of queries initiated in AI chat panels during the specified timeframe. This includes queries typed by users as well as user clicks on AI-generated prompts.
  • Meeting active users: The number of unique users who completed at least one action with AI in Meetings features (e.g., Meeting Summary, Meeting Questions) during the selected timeframe.
  • Meeting summary hosts: The number of users on the account who have used the meeting summary feature in the specified timeframe.
  • Meeting with summaries: The number of meetings on the account that have used the meeting summary feature in the specified timeframe. Users attending external meetings where AI features were used are not included.
  • Meeting questions users: The number of users on the account that have used the in-meeting questions feature in the specified timeframe.
  • Meeting with questions: The number of meetings on the account that have used the in-meeting questions feature in the specified timeframe.
  • Chat active users: The number of unique users who completed at least one action with AI in Chat features (e.g. Thread summary, Compose, etc.) in the specified timeframe.
  • Chat compose users: The number of users on the account that have used the Chat compose feature in the specified timeframe.
  • Chat compose events: The number of Chat messages composed with the Chat compose feature on the account in the specified timeframe.
  • Chat thread summary users: The number of users on the account that have used the Chat thread summary feature in the specified timeframe.
  • Chat thread summaries generated: The number of thread summaries generated with the Chat thread summary feature on the account in the specified timeframe.
  • Smart Recording users: The number of users on the account that have used the smart recording feature in the specified timeframe.
  • Smart Recording generated: The number of smart recordings created on the account in the specified timeframe.
  • Phone active users: The number of unique users who completed at least one action with AI in Phone features (e.g., call summary and voicemail prioritization) in the specified timeframe.
  • Call Summary active users: The total number of unique active users who use phone summary feature during this period.
  • Voicemail Prioritization active users: Total number of unique active users who use Voicemail Prioritization feature during this period.
  • Voicemail Tasks active users: The total number of unique active users who use voicemail task.
  • Team SMS thread summary active users: Total number of unique active users who use Team SMS thread summary.
  • Calls with call summary on: Total number of calls that have call summaries during this period.
  • Voicemail Prioritization generated: The total number of voicemails that have voicemail prioritization generated during this period.
  • Voicemail Tasks generated: Total number of voicemails that have tasks generated.
  • Team SMS thread summary generated: The total number of Team SMS thread summary generated.
  • Whiteboard active users: The total number of unique active users who take any action using the AI in Whiteboard during this period.
  • Whiteboard content generated: The total number of unique active users who take any action using the AI in Whiteboard during this period.
  • Whiteboard content refined: Total Whiteboard content refined with AI during this period.
  • Clip active users: The number of unique active users who took at least one action with AI in Clips in the specified timeframe.
  • Auto-generate Clip metadata: The total number of Clips content elements (such as titles, descriptions, tags and chapters) automatically generated using AI during this period.
  • Template avatars used: The number of avatars used in Clips that were selected from predefined templates during the specified timeframe.
  • Custom avatars used: Number of custom avatars used in Clips during the specified timeframe.
  • Custom avatars generated: The number of custom avatars created from scratch using AI in Clips during the specified timeframe.
  • ZoomMate chat active users: The total number of unique active users who submit at least one query through ZoomMate chat during the specified timeframe.
  • ZoomMate chat queries: The total number of queries that were initiated by users in ZoomMate chat during the specified timeframe.
  • ZoomMate chat threads: The total number of conversation threads that were initiated by users in ZoomMate chat during the specified timeframe.
  • Average web threads per user: The average number of conversation threads initiated per active user in ZoomMate chat during the specified timeframe.
  • Average web queries per user: Average number of queries initiated per active user in ZoomMate chat during the specified timeframe.
Custom AI

The following metrics may be available, depending on which Custom AI features are enabled on the account:

  • Active users: The total number of unique active users who use any Custom AI feature in the specified timeframe.
  • Assisted Actions: The number of unique licensed users who completed at least one action using Custom AI.
  • Queries using knowledge: The total number of user queries that were answered using custom knowledge collections created in AI Studio.
  • Queries using BYOI: The total number of user queries that were answered using third-party indexing services like Amazon Q or Glean.
  • Queries using 3rd-party app: Total number of user queries against third- party applications.
Agent

The following metrics may be available, depending on which Agent features are enabled on the account:

  • Active users: The total number of unique active users who submit at least one query through the agent during the specified timeframe.
  • Total queries: Total count of user-initiated queries submitted through the agent during the specified timeframe.
  • Total threads: The total count of user-initiated conversation threads started in the agent on the web during the specified timeframe.
  • Total custom agents: The total number of custom agents created by users within the agent during the specified timeframe.
  • Average queries per user: The average number of queries initiated per active user in the agent during the specified timeframe.
  • Average threads per user: The average number of conversation threads initiated per active user through the agent during the specified timeframe.
ROI

The ROI productivity metrics displayed in this dashboard are estimates calculated based on available account data and the current calculation settings. These calculations can use either the default values based on industry benchmarks or custom configured values. Actual results may vary significantly depending on your organization’s implementation. These projections are provided for informational purposes only and should not be considered guaranteed outcomes. Learn more

  • Total minutes saved: Represents the total estimated savings provided by Meeting Summary. This value is calculated by multiplying the number of meeting minutes by the host and participant savings factors.
  • Host minutes saved: Represents the total estimated savings for meeting hosts provided by Meeting Summary. This value is calculated by multiplying the number of meeting minutes by the host savings factor.
  • Particpant minutes saved: Represents the total estimated savings for meeting participants generated by Meeting Summary in meetings where the summary was shared with participants. The calculation multiplies the number of meeting minutes by the participant savings factor and by the number of participants, excluding the host.
  • Unrealized host minutes: Represents the potential savings that could have been generated by Zoom AI if the host had created a meeting summary. This value is calculated by multiplying the total meeting minutes by the host savings factor.
  • Unrealized participant minutes: Represents the potential savings that could have been generated by Zoom AI if the host had created and shared a meeting summary with participants. The value is calculated by multiplying the total meeting minutes by the number of participants (excluding the host) and the participant savings factor.
  • Average number of views per shared meeting summary: The average number of times a meeting summary was viewed.

Understanding the usage and engagement trends

The next section of the dashboard provides similar information, but in a graph format to show trends over time. Admins can:

  • Choose a time range to view metrics for that period. Note: This time range also affects the Top 10 users section below.
  • Click color-coordinated metrics to add or remove their data from the graph.
  • Hover over plot points to view exact details for that date.
  • Export as a CSV or JPEG file by clicking the download icon in the top-right corner of a usage chart.

Understanding and managing Zoom AI Credits

Category: Getting started and setting up

AI Credits included in plans

Different Zoom plans include varying amounts of AI credits, which may be allotted at the individual license/user level. Plans that include a monthly allotment will refresh every month at the subscription anniversary date. To learn more about plans that include AI Credits, please see the Zoom Pricing page or contact your account executive.

Credit pools and credit usage limits

All AI Credits are pooled at the account level, no matter the source (credits included in plans, prepaid commitments, or credit packs). The amount of credits a user can use is determined by their credit limit.

By default, a user’s credit limit will be the same as the standard credit allotment assigned to a license. For example, if an account purchases ten (10) Zoom AI Productivity Suite licenses with 1000 credits/per user per month, the monthly account-level credit pool will be 10,000 credits per month, with a default credit limit of 1000 credits/license per month for each assigned user.

User access to credits can be managed by settingcustom credit limits, which limit the amount of credits a user can use from the overall account pool.

Overallocation and underallocation of AI credits

When you set per-user credit limits, the total of all limits can be higher or lower than the account pool. Both states have implications for how your users experience AI features:

Overallocation happens when the sum of per-user limits exceeds the account pool. Users can be blocked even when credits remain within their individual limits because the shared pool runs out.

Underallocation happens when the sum of per-user limits is below the account pool. Credits in the pool may sit unused because no user is permitted to draw from them.

Credit expiration behavior

Monthly or annual subscription plans: For monthly credits allotted as a part of a monthly or annual subscription plan, unused credits will expire monthly at the subscription anniversary date and do not rollover.

Credit pack add-on (available online only): For credits purchased via a Credit pack add-on, credits will expire one (1) year from the date of purchase.

Prepaid commitment: For credits purchased as part of a monthly or annual prepaid commitment, credits will expire at the end of the billing cycle.

Purchase additional credits

If your account’s credit usage exceeds the amount included with licenses, admins can purchase more credits via Prepaid credit packs or purchase Prepaid credits as part of a monthly commitment. The available purchase methods depend on whether you purchased your plan online or purchased it via a direct sales quote. To purchase or learn more about credit packs, visit the Zoom pricing page.

In addition to purchasing additional credits, accounts can configure and allow overage usage and limits.

Zoom AI features and associated AI Credit costs

Each metered AI feature consumes credits based on the action performed. When the available credits reach zero, users receive an in-product message and may experience limited access to metered AI features.

The actual credit usage of a metered action can vary and will depend on a number of factors, which may include the prompt and requested action, complexity of the action, the artificial intelligence model(s) used, the amount of data processed, and the capability utilized. For example, when making a slide deck, the prompt “Make a 5-slide pitch deck from an outline” may use fewer credits than “Research, then make a 50-slide graphic storyboard based on my docs, meetings”.

Metered actions for AI Credits

The following table provides an example list of Zoom AI features that consume AI credits (metered actions).

Many AI features in Zoom Workplace, such as meeting summaries, note-taking, chat compose, phone summaries, whiteboard content generation, and more, are not currently metered and do not consume credits.

The table below is not exhaustive, and Zoom may add new credit-metered AI-powered capabilities and actions in its discretion.

[TABLE]

*Note: Workflow runs that utilize the Send email node for Microsoft Outlook and Gmail will not count as a metered action if the workflow does not contain AI nodes, advanced tool nodes, and other third-party nodes.

**Note: When using AI Create or AI Actions directly within the Zoom Canvas product interface, no AI credits are consumed. However, when using theZoomMate work surface on the web or desktop app to execute tasks that generate or modify Zoom Canvas content, AI credits will be consumed.

Ways to use AI credits efficiently

Below are examples of ways to use credits efficiently and minimize wasted credits:

  • Be specific in prompts: Clear, well-scoped prompts reduce back-and-forth reasoning and unnecessary tool calls, lowering credit usage.
  • Use lighter actions when possible: If you only need a quick summary, a simple prompt (lower credit usage) is better than triggering a full Deep Research task (higher credit usage).
  • Leverage Scheduled Tasks for routine lookups: Scheduled tasks that do simple checks (e.g., “summarize my meetings today”) generally use fewer credits.
  • Avoid unnecessary regeneration: Iterating on the same output (re-generating slides repeatedly) uses credits each time. It is recommended to refine your prompts upfront to optimize a specific task execution.

Manage AI Credits overage limits and behavior

If your account is eligible for a Pay-as-you-go rate, by default, the Set overage limit setting is disabled. This means users on the account will not be blocked from using metered AI features and your account will continue to accrue credit usage based on the Pay-as-you-go rate.

To manage overage limits for account usage of AI Credits:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin.
  2. In the top-right corner, click your profile picture or initials, then click Admin Center.
  3. In the side menu, click AI credits.
  4. Click the Usage tab.

  6. In the drop-down, select the number of credits for the overage limit.
  7. Click Set.

Once the overage credit limit has been met by the account, eligible users will be unable to utilize credits until additional credits have been provisioned/purchased. In addition to the banner, admins who have been configured for overage notifications will also receive an email notifying them that the overage limit has been reached.

To view the AI credits usage report for metered actions:

  • Date and time: Date and time of the action.
  • Name: The name of the user who consumed the credits.
  • Email: The email address of the user who consumed the credits.
  • UUID: The unique ID of the user who consumed the credits.
  • Action: The action performed that consumed the credits (e.g, Create slide deck, Run workflow, etc.)
  • Amount of Credits used: The amount of credits used for the action.
  1. (Optional) Click Export, to export the report into a CSV file.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do unused monthly credits roll over?

For monthly credits included in a monthly or annual subscription plan, unused credits will expire monthly at the subscription anniversary date and do not rollover.

AI credits included in your monthly or annual Zoom subscription plan are allocated on a monthly basis and do not roll over to subsequent months. Any unused credits will expire at the end of each monthly anniversary of your subscription start date.

Your AI credits reset on the monthly anniversary of your subscription start date. For example, if you purchase your plan on January 5, your credits will expire on the 5th of each month.

On February 5, any unused credits from January will have expired, and you’ll receive a fresh allocation of credits for February.

What happens if I disable overage limits?

For eligible accounts using Pay-as-you-go or prepaid commitment, when the credit pool is exhausted, and an overage limit has been disabled, additional credit usage will be billed at the applicable pay-as-you-go rate. If on a monthly plan, this rate will be utilized for the rest of the billing cycle until the next month’s credit refresh. If using prepaid credits, the pay-as-you-go rate will be utilized until more credits are purchased.

Can I track how my account is using credits?

Yes. Admins can view usage analytics for users, actions, or departments in the Zoom web portal.

What happens if I run out of credits?

Once you run out of credits, you will be unable to use metered AI-based features, unless you have pay-as-you-go overages configured and Set overage limit is greater than zero (0). For example, if using Zoom Sheets, Slides, or Paper, once you run out of credits, you will not be able to use AI Create or Edit actions to generate or analyze content and will only be able to manually create or edit content until overages are enabled, the credits refresh, or additional credits are purchased.

What order are credits consumed?

When a user runs an AI action, credits are consumed in the following order:

  1. Credits included in the user’s license.
  2. Prepaid commit credits or prepaid credit pack credits.
  3. Credits as part of a Pay-as-you-go plan or credits made available via overage.

Tips for drafting your prompt

Key components for creating effective AI prompts:

  • Be specific and provide context: Describe what you’re looking for in detail, including why you need it and how you’d like the response formatted or structure.
  • Give clear instructions for analysis: Tell AI how to approach the information: do you need a summary, specific data points extracted, or in-depth insights? The more precise your instructions, the better the output.
  • Include relevant background information: Providing up-to-date context on the subject helps AI return more accurate, relevant results.
  • Request a specific output format: Clearly describe the output you want AI to produce based on your input.

  • Available: Skills available to be installed and enabled in your ZoomMate instance.
  • Shared with me: Skills that have been shared with you by other users.
  • My shares: Skills that you have shared with other users.

In addition to managing Skills, you can also add new skills by going to the upper-right corner, clicking the Add icon , and selecting one of the following:

  • Create with ZoomMate: Create skills by chatting
  • Import from Github: Paste a repository link
  • Upload a skill: Upload .zip or .skill file
  • (Optional) In the upper-right corner, click the magnifying glass icon to search for skills.

ZoomMate web access

ZoomMate allows users to browse the web as a part of their ZoomMate session, either using an extension or a cloud browser. This extends ZoomMate’s capabilities to enable the ability to access and interact directly with web pages and perform actions using a browser at your direction. This allows ZoomMate to execute tasks directly on websites rather than only providing conversational assistance.

When the browser session is closed, any data that has been used or collected by ZoomMate for the user’s conversation/session, including screenshots, will be saved to the user’s Conversation history.

Using the Local browser access

The browser extension can access the page debugger backend, modify website data, and manage your tab groups.

The ZoomMate Browser Operator is a browser extension that can use your active sessions on your local browser. To use local browser access:

  1. LaunchZoomMate.
  2. In the chat box, click the plus + icon.
  3. Click Connectors, then click Local browser access toggle to enable or disable it. Once enabled, Chrome users will be redirected to the Chrome Web Store.
  4. Click Add to Chrome to add ZoomMate Browser Operator.
  5. Click Add extension.

The ZoomMate Browser Operator extension icon should appear in the Chrome extension toolbar.

Using the Cloud Browser Operator

ZoomMate Cloud Browser Operator lets ZoomMate perform the same actions as the local browser access (complete real web tasks including research, form-filling, data gathering, repetitive workflows, etc.), but within a sandbox environment for ZoomMate.

The cloud browser session may not persist. Due to this, you may need to start a new browser session even when opening a saved conversation.

Available third-party connectors for ZoomMate

ZoomMate can access your data from third-party services via Connectors.

Note:

  • Support as a data source requires a ZoomMate license.
  • Third-party data sources must be connected to use. Once connected, they remain available unless manually disconnected.

The following connectors are available for utilizing third-party applications with ZoomMate:

Application Connector Description
Salesforce Salesforce for Zoom Integrates Salesforce CRM with ZoomMate for sales automation.
Jira Jira for Zoom Connects Jira with ZoomMate for project management automation.
Slack Slack for Zoom Connects Slack with ZoomMate for messaging automation.
Google Calendar Google Calendar for Zoom Integrates Google Calendar with ZoomMate for smart scheduling.
Confluence Confluence for Zoom Connects Confluence with ZoomMate for documentation automation.
Workday Workday for Zoom Connects Workday HR with ZoomMate for HR automation.
Microsoft Outlook Outlook for Zoom Connects Outlook with ZoomMate for email and calendar automation.
Microsoft OneDrive OneDrive for Zoom Integrates OneDrive with ZoomMate for file retrieval.
ServiceNow ServiceNow for Zoom Enables ZoomMate workflows and agents to manage IT service management, incidents, and automate workflows through ServiceNow integration.

Responsibilities for using ZoomMate

You are responsible for your use of ZoomMate and the actions it takes on your behalf (including your obligation not to access non-public areas of websites and services without authorization or in a manner that violates the website/service’s terms) and for ensuring that your use of ZoomMate complies with Zoom’s Acceptable Use Guidelines, including those specific to AI. For example, and without limiting the foregoing, you may not use ZoomMate to make decisions with limited or no human input that have legal or similarly significant effects, including provision or denial of financial or lending services, housing, insurance, education enrollment or opportunity, criminal justice, employment opportunities, health care services or access to essential goods or services.

Managing the Risks

ZoomMate utilizes agentic AI capabilities that, together with Internet access, may have unique risks and may take unintended actions.

ZoomMate is designed to operate generally under your guidance and direction. Throughout your interactions, ZoomMate may:

  • Request your input when clarification is needed to complete tasks accurately
  • Ask for your confirmation before executing what ZoomMate thinks may be sensitive or significant actions
  • Provide you with opportunities to review and approve actions before they are finalized

You can pause ZoomMate’s operations at any time during the process.

When using ZoomMate, among other things, please remember to:

  • Use ZoomMate only with third-party websites, sources, and skills/tools you trust
  • Review sensitive actions before execution
  • Monitor all activity for suspicious behavior
  • Stop or pause ZoomMate actions when needed
  • Use caution if choosing to allow ZoomMate to take future actions without your review (for example, before selecting “always approve” or creating scheduled tasks)
